EC2 cold start: 47.6, 52.2, 58.7 seconds to the first job step (2026-08-18).
EC2 image 26.8GiB x64, 24.9GiB arm64.
EC2 renders the resource account-less, which the wildcard account matches.
EC2 user data is 16384 bytes and base64 is the wrong way to spend it. billet gzips the provisioning script (cloud-init decompresses it).
EC2 was asked directly under a throwaway role holding the generated document, three `run-instances --dry-run` calls: billet's own launch shape is `DryRunOperation`, the same request with the ledger snapshot in a mapping is an explicit deny naming `arn:aws:ec2:us-west-2::snapshot/snap-…`, and the PREVIOUS rendering allowed that same request — which is the exposure, measured rather than argued.
EC2's `CreateSnapshot` takes no `ClientToken` (`UnknownParameter`), so the token travels as the `sh.billet.snapshot-token` tag and idempotency is billet's: an attempt looks for a snapshot carrying its token before creating one and again after a failed call.
EVERY ANSWER OF THE PROTOCOL IS READ THROUGH `junioryono.billet.from_json_strict` (`plugins/filter/strict_json.py`, proved by `tests/strict_json_check.py`, run by the gate), never `from_json`, because `from_json` keeps the last of a repeated member and an answer ending `"pointer": true, "pointer": false` read as settled where the Go decoder refuses it; the parser's `id`, `token`, `reason`, `why`, the record's paths and `pointer_target` are required `is string` before their pattern, because a 32-digit number matched the coerced pattern, was stored as a number, and the rescue's `length` over it ended the cleanup diagnostic; and `record_error` is read by presence (present: a non-empty string; absent: the healthy members), with `pointer_problem` and `pointer_target` typed when present (round 5, 2026-09-10).
EVERY DISCARD UNMAPS FIRST, inside `discardCacheVolume`, because `trash mv` ignores watchers and a volume this host still maps answers every purge with EBUSY for good.
EVERY DOCUMENT IS DECODED TYPE-DIRECTED (`strictDecode` → `checkMembers`): encoding/json matches a member case-insensitively, so `"ROW"` beside `"row"` is two values for one field that `DisallowUnknownFields` admits; the walk carries the Go type per frame and refuses a member the struct does not spell exactly, a repeated one, and content after the document.
EVERY GUARD COMMAND CARRIES `expand_argument_vars: false`, because `ansible.builtin.command` expands environment variables inside `argv` by default (ansible-core 2.21), so a holder spelled `ci-${USER}`, which the command accepts as a name, was published as `ci-root` and the parser refused the answer's holder before the token was saved, stranding the guard (round 15; the order test requires the parameter of all ten commands, the gate's `b1c` publishes such a holder as spelled), and the collection's floor in `meta/runtime.yml` is therefore `>=2.16.0`, which the order test pins (round 16).
EVERY ID, TOKEN AND DIGEST PATTERN ENDS IN `\Z`, and the module uses `fullmatch`, because Python's `$` also matches before a final newline and a token with one passed the parser and was refused by the command at the settlement (round 6).
EVERY ONE OF THOSE QUESTIONS IS ASKED OF THE WHOLE ERROR, and the same way for each: `errors.Join` puts unrelated failures beside each other and billet's own opens join a startup failure with their close, so `Unreachable` requires EVERY INDEPENDENT BRANCH of the tree to establish an availability failure (each branch judged with the evidence of the nodes above it, because `ConnectError` and `net.OpError` both unwrap and a split that looked only underneath would discard the measured shapes) and `OnlyCause` requires every leaf to be the sentinel.
EVERY PURCHASE OF A LEASE ASKS IT, not only the pool path: `backAssignment` and the offer path gate on `mayBuy` too, because on GitHub.com the work arrives as direct assignments and a stream of small ones took every fragment of room a large tier was accumulating (#157).
EVERY host asserts both, never one host for all: a run_once task is skipped for every host when the first host's inherited `when` is false, and a consumer may invoke the role under a condition.
EVICTION TAKES THE SAME PROOF for every expired `cache-v` (#305): `Evict` removes generations under the cache lock, then calls `judgeVolumes`, the pass `ReclaimOrphans` runs after validating its options, with `Reclaim`, the eviction age floored at `OrphanMinimumAge`, `evictionVolumeLimit` (1,000) and the node's sessions, OUTSIDE the lock, because the proof costs about six rbd calls a volume and `rbd trash mv` needs no index consistency.
Each graph pass rebuilds its protected set from the original declarations; discovered aliases never become additional declared roles in the canonical-identity comparison.
Each offline answer carries the id GitHub holds for `billet-<lease id>` (`RunnerState.ID`); both must name the same id, an answer naming none (or another than an id the pool did journal) is no evidence, that id is the one withdrawn, and the cleanup's `RemoveRunner` is handed it (the cached member on a retried claim, `destroyCompleted` keeping a job's id for the same name) so a registration that took the name since is refused rather than deleted by name.
Each operation-admission pass reads all needed properties in one `systemctl show` invocation per unit: an unfiltered `--all` read for the retained node and an explicit `--property=` list for other units.
Each rule is a SAFE SUPERSET of what the family reads, derived from its steps, the Makefile targets they run and the Go closures they build, not from names: `cmd/`, `internal/` and `deploy/` select every family that builds or drives billet; non-test Go also selects `postgres` (its raw-SQL walk reads every Go file); the replay harness's own package set selects `replay`; `ansible_collections/` selects the host and command/retirement PostgreSQL families; Terraform, packaging and lint inputs select theirs.
Each target's `scaleset.New` builds one retryable client, and every listener, JIT mint, describe and runner lookup of that target multiplexes over its HTTP/2 connection to the broker.
Each tier is its own scale set with its own `maxCapacity`, and every tier advertises at once (`steadyAdvertisement`: committed work raised to `Allocator.AdvertisedCeiling`, which reads configuration only, so the number does not flicker with live headroom).
Each timer may trigger only its own service.
Enabling this witness without a PostgreSQL DSN fails rather than skips.
Enrollment is two fingerprints compared by a person.
Entry reads single raw property values: only exactly empty `Job=` proves no queued job, and whitespace-only or padded evidence is malformed rather than empty.
Entry state separates retirement completion from retained ordinary work.
Entry uses `observeRetireEntryNode`: active shares the full strict done observer; inactive/failed requires explicit zero MainPID and ControlPID, positively empty Job, no contradictory cgroup process evidence, persistent enablement through the shared retained-enablement predicate, and supported loaded/installed execution.
Escrow bought and not used is released after the message against `targetCapacity`/`messageCapacityTarget`, never beneath the advertisement, because the advertisement is no longer backed.
Even that fails if the delivering shell returns before the child calls `setsid()`, so the script waits for the launcher to announce its pid before writing the sentinel; removing that wait fails `realguest_test.go`.
Every JIT config GitHub mints carries `Ephemeral = True` and `DisableUpdate = True` (measured against the live API), which is why the runner-release deadline is billet's to watch (`billet-guest-images`).
Every JSON a role consumes has fixtures written by the Go test that produces it.
Every `.md` and `.txt` file is one paragraph per line.
Every `Open*` takes `...OpenOption`; `WithRunningRelease` names the binary, and an open that names nothing gets neither the check nor the record (which is what every test opening a throwaway ledger wants; `cmd/billet/ledger.go` passes it on all six helpers, asserted structurally).
Every `StartBuild` field is rendered in the console and CloudTrail, so the JIT config is a SecureString under `<jit_parameter_path>/<instance>` handed over as a `PARAMETER_STORE` environment variable named `ACTIONS_RUNNER_INPUT_JITCONFIG`.
Every `could not tell` and `move not confirmed`, and every generation failure, is joined into `Evict`'s error, the first ten by name and the rest counted (`evictionFailures`), because one unreadable cluster clock keeps every volume alike.
Every absolute path in every property is checked, including conditions, assertions, namespace access lists, working/root directories, environment files, credentials and command arguments.
Every admission and stopped/archive proof rereads the complete loaded node property inventory with unfiltered `systemctl show --all <unit>` (no `--property=`), plus one typed `busctl` `Properties.GetAll` read across its interfaces.
Every advertisement is authorised by GitHub with the job's header (numbered, so a later refusal ends an earlier grant), the mirror (per trust, owner and repository) is fetched to GitHub's refs with `--prune` under a node-wide cap of two fetches and a watchdog for the tier's ceiling and the disk's fill, and served under protocol v0 only: v2 serves any object present, and v0's check walks commits, so a fetch is served from the mirror only when every want is a commit or a current ref's object and its advertisement was served from the mirror; anything else, a partial clone's blob fetch included, goes to GitHub whole.
Every apt call in the rehearsal and lifecycle gates (`restore-rehearsal.sh`, `postgres-restore-rehearsal.sh`, `systemd-lifecycle.sh`, `test-package-lifecycle.sh`, `rehearsal-lib.sh`, `test-systemd-lifecycle.sh`) is now `timeout -v -k 10 300 apt-get -o Acquire::Retries=3 -o Acquire::http::Timeout=30` (the `https` method inherits the `http` timeout), and the two container entrypoint strings keep apt's stderr so `docker logs` carries the reason; the guest image and kernel builds are not gates and keep bare apt.
Every asset is checked against a digest the manifest names, which is worth nothing without the signature binding the manifest to the workflow that produced it.
Every background writer is patient with an error it cannot classify, which is right for a blip and wrong here: a replaced controller would go on polling GitHub and running the cleanup loop that calls `Runner.Destroy`, which touches no ledger.
Every billet lock unlocks with `LOCK_UN` before it closes, and `TestReleasingTheProbeLockReleasesItWhileADuplicateIsOpen` stands in for the child with `unix.Dup`.
Every cache is on by default where the tier can have it, and a default that cannot run is off, never refused.
Every cache is on by default where the tier can have it: the Docker store and sticky disks everywhere; the Git, Bazel and Go caches on a Linux-only Firecracker tier (`servesGuestCaches`); the Actions cache where its scope rules already hold (`actionsByDefault`); Go test results off, because caching them changes what `go test` runs.
Every call is bounded by platform (`timeout -k 10` on Linux, the task's `async` bound with no escalation on a Mac) and the calls that carry the token run under `no_log`; a later inclusion sends `--expect-id`; a second answer must carry the pointer the intent was declared from (`--recovery` exactly when the first answer carried one) and, with it, the target the first answer named, and the interruption facts are the first answer's alone, or a second answer that cleared the pointer would send the ordinary path over the recovery directory's material before the pointer refused its publication; check mode runs `prepare --dry-run` before any shape dispatch and then the read-only staging.
Every command runs with the launch agents' PATH (`billet_macos_node_path`, from `deploy/sh.billet.node.plist`), because a non-login SSH PATH has no Homebrew and would judge tart differently from the node.
Every completion path that cannot reach its holder corrects a verdict something else recorded (`SettleCompletionOnTerminalLease`) and never settles one.
Every container, instance, jail, VM directory and build carries the identity; `List`, `Find` and every destructive AWS statement filter on it, and a missing or unreadable tag is not ownership.
Every edge between a protected unit and a standard unit must still be on the edge list, and a standard unit that an operation would start must already be active.
Every enable, disable or mask in the role notifies `billet unit files changed` (`tests/unit_file_notify_check.py` refuses one that does not), and `main.yml` ends by flushing that handler, which reloads when the manager still reports the flag: the role's own operations justify it, and it adopts whatever else is pending without claiming the flag was its own.
Every existing lock file (global, init, inner, and the repair's) is opened through `regularfile.Open` with `NoFollow`, so a FIFO planted at a lock's name refuses instead of blocking inside the open before any deadline runs.
Every expected host must render exactly once and no other host may, or nothing is probed; a play that overrides connection variables at play level is outside the render, stated in the README.
Every failure to ask is could-not-tell, bounded by `cacheAuthorityLimit` (10s), and publishes nothing.
Every forward, inverse and installation relationship from or to the controller, backup and updater services, both retirement timers, retained node, required `billet-network.service`, configured `billet-dnsmasq@` instances and dedicated ledger mount is checked, including loaded aliases.
Every generation is still booted by `images pull --verify` before it can become `@verified`.
Every generator keeps individually fitting entries rather than summing sibling shapes; remote feasibility uses the first fitting charged shape, and local ceilings still reserve operating-system headroom.
Every guest runs under the jailer, chrooted, dropped to its own uid, in a cgroup, under seccomp, and the jailer names its chroot after the resolved `--exec-file`: the reference host installs `firecracker-v1.16.1` behind a stable symlink, so the jail is at `/srv/jailer/firecracker-v1.16.1/<id>/root`, and `List` enumerates every directory a jailer has built in rather than the path the config names, or every guest started before a version bump sits where the new process does not look.
Every hash is of a descriptor opened by a link path (`/proc/self/exe`, `/proc/<pid>/exe`; `os.Executable` returns a pathname, and a pathname opened after a replacement is the replacement) or by the file's path, and is BRACKETED BY THAT DESCRIPTOR'S OWN METADATA: a stat before and after the read that disagree in size or mtime are could-not-tell, a write after the second stat is outside the observation, and equal metadata is not proof the bytes never changed.
Every key it installs is proved readable by `ssh-keygen -l -f -` on the host first, because the module installs any material and `sshd -t` reads no authorized_keys file; present keys are installed before any absent key is removed, so a rotation never leaves a hardened host keyless between two tasks; and `unique(case_sensitive=true)` is what compares materials, because Jinja's `unique` folds case.
Every later write is conditional on the state it leaves and answers `ErrRetirementMoved` on zero rows (`AdvanceRetirementToIntent` by host, id and `reserved`; `CompleteRetirement` by host, survivor, id, reservation and `reserved|intent`, or a RECONSTRUCTION from the document on positive absence, since a ledger restored from before the reservation still belongs to a deployment that retired this host; `ReleaseRetirement` by host, run and `reserved`, the one delete).
Every lease write presents its epoch and a stale one is refused with `ErrFenced`, or a holder declared dead keeps writing to a lease somebody else owns.
Every microVM gets its own 32-byte bearer scoped to its five drive slots; EC2 carries it in user data and sends it back only over HTTPS; it is never a cache key, a log field or a deployment secret.
Every one of them contains gates whose whole purpose is to end a build, and every rule below is a way one of those gates computed the right answer and then let the build succeed.
Every option in `scripts/kernel/required-builtins.txt` must be `=y` and the config may contain no `=m` line, because a microVM has no initramfs; that file is also what the build enables, so the set list and the check list cannot diverge.
Every other claim a build makes is checked on a builder that has been apt-installed and never rebooted; the Docker gate read `overlayfs` off exactly that machine while the image reports `overlay2`.
Every other incapable or absent check-mode case reports the hold and succeeds without ordinary work, including a below-floor managed answerer beside a newer candidate source and an incapable legacy claim.
Every other process, a release before the request, one not yet reporting, one whose report is unreadable, malformed, another pid's or an earlier process's, takes the recorded SIGTERM path below UNCHANGED.
Every other writer meets the closed status and exits with status 6 (`exitRetiring`), which is what makes the backup's refusal recognisable to the transition that caused it — `openIdentityAccess` wraps `ErrRetiring` in an `*exitError` that KEEPS the cause, so `errors.As` still reaches it.
Every package whose tests write an executable does it through that package's `forkSafeWriteFile` (in `forksafe_test.go` or `forksafe_ext_test.go`), which holds `syscall.ForkLock` across the write; a bare `os.WriteFile` with an executable mode is the flake (#233).
Every protected role must resolve to a distinct canonical `Id`, and no role’s `Names` may include another protected role’s name; a collision refuses with `operation-role-collision` at every fresh or resumed admission before any operation.
Every reader goes through `AutomaticUpdates()`, because a reader of the field reads an absent block as off, which is the old default coming back one call site at a time.
Every recovery path is nevertheless written to be safe without it: idempotence is what makes the redelivery harmless, and `internal/e2e`'s `TestARedeliveredAssignmentDoesNotStartASecondRunner` pins that a redelivered exchange after a restart starts no second runner and releases no adopted lease.
Every release or image fetch wraps its transport error with `imagesource.WithoutSignedQuery`, which keeps scheme, host and path and drops query, fragment and userinfo.
Every release up to and including `v0.3.26` predates `terraform/` and carries no module; an equality check on the wire version shipped through v0.3.26 and refused every node in the field on a bump.
Every request goes through `exchange`, which adds a per-request context bound and reads the body whole up to `maxPolicyResponse`; a larger body is refused rather than truncated, because a prefix of it can be a valid document the whole is not.
Every reservation names a machine (`target_node` at escrow, `node` at bind) and capacity is charged on whichever is set, or a tier could escrow against the same host repeatedly before its first launch.
Every route and request section reports to the same cross-shard inventory union.
Every rule under the two headings below was a defect that passed a fake and died on a real call, so a backend is not finished until one real job has run on it.
Every scenario that is about the plane and the wire rather than about docker (lifecycle, wire, multiday, compute barrier, restart) runs through `forEachBackend`, once on docker and once on the simulated backend over one shared `simulated.Host` per leg, so a restarted stack (`sameBackend`) re-adopts what the previous process launched and a second deployment is on the same machine; the docker leg skips without a daemon and the simulated leg never does.
Every systemctl the inspector runs is bounded, and a stop or a start runs under the caller's deadline from the unit's own bound.
Every tier is `untrusted` unless promoted; a `trusted` tier requires a non-default runner group and an exact `workflows` allowlist, and the plane reads GitHub's `restricted_to_workflows` policy at startup and before every JIT mint, refusing drift.
Every token billet mints is scoped to an installation, so losing the installation looks like nothing.
Every toolcache vendor spells the architecture differently, and the record has three states.
Every transaction entry classifies the claim IMMEDIATELY AFTER THE LOCK: `startHostUpgradeHolding` before darwin's `checkBinaryDir` seam and the `resolveRelease` seam, `resumeHostUpgrade` before any journal, and `hostUpgradeFromRollout` takes the lock FIRST and holds one lock from classification through `settleOnTarget` (the `timerBarrier` seam observes it held at the instruction read and at settlement), exiting 0 with "guarded by H since T; nothing to do" on a guarded host and "nothing to decide" under a held lock; a guarded host's refusal is `guarded by H since T (HOSTNAME)`, carried by the node's `AckRefused` as the retryable refusal the coordinator records.
Every type that holds a credential redacts itself, on a value receiver, and the table proves it by mutation.
Every unresolvable state is an error that leaves the fence and journal standing, because `abandonLocked` reads nil as "ready to start" and a control plane repopulates an empty directory with a fresh ledger.
Every upholder and every unrelated path, socket, timer or automount trigger refuses, even when inactive.
Every version test injected `v1.2.3` while the release build injects `1.2.3`; `version.Compare` refused the bare form as "not a release", all four downgrade guards were could-not-tell on every release binary for nine releases, and a stale rollout downgraded a control plane (2026-09-05).
Every write is `If-None-Match: *`; the manifest is uploaded last so an interrupted upload is not something a listing offers; the local archive is written and verified first; the credential is env or IMDSv2.
Every write transaction begins IMMEDIATE, and that is not tuning.
Every writer of the identity directory takes the exclusion before its first access, and borrows it downward.
Everything a holder opens under the root opens relative to `txLock.dir`, and the guard directory a mutator acts on is opened, validated (0700, owned) and classified through one descriptor (`openGuardForMutation`) before its record is believed; the record and a candidate are opened identity first (`regularfile.OpenAt`) and THE RECORD IS JUDGED ON ITS OWN DESCRIPTOR (`requireTrustedFile`: regular, owned, writable by nobody else), because a record hard-linked from a file another account owns is one that account can rewrite whatever the directory's mode says; a stale `guard.json.tmp` is examined through an identity descriptor (regular, owned, one link) and then REMOVED by name relative to the directory and re-created exclusively, never opened for writing and never truncated; a symlink claim whose target cannot be examined for any reason but ENOENT is could-not-tell, never dangling; a record that cannot be read names no holder, so `holder`, `release`, `recover --holder` and a takeover refuse over it; and the timer's `--from-rollout` exits 0 only over a recognised guard (`errHostGuarded`), a claim that could not be classified being the failure it is.
Everything a queue host has to be is asked ONCE, of the whole host, before it is classified (`isHostname`, on the RAW host because `strings.ToLower` folds U+0130 to an ASCII `i`; plus a port of 443 or none, compared numerically because `:0443` is a reachable 443): the label rule lived in the VPC-endpoint branch and `awsRegionRe` has no length cap, so a 64-character region built an over-long label in the STANDARD host, which never went near that branch.
Everything billet does differently is one reviewed file, `differences.tsv`: a `skip`, or a `prepare:<name>` the runner performs just before a step, each with its reason; an entry naming a step the plan no longer has stops the build before anything runs.
Everything here exists because a quiet mistake with one of those credentials is expensive and invisible.
Everything in `internal/scaleset` is translation (vendor types in, billet types out); `provision.go` reconciles one scale set per tier before any listener starts, `quiet.go` and `runner_lookup.go` find and remove runners.
Everything that talks to GitHub by name (the server's `EnsureScaleSet` and record, the provenance report, the plane's describe and mint, `teardown`) goes through `Tier.ScaleSetName()`; the node still sends the label on the wire and the plane translates, so no wire version was needed.
Eviction removes an expired generation with `rbd rm`, because it sees only its own host's mappings, so rbd's refusal to remove an image still open (EBUSY) is what protects another node's job, and `rbd trash mv` makes no such refusal; an expired writable volume it moves to the trash instead, after the lock, on `ReclaimOrphans`' proof (below, #305); a failure on one image of either kind is reported and the pass goes on; and it never deletes from the trash under the cache lock, so a chain is reclaimed over eviction passes as the purge removes the writers between its links.
Eviction, Snapshot, retirement and Discard likewise act only on the exact names billet gives (`cacheImageName`, `isCacheVolume`), never on a prefix: `cache-v-<second>-by-hand` or `cache-v-ns/cache-g-…` is not billet's.
Evidence is local to the call, discarded once before the comparison reread and at return; no cache crosses a retirement step.
Exactly one party renews a lease, and every defect here was a moment when that count was zero.
Except for ancestor mounts and default slices, listed ordering edges and inverse edges that the operation does not propagate need no activity proof: stopping the controller with `Conflicts=shutdown.target` cannot start shutdown.
Exclusions are anchored with `(^|/)`, and that was measured. golangci-lint's cache is keyed on file content and shared across checkouts; a `^cmd/billet/` anchor stopped matching in a second checkout and 612 previously excluded findings came back as failures against a tree with nothing wrong.
Execute a gate against both a passing and a failing fixture.
Existing C3 guard cases retain the external-ledger refusal witnesses.
Existing binary, server policy, survivor and preparation refusals retain their order.
Existing marker and complete-drop-in paths revalidate their bytes and re-discharge directory and ancestor flushes before proceeding.
Existing private trees are scanned for either loaded `PrivateTmp` value; `no` cannot prove that a running invocation has no trees to remove.
Exit codes: 0 nothing to do, 2 rebuild due, 3 GitHub already refusing; failing to reach GitHub is an error, not one of the three.
Export, continuation, repeated assignment, CR, unsupported controls and Unicode noncharacters refuse; no shell expansion runs.
Exported entry points enforce their own rule (the `alloc.New` argument).
Extra aliases of a single role remain accepted.
Fake boundary witnesses introduce drift after successful operation admission; a later final-done refusal does not prove these boundaries.
File, append, truncate, terminal, socket and named-descriptor modes refuse, including for `ExecStop` and `ExecStopPost`.
Filesystem assertions read the namespace's lstat snapshot, and `expect_no_ordinary` watches the account, rendering and service tasks independently of recovery.
Filesystem metadata is nonrecursive; extraction is `recursive-write`; services are exactly the node's enable/stop/start superset and only the node supplies proposed unit bytes.
Firecracker reserves five hot-attach slots per guest (`provider.MaxVolumes`); EC2 attaches owned volumes to the one-job instance at runtime.
Firing twenty destroys at once starts twenty clocks against a queue served in turn, so fan-out is bounded against the server's concurrency, not the client's patience.
First converge the endpoint ordinarily with `billet_server_retire: false`, then collect only after receipt, runtime registration and installed configuration agree on the survivor.
First real long poll: about 88 seconds against a 90-second lease TTL.
Five instances in one day: `printAdmission` rendered a seal and nothing proved `billet status` called it; a fake converger carried its own copy of `StopAndProve`'s refusal so deleting the production one left the test green; `TidyStagedRegistration` had only test callers while its doc comment named a production one.
Fixed in v0.9.2: the tag spelling everywhere, both spellings ordered, and the starter finishes a rollout behind the control plane as superseded.
Folding an error into "not found" is the could-not-tell collapse this repository keeps removing.
For the reference deployment's gateway class its users REPORT a cap of 8192 sessions on older firmware and 32767 on newer, with new connections dropped near it; the deployment's own session count was not read (2026-09-11, `docs/reference/records/shared-uplink.md`), so the cap is a reported number and the saturation a hypothesis consistent with the symptoms, not a measurement.
Force refuses unless an operator sealed admission, fixes its target set when the request is taken (a standing flag would be a timer wearing different clothes), and archives forced leases as `failed`.
Format: `<name>-<monthday>-<description>`
Four mechanisms in one piece of work each reported success: a suppressed `apt-get update` made a probe report "0 lines" from a file it never fetched; an `ldd` jail copied the very library it tested for; a fake chroot prefixed only `argv[1]`; and this Mac's `grep` is ugrep, which reads UTF-16 transparently where GNU grep cannot, so a broken decoder looked correct.
Four rounds of modelling what starting one unit does to the other were wrong every time, because the closure is systemd's to compute through units billet has never heard of.
Four rounds on the deployment lock: a gid comparison proved `20 == 20` because a temp dir is owned by the primary group; setgid was set before the file existed so the kernel supplied the gid; an `O_NOFOLLOW` test proved `os.Root` refuses an escape rather than a symlink; a "second process is refused" test ran both opens in one process, which a package mutex satisfies.
Four things hold above the `backend` interface whichever engine is under it: one authoritative process; one writer within the process (a single-connection writer pool); durability verified rather than assumed (`Open` reads the pragmas back and fails closed if `journal_mode` is not WAL, which is what catches a network filesystem); and contention retried rather than returned.
Fresh requests and incomplete or unsettled continuation end after transition/tail even when their result settles.
Fresh retained request callers have independent rendering oracles.
Frozen done publication, status republication, marker clearing and settlement keep their strict proofs and registration re-proofs.
Full closed-edge admission also precedes request lock and ledger preparation, `EnsureRetiredDir`, the staged configuration and intent publication, using protection derived from the installed request configuration before a journal exists and from the recorded journal on resume.
Full confirmation-controller selection remains #14; a retained migration refuses inventory_hostname as its confirmation controller while unchanged quiet startup needs no selection.
Full effect admission precedes timer-stop metadata, stopped status, every phase journal write, archive rename and directory flush steps, and the configuration rewrite.

It also enables a controller along the path (`+memory` in every ancestor's `cgroup.subtree_control`) only for the controllers its keys name (`write_values` in v1.16.1's `cgroup.rs`), so with `cpu.weight=100` alone a job's cgroup has no memory or io accounting.
It also renders and enables the backup timer in `tasks/backup.yml` on every host whose server may run (`billet_server_should_run`, never the bare flag: a prepared host is not archived), under `billet_backup_timer` (default true), and removes it elsewhere; the rendered unit carries the same ledger fence as the server unit (`RequiresMountsFor=` always, plus `Requires=`/`After=` on the exact mount unit when a volume is configured) and a drop-in on it is refused by asking systemd for `DropInPaths` after the reload.

It decides by signature, not by name: a callee with one of `database/sql`'s statement-executing names and a matching signature (`(context.Context, string, ...any)` returning `(sql.Result, error)`, `(*sql.Rows, error)`, `*sql.Row` or `(*sql.Stmt, error)`, plus the four non-context forms).
It deliberately does not guess at package-level state, anything declared inside a `for`/`range` (Go 1.22 gives each iteration its own copy, so the table-driven pattern shares nothing), writes through a pointer, reads, a merely-declared function literal, a closure reached non-lexically, or which parameter a parallel helper makes parallel (zero such helpers exist, measured).

It does not upgrade the controller (a process cannot install its own successor, and this one is unprivileged; the root timer below does that); it observes the running binary is the target and only then begins on the nodes, which is what makes a rollout server-first.
It drives active, quiet inactive/failed, activating/deactivating/reloading, a queued start and pending reload; the command fixture still supplies retirement, source/effect and registration evidence.
It exists because `billet-backup.timer` is not enabled by the package (each archive holds a copy of the App key) and a host converged from a tarball ran no postinstall; the timers are deliberately not in the plan `up`/`down` prove and unwind, which owns the two services that hold compute and a ledger, and `down` leaves them running, since a backup of a stopped deployment is the useful kind. systemd only, by `ManagerName()`; launchd's `StartTimer` refuses, and the Mac's schedules are `enableScheduledAgents`.

Measured (2026-09): Route C's Access SSH proxy never engaged on a real hybrid deployment while this route worked first time; Gateway stores a `/32` as the bare address, so a rule written with `/32`s never converges; `precedence` is required because it is one account-wide sequence.
Measured 2026-08-28: provisioning 3m54s, snapshot to available 11m06s, console report 4m40s after the verifier launched.
Measured 2026-08-31: `BatchGetBuilds` reports the parameter's name as the value, the staged value appears nowhere, and a service role holding only `ssm:GetParameters` resolves it.
Measured 2026-09-04 on eight runs: the abandoned session was still refused at 60 seconds every time and open at 91 on three of them and 92 on the other five (a bracket, not an expiry), and the successor was then handed the id the abandoned session had been holding, carrying the same one assigned job (the run that compared identities rather than counts found the same run id and the same stable workflow-job id).
Measured 2026-09-04: the acceptance lane's App was given `actions: write` so the lane could dispatch a workflow, and every rehearsal's `local up` refused `actions: granted write, but billet never requested it`.
Measured 2026-09-09 on both platforms: `O_NOFOLLOW` on a symlink to a file or a directory is ELOOP, `O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY` on a symlink to a directory is ENOTDIR, parent-component symlinks are followed (which is why every component is opened relative to a descriptor), a FIFO opened `O_WRONLY|O_NONBLOCK` with no reader is ENXIO, dup'd and inherited descriptors share a flock and `LOCK_UN` on any releases all.
Measured 2026-09-11: every `archive.ubuntu.com` IPv4 address refused port 80 for hours from two unrelated networks (the reference deployment's site and AWS), two answered nothing on 443 either, and a job's apt stalled 30 s per attempt on one of those (`docs/reference/records/shared-uplink.md`).
Measured 2026-09-14, run 34848474843 on 46fcafa started retirement at 13:56:15Z and failed at 14:32:15Z on R2's policy diagnostic after every route case passed, leaving the request suite unexercised within the 45-minute budget.
Measured 2026-09-25: a node the control plane had forgotten re-registered, destroyed eleven finished jobs' VMs as orphans, kept all eleven in `running`, and its drain ninety minutes later waited six and a half hours on compute that was gone.
Measured 2026-09-25: every `rbd rm` of a finished job's clone failed for an hour (`exit status 16`, image still open, or no answer).
Measured 2026-09-25: slots launched a minute before a host upgrade's drain sat idle for sixteen minutes with jobs queued for their tier.
Measured against real S3 in us-east-1 on 2026-09-04, both HTTP 404: a missing key in a bucket that exists is `<Code>NoSuchKey</Code>`, and any key in a bucket that does not exist is `<Code>NoSuchBucket</Code>` — a bucket is resolved before a request is authorized, so the second needs no identity at all.
Measured at zero violations before it went in, which is the bar for any rule in CI.
Measured in a real guest: `nohup`, a double fork and `systemd-run --user` all leave the runner dead three seconds later while `tart exec` exits 0.
Measured on macOS 26 (2026-09-30, a CGO_ENABLED=0 Go 1.26 probe): a Go process that has not asked for SIGUSR1 survives it and exits 0 later, because the runtime installs its own handler and drops an unwanted `_SigNotify` signal, so an older node sent the request by mistake does not die, it just never drains and the stop waits forever; that, and a process in the instant before its runtime starts, where the default action does kill, is why the gate exists.
Measured still refusing a changed relaunch of the same lease long after the fact, so `clientTokenFor` is a safety property: an ambiguous retry cannot start two machines.
Measured systemd facts, each of which reads the other way somewhere.
Measured the same day with GNU tar as root on ubuntu-24.04: plain `-xzf` gives `1001:1001`, `--no-same-owner` gives `0:0`.
Measured under dash in `ubuntu:24.04`: in `mkdir …; curl …; sha256sum -c -; tar -xzf …` a failing checksum prints `FAILED`, execution continues into `tar`, and the compound exits 0.
Measured with `iam:SimulateCustomPolicy` (2026-09-04): a role scoped to one deployment is allowed on its own builder, implicitly denied on another's, and implicitly denied on an ordinary job instance of its own; the same holds at create time against `aws:RequestTag`, which AWS authorizes separately, so both moved together.
Measured with the bundled driver (2026-09-09): a read-only open of a cleanly stopped WAL ledger CREATES `billet.db-wal` and `billet.db-shm` owned by the opener and leaves them, a crashed ledger's WAL-resident row is visible, and a live controller's later commits are visible to a later `View`; that is why `billet rollout status` runs as the identity directory's owner and as nobody else: root re-executes itself as the owner, the owner runs in place, and on a SQLite ledger any other account (an operator with group access, say) is refused before the open, since its sidecars would be that account's exactly as root's would.
Measured: a 700ms stall against a 300ms TTL reproduced a CI failure exactly.
Measured: a dot-directory at the top of `TART_HOME` is invisible to `tart create`/`list`/`get`, `tart prune` targets only `caches` or `vms`, and `tart rename` already refuses an occupied target.
Measured: a second flock on a separate descriptor in the same process is denied (EWOULDBLOCK on darwin), so a holder must not call anything that takes it again.
Migration 48 adds the `release_watermark` singleton and `nodes.highest_release`.
Migration 48's `release_watermark` singleton; `state.WithRunningRelease` on every open in `cmd/billet/ledger.go` (asserted structurally by `ledgerrelease_test.go`); `enforceReleaseWatermark` after the schema is settled.
Migration 50 adds `rollout_nodes.last_refusal`, with three behaviours and no fourth: the coordinator's failed-dispatch path writes the error's text (`AdvanceRequest.Refusal`, bounded to 4096 bytes at a rune boundary with ` [cut]` and made valid UTF-8, since PostgreSQL's `text` refuses invalid bytes), the accepted-dispatch path clears it (`ClearRefusal`, and only after the dispatch was accepted, so a reader during the dispatch still sees the old refusal), the convergence walk's commit clears it too (the accepted dispatch's clear is a write that can fail after the updater is already running, and a host an operator moved by hand after a refused dispatch is stuck on nothing: the record means the refusal the host is still stuck on, never a history), and every other advance leaves it as it is, because an empty parameter cannot stand for "keep what is there" when clearing is a write of exactly that empty value (`SetLastRefusal` is the statement's own guard; both flags together are refused).
Migration 50 carries dated listener observations with exact discovery and pending lease IDs, the last sent advertisement and the last completed exchange.
Migration 51's `controller_retirement` (primary key the deployment; `retiring` and `survivor` are INVENTORY names; `run` the reserving holder; `state` in `reserved`, `intent`, `done`; `transition_id` minted at the reservation and immutable; `reserved_at`, `updated_at`, `completed_by`, `completed_at`) is written by `state.ReserveRetirement` BEFORE a request collects any evidence, read-then-write inside one `DB.Tx` so the single writer decides between two requests: no row inserts, this host's `reserved` row is adopted (the run re-bound, the id and the reservation time kept), a `done` row refuses `ErrRetirementDone` for the life of the deployment (a deployment that retired one controller has no survivor for a second), anything else `ErrRetirementReserved` with the row so the caller's sentence names the holder.
Migrations 1 to 42 keep the tab indentation they inherited from Go raw strings; it looks wrong and it is correct.
Migrations 53 to 55 carry #226's cache evidence and outcomes.
Migrations are files in `internal/state/migrations` (SQLite) and `internal/state/pgmigrations` (PostgreSQL), 57 of each, discovered by `go:embed`.
Migrations are published bytes.
Minting a registration and then being refused leaves it on GitHub with nothing to consume it, one orphan per pull request.
Mirror sync in progress?` after ten.
Mirrors unused seven days are reaped, and a mirror in use is passed over.
Mismatched `adopted` answers do not trigger cleanup: the caller has not confirmed the observed binding.
Missing owned files can be repaired; altered sources refuse.
Missing stopped registration does not require an active node.
Mixing is safe for a node that has the handler: its first SIGTERM after any number of requests is still its first level.
Modules pin to release tags, and every layer names the same version.
Moving `billet.db` first and crashing left no ledger at the source, so a re-plan read an ordinary install and put the archive's database beside a `-wal` from a different one, which SQLite replays.
Moving both operands to another file with identical bytes still refuses with `retained-config-path-changed`.
NEVER ON `main`: a `main` run is the check on what merged, and cancelling it for the next merge left `main` with no completed run across nine merges on 2026-09-25.
NO LEDGER IS OPENED TO GET THERE and no identity exclusion is taken: the row reached `intent` before the archive did, so nothing must be asked of a database before `done`, and a host past the archive is exactly the one whose database may be out of reach — which the tail already answers as a pending row rather than a failed converge, so requiring a ledger read to resume would make an outage the one thing that leaves a half-transitioned host with no way forward.
NOTIFY_SOCKET is NOT the tell, because a node's detached updater inherits its unit's socket and so would the candidate.
Named pipes cannot replace this socket: a FIFO with no writer reads EOF immediately, and holding a writer open hides an updater's death.
Neither uses the AWS SDK: `awssig` signs SigV4, `awsjson` speaks JSON 1.1, `awscreds` resolves env or IMDSv2 credentials, `awspolicy` generates least-privilege IAM from action constants each package declares, `awsquota` reads Service Quotas, `awsssm` reads and writes Parameter Store, `awssts` answers which account a credential is in.
Never `SELECT *` (`-- wildcard-ok: <reason>` is the escape; `TestNoQueryUsesAWildcardProjection`).
Never await backup under that exclusion, restore an archive, restart a collaterally stopped node, or manufacture missing historical evidence.
Never guess a byte size.
Never let a fallback down `PATH` reach a real binary.
Never quote the guest.
Never recreate a rolling guest release: its tag and assets freeze on first publication, and the publisher creates the dated tag before `gh release create --verify-tag` so a conflicting tag fails rather than relabelling the build.
Never rely on `~/.codex/config.toml` defaults; they vary per machine.
Never signal a pid you have not proved is still yours.
No Contents either way (billet cannot read your code), the webhook inactive (`hook_attributes`; a test asserts the field is present and false, not merely absent).
No `GuestContract` bump: every piece is additive, and an older image simply builds cold.
No `git rebase`, no `git push --force`/`--force-with-lease`, no history rewriting.
No cache bearer is written where a job can read it after the fact.
No implementation-time execution establishes their mutation results; CI must do that.
No include variable aliases desired configuration.
No service-account import or fleet collection precedes cancellation.
No shard preserves the existing ONLY/SKIP behavior, including all request sections together.
No shipped unit declares installation `Also=`, so every nonempty assignment refuses, even before a later empty assignment.
No timing or mutation outcome follows from source review.
Node names default to the hostname, so two billets on one machine share one; labelling by name let one installation enumerate the other's containers.
Node presence is the unit's, never a configuration's: an absent installed configuration is `config: absent` and the unit is still observed; two configurations without a node section are observation-only (`record: unread`, the record reader never called); a missing, empty or malformed `MainPID` is could-not-tell.
Node upgrades therefore launch through `systemd-run` in a transient root oneshot of their own; opening more writable paths in the node unit would leave the lifetime defect.
Nodes carry `highest_release`, reported by `billet status` as `DOWNGRADED` and never refused, because the coordinator's rollback inference IS an older re-registration.
None reaches another machine, so `--old-controller-fenced` is the operator asserting the old controller is stopped and disabled everywhere; without it two controllers share one identity, one CA and one App credential.
Normal completion and publication still call the strict retained-node predicate.
Normalise a value something else will use; refuse an identity.
Not at the top, or a config the packaged units cannot use is reported as a failure to create a lock directory; `--dry-run` never needs it. macOS has no `/var/lock` and no `/usr/local/var`, so `up` refuses with the `sudo mkdir -p` to run rather than creating root-owned directories.
Not modelled against a real cluster: whether an interrupted `rbd rm` leaves a directory entry or a hidden `REMOVING` trash entry; `rbd rm` by name finishes either.
Nothing compares a checksum across timelines.
Nothing else renders a plist, so a difference there is an operator's edit or a stale billet, and both want a person.
Nothing is deleted unless it is known not to be a key: `inspectKey` answers present, absent or unverifiable, and only absent permits a deletion; the staging name is re-inspected after `O_EXCL` fails; "not a valid key" is not "safe to clobber".
Nothing is lost in the window: GitHub queues a job for 24 hours.
Nothing is lost while it waits: GitHub queues a job for 24 hours with no runner available.
Nothing is released or destroyed on that proof, because a stopped guest is also what a job that finished normally looks like while its Destroy is on the way: the entry stays for that Destroy, and what a drained process leaves behind is the next process's Recover to destroy.
Nothing is reserved for an idle tier, and there is no rotation (#140). v0.10.0 escrowed one slot per tier to advertise and wasted the catalogue's capacity (#116); v0.11.0 rotated one shared discovery turn across tiers, which on GitHub.com left each idle tier assignable for about one poll in eighteen minutes, and a job queued against an idle tier went unassigned for hours.
Nothing prevents a trusted job leaking into its own cache: do not cache secrets.
Nothing runs without a lease: the invariant is enforced at the purchase, never at the advertisement.
Nothing the guest wrote is ever quoted into a billet error.
Nothing unlinks a pathname it cannot prove it owns: the staging name is `os.CreateTemp`'s and the planner refuses an App-key path that is one of billet's own state files.
Nothing weakens the contract for being a stand-in: `List` and `Find` error on a done context and under `FailInventory(err)`, the harness's seam for a host whose inventory cannot be read, and never answer short; `Destroy` proves (`TeardownStopped`) only for an instance the store held and removed, answers stopped for an id it never held because the store is authoritative, and refuses another deployment's id; untrusted and unknown work are refused because there is no boundary at all; a name in use on the host is refused; the registration is retained nowhere and no rendering of the provider, host or instance contains it.
Now there is one way through: `ca.crt` and `ca.key` read, parse, match and name this deployment; everything else refuses.
ONE CLASSIFIER JUDGES EVERY ERROR the tail's ledger work produces (`retireLedgerProblem`, over the open, the binding and the row's completion alike, because an outage that begins after the connection is established is the same outage), and THE PENDING LIST IS CLOSED: `state.Unreachable`, `ErrSchemaAhead`, `ErrSchemaBehind`, `ErrReleaseBehind`, a DSN variable the locator names that is unset or whose environment file cannot be read, and a DEADLINE — while a ledger bound to another deployment, or a row naming another host, transition or reservation, says the ledger disagrees with this journal and stops for an operator.
ONE CONFIGURATION BINDS THE REPORT, AND IT IS ONE OBSERVATION: the file is read once through one descriptor, bracketed, those bytes are parsed and their digest is `installed_config.sha256`, that descriptor's identity is what every process's view is compared with, a service whose view is that file publishes the observation's digest rather than a second open of the pathname, and at the end of the report the descriptor is re-checked by its own metadata and the name by identity and metadata (`config.same_as_installed`: a rewrite in place STILL PRESENT at the closing checks withdraws a true binding, the observation's digest and every service field copied from it; a replacement by rename STILL PRESENT at the closing name check makes the binding false; a replacement or rewrite undone before those checks is outside what they observe, and a write after them likewise); `config.presence` is the typed answer `present`, `absent`, `malformed` or `unreadable`, so a consumer never reads a failed read as absence (an ENOENT through a dangling symlink is absence of the resolved configuration, not of the directory entry); each unit's `unit_file_state` is systemd's literal answer and `enabled` is derived from it, true for `enabled` and `enabled-runtime`, false for every other state systemd defines and unknown outside that set; false means a recognised state other than those two and NOT "positively disabled" (`static`, `alias`, `indirect` and `generated` units can still be started by something else), so a consumer that needs a particular state reads the literal against its own accepted set, and one is never handed an empty answer as either; a service that names another configuration than the inspector's publishes the digest and mtime verdict of ITS OWN VIEW of that path, read through its root in the sample, never the inspector's file at that name, while a service naming the inspector's path has its view opened for identity alone; ONLY THE SUPPORTED COMMAND LINE IS FOLLOWED INTO THE FILESYSTEM, the one predicate the sample and the report share, and `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` is decoded losslessly (one terminator off, every empty argument kept, because trimming every trailing NUL turns a five-argument command line into the supported four), so an unsupported process's fourth argument is never opened, whatever it names; the view is an `O_PATH` descriptor on Linux (no read, no wait on a FIFO, no device open), reopened for reading on the same inode through `/proc/self/fd` only for a regular file (by duplication off Linux, where only the fixtures run a view), so a special file at the inspector's path makes the binding false with the content evidence unknown, and one at another path is could-not-tell; EVERY PATHNAME THE COMMAND READS DIRECTLY goes through `regularfile.Open` (`internal/regularfile`, the one identity-first open: `O_PATH`, fstat, fstatfs refusing an enumerated kernel pseudo-filesystem (configfs included, whose attributes dispatch reads to a subsystem), and a NON-BLOCKING reopen through `/proc/self/fd` on Linux, so a device is never opened, `/proc/kmsg` is never read and a write lease answers EWOULDBLOCK (its holder is still signalled and the lease marked for downgrade: the wait is avoided, not the break); a non-blocking open and fstat elsewhere, where a device is opened and then refused and the package says so; a reopen that fails is `ErrReopen` with the cause quoted, never `fs.ErrNotExist`, so a missing `/proc/self/fd` cannot read as an unheld lock or a missing record; `ReadFile` refuses a file over its limit rather than cutting it), for its configuration, the transaction lock with `NoFollow`, an environment file systemd names, `guard.json`, the recorded release executable, darwin's managed binary and every `readPublicFile` read, each whole-file read and every hash bounded by its purpose and refused rather than cut past the bound, and the readers it delegates to (`provenance.Read`, `state.PeekDeploymentID`, `hostupgrade.ReadJournal`, `wirecert.SnapshotAuthority`) read through the same package with their own size limits, because a plain open of a FIFO blocks before any stat and nothing else in the report bounds it, so a special file at any of them is could-not-tell with the reason, never a wait; the source scan holds the direct `os` calls of `releaseinspect.go` and its platform files to a listed set and says that syscalls and the delegated readers are outside it, which the FIFO cases prove behaviourally; identity, authority and the DSN come from the inspector's `--config`, made absolute, and `config_binding` is true only when every present unit's LOADED `ExecStart`, read as structured records from the bus property (`busctl --json=short get-property … org.freedesktop.systemd1.Service ExecStart`, `a(sasbttttuii)`, where argument boundaries survive; `systemctl show` joins argv with spaces and `systemctl cat` shows text the manager may not have loaded) is one record whose argv is exactly `<managed path> <role> --config <that absolute path>`, and every running process's own four-argument command line names that absolute path AND the file its own root resolves that path to is the inspector's file by identity (a bind mount removed from the unit and reloaded without a restart leaves the process in the namespace it started in, where the same path is another file, and the root's name reads `/` in both); false beats unknown beats true; a unit whose fragment is gone binds trivially only when positively inactive with no main process.
Observations and dispatches are two passes with a ledger re-read between, or the failure budget depended on what hosts were called.
Off systemd the updater remains a `setsid` child, reaped by a background `Wait` (`Process.Release` does not reparent).
Old retained journals without this evidence cannot establish the new guarantee and refuse.
On 2026-09-04 a session holding one `JobAssigned` message was abandoned without being closed, and the successor was handed the same message id back on all eight runs.
On 2026-09-25 a TLS timeout on that hop put both into a rollout refusal that `billet rollout status` printed and the journal kept (#253).
On Ceph, a discard moves to the trash and the node's sweep deletes (#280, #292).
On Darwin Go does not poll FIFOs (kqueue, Go issue 24164), so `SetReadDeadline` refuses with "file type does not support deadline"; reported by the probes for #98 on 2026-09-06.
On PostgreSQL the DSN variable is compared with the unit's one environment file INSIDE the process, the whole file validated first as bytes (valid UTF-8, LF only, no control character but LF and TAB, because systemd reads a carriage return as a newline and one inside a comment would hide an assignment, and no Unicode noncharacter, which systemd's stricter UTF-8 rule refuses and Go's `utf8.Valid` accepts) and then against the restricted `NAME=value` grammar the role's template writes (a name assigned twice, whitespace systemd would trim, a quote or backslash or hash in an unquoted value, an `export` are unsupported syntax and could-not-tell), and only `equal`, `differs`, `not_in_file` or `absent` leaves it.
On PostgreSQL the exclusion is a session advisory lock, so a controller is dead when its session is, decided by the database; there is no lease, renewal, timeout or failure detector.
On PostgreSQL the writer pool's `lock_timeout` is 50ms so contention comes back to `beginWrite`'s loop, and that loop covers the BEGIN and the advisory lock only; the migration transaction is the one write that waits for its locks instead (`SET LOCAL lock_timeout = 0` in `beginMigration`), bounded by the 30s startup budget wherever it runs, promotion included, because DDL takes locks the advisory lock does not cover and a 50ms cap failed the open under CI's parallel schema builds (#75).
On Ubuntu 24.04 unattended-upgrades runs `needrestart -m u` after every upgrade and `needrestart.conf` ships `$nrconf{restart}` commented out, so it restarts every service mapping an old copy of an upgraded library, as an ordinary `systemctl restart` with no sudo session in the journal; an OpenSSL update restarted the reference deployment's Linux node on 2026-10-01 and 2026-10-02 (#309), and a node stop is a drain with no time limit.
On a Mac the node is a launch agent and a root daemon cannot do the job.
On a Mac the node is a launch agent in the user's session, never root (Virtualization.framework needs the login keychain and tart's store is per-user).
On a Mac the same two are `sh.billet.upgrade` (`StartInterval` 300) and `sh.billet.images` (`StartCalendarInterval` daily), no `KeepAlive`, `RunAtLoad`; `agentOf` knows them, `Converger.Scheduled()` names them, and `local up` installs and loads both through `EnableScheduled` after the two services are proved (install, enable, then bootstrap; a loaded idle job is booted out and back in so a changed plist takes effect; a loaded job WITH a process is left alone, because it may be the upgrade transaction).
On a PostgreSQL ledger the journal carries `Ledger: external` and `advance` records `fenced`, `snapshotted` and `migrated` as reached without doing them, `rollBack` restores no ledger and `finish` clears no fence; the probe is `state.OpenPostgresProbe` (the standby's open across the fence, writes refused, nothing claimed or migrated), and the migration happens when the candidate claims.
On a difference it runs `billet check` against a candidate beside the file (removed in `always`), then `billet local down` against the configuration still installed, then installs 0600 with `backup: true`, then `billet local up`; an unchanged file runs `local up` alone.
On a loaded node, a cache-index `lock add` killed at the 15-second rbd bound was committed by the cluster after the attempt had listed the lockers, found none of its own, and failed.
On a packaged host the App key lands in root-owned `/etc/billet`, and systemd's `StateDirectory=` repairs recursively only when the top directory's owner is wrong, which after a restore it is not.
On a pull request `scripts/ci-scope.sh` selects JOB FAMILIES from the merge commit's diff (`HEAD^1..HEAD`, `--no-renames`, both sides of every record): ten `<family>=true|false` outputs (`host_lifecycle`, `postgres`, `postgres_command`, `postgres_retirement`, `package_lifecycle`, `terraform`, `terraform_consumer_floor`, `terraform_lint`, `replay`, `lint`) plus `schema=2`, written straight to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`.
On a shared ledger the claim authorises the migration, not the directory flock.
On ansible-core 2.21 `retries: N` runs N+1 attempts, sleeping between them without subtracting run time, and an exhausted `until` under `failed_when: false` is not failed (measured 2026-09-30), so the loop ends on the deadline rather than a count and the judgement is the tasks after the poll.
On clone v1 a snapshot must be protected before it is cloned and a protected snapshot with a live clone can be neither unprotected nor removed, so a generation any running job holds would be undeletable.
On systemd 255 `NeedDaemonReload` answers yes when a unit's own fragment or drop-ins changed since load AND for every unit while `unit_file_state_outdated` is set, which every bus unit-file operation that changed something does (`systemctl enable`, `disable`, `preset`, `mask`, `link`, `revert`: a snap refresh, a package install, the role's own enables) until a daemon-reload clears it; measured on the reference controller on 2026-09-07 (systemd 255.4): 464 of 464 units after snapd enabled one mount unit, billet's unit files untouched since the previous day, and the consumer's fleet check refused the whole fleet on it.
On tart it runs `pullTartImages` (absent only, a moving tag is not re-pulled); docker, ec2 and codebuild are nothing to do; `release.automatic: false` is nothing to do.
On the node, `internal/node/actions_cache.go`, `actions_proxy.go` and `actions_volume.go` intercept `actions/cache` traffic for Linux firecracker tiers.
On the reference systemd node, `ProtectSystem=strict` made `/var/lib/billet/upgrades` and `/usr/bin` read-only to the node's children: its first dispatched upgrade refused `open /var/lib/billet/upgrades/transaction.lock: read-only file system` on 2026-09-06 (#98).
On-demand Linux destroyed its machine between all 31 builds measured (31 boot ids), so untrusted work is admitted there only under `untrusted_vpc_id`, `untrusted_subnets` and `untrusted_security_group_ids`, verified on the project through `BatchGetProjects` because `StartBuild` has no VPC override, and still strictly weaker than an instance (the service role is readable at `169.254.170.2`).
Onboarding is the App Manifest flow, so every deployment ends up with provably identical minimal permissions for its scope.
Onboarding refuses everything it can before it touches GitHub.
Onboarding status handling: `{404, 422}` left the kill switch open for a 414; "every 4xx" swallowed a valid code on 429; only 404 establishes a code is unusable.
One `awk` reads to the end and has nothing to signal.
One branch per minor carries every patch; a hotfix is a commit on `release/vX.Y` plus the same button with the patch version, then merged back into main or the next release reverts it.
One gRPC server, in one package.
One key per target: the `default` target's store parameter is `github-app-key` and a further target's `github-app-key-<name>` (`GitHubTarget.KeyName`); the default key file beside the config is `app-private-key.pem` for `default` and `app-private-key-<name>.pem` otherwise; the archive carries `github/<name>/app-private-key.pem` per target (schema 3) and the host role installs each at `/etc/billet/app-private-key-<name>.pem`.
One lifecycle command at a time, via a host flock taken immediately before the first mutation.
One process writes the launch verdict from a closed vocabulary.
One query set serves both engines, generated once with the PostgreSQL engine.
One scale-set client and one policy client per target (`wiring.BuildTargets`; the server resolves each tier's through `WithTargets`, the node plane through `WithTargetJIT`); the path (`owner` or `owner/name`) is the client's config URL and the `scale_set.org` column, so a target rename in config orphans nothing.
One shard variable selects one section; the gate refuses a section from the wrong family.
One target, one connection, so the connection is health-checked.
One timeout knob must never serve a deadline that must expire and deadlines that must not; compare the deadlines the code handed out instead (`context.WithTimeout` on a bounded parent keeps the parent's deadline, so an inherited context compares exactly equal).
One to three commits is the working size.
One transaction, two service managers, three ledgers.
Online-and-idle, busy, absent and could-not-tell all keep the member and reset the run, and the watch lives in memory so a restart only delays a retirement.
Only "gone" lets teardown continue to unmap disks and remove the jail.
Only `-p ExecStartEx` shows `flags=privileged` (systemd v246 and later; an absent answer is uncertainty).
Only `CreateCacheEntry`, `FinalizeCacheEntryUpload` and `GetCacheEntryDownloadURL` on the CacheService are served locally; everything else, all of `ArtifactService` included, is spliced upstream with the runtime authorization untouched, because `ACTIONS_RESULTS_URL` carries artifact metadata and is in the release path.
Only `Discard` used to unmap; a failed create discarded directly, and on 2026-10-03 a `device map` that passed its bound was completed by the kernel afterwards, so the trashed volume stayed mapped until it was unmapped by hand.
Only `FragmentPath`, `SourcePath`, `DropInPaths`, `ControlGroup` and `ControlGroupId` are excluded.
Only `setsid` survives; macOS guests have no `setsid`, so the fallback is perl's `POSIX::setsid`.
Only `state`, `alloc` and `rollout` may import `ledgerdb`, for types; `forbidigo` bans `ledgerdb.New` outside `internal/state`'s direct members.
Only a cache a tier turns on explicitly (`explicitGuestCaches`) is held to where it can run, including the node-level refusal of a node without `node.cache`; otherwise every existing Firecracker node file without a cache listener would stop loading.
Only a job in the run's top-level workflow carries the run's own triggering ref, so only it can write, and only when the run calls no workflow file of the same path under any spelling of any ref (`callsTheFile`): `calledByTheRun` compares whole strings, and a self-call GitHub records as `@main` beside a job's `@refs/heads/main` would otherwise read as the top-level workflow.
Only absent or undecodable bytes fall back to `retirement.Root/server` — which is the PACKAGED path and emphatically not `config`'s own default, resolving under the invoking account's config directory; that confusion has now failed a package postinstall and a classifier admission on this branch.
Only build invocations are rewritten because the results origin also carries artifacts and logs the adapter does not serve.
Only check mode with that fact, an empty incapable answerer and no legacy claim admits the ordinary preview, reporting `unverified-check-mode` and explaining that a real run classifies with the staged candidate and may choose different work.
Only env-var and IMDSv2 credentials are supported; everything else is projected into the environment.
Only idle `held` escrow goes back, and only after the old session closed, since until then GitHub can assign against the advertisement it carries; when the close fails or outlives its grace it is kept until a poll lands, and the teardown neither closes a session the recovery already closed nor starts a second close beside one still in flight, and while a recovery is under way its own close runs aside too, so an open stuck on the client's per-target mutex cannot hold a stopping listener.
Only inside that branch does `billet_preparation_state_backend` read and validate the desired controller subtree; absent `server` means no ledger, while a present controller retains the SQLite default.
Only once the handler is installed does a node on a Mac publish `<log dir>/.drain-<label>` (`PublishDrainReport`: schema 1, label, pid, the kernel start time from `sysctl kern.proc.pid` to the microsecond, `request: "SIGUSR1"` as the capability, release for diagnosis; not `ps -o lstart=`, whose text follows the caller's time zone and locale, which differ between an operator's shell and the agent).
Only positive absence starts hypothetical-parent reasoning; returning to an existing ancestor resumes real observations.
Only positively absent optional files are omitted.
Only server-only passes `--server-only`; only retained-node carries B in `desired`.
Only states that prove no process remains count as stopped.
Only the control plane proper records (`openMode.records()`: not admin, not standby, not the probe), and only in `ClaimController` after the deployment binding, or a `billet check` from a newer laptop binary, or a newer server pointed at a foreign ledger, would fence the running server out of its own restart; a promoted standby records there too, and a revalidating admin handle re-reads the mark inside every write.
Only the retained route omits the server path from upgrade inspection; node checks remain.
Only what this run committed is unwound, on `context.WithoutCancel` with a timeout, because the likeliest way in is the operator's own interrupt.

Past the deadline the last read decides the words, naming `systemctl show billet-node -p ActiveState,SubState,MainPID` in each: a read without exactly the four properties is could-not-tell, the old process still in charge (deactivating, or its MainPID still there) or an active node with a job queued is "still draining", anything else (failed, a new process never ready) "did not come back"; a poll that lost the connection (`ignore_unreachable`) fails as could-not-tell.

Publication is guarded by three things at once: the expected generation, a live writer lease, and a monotone `FencingToken` whose zero value authorises nothing.
Publication merges: if the key moved since the clone, the newest generation is cloned (recorded in `hostVolume.Merge` before it is mounted), the job's missing objects copied in, and that published, so concurrent jobs' writes both survive; a failed discard keeps the record (`discardCASVolumes` is done only when every step succeeded).
Publication under the transaction lock, in one order the fs hook (`guardHook`, operations identified by descriptor metadata) asserts: `Lstat(active)` absent, `mkdir`, create `guard.json.tmp` (`O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK`), write, fsync, rename, fsync `active`, fsync the root (the root's parent is flushed by EVERY acquisition of the lock, right after the root is found or made, because an acquisition that made it and died before its flush leaves a root the next one finds existing).

Rotate mutates five files in sequence; a reader without the lock captures a key from one generation beside a certificate from another, an archive that loads cleanly and verifies nothing.
Rotate writes certificate then key, Retire removes key then certificate, and `LoadServing` reads in that same order, so a certificate with no key beside it always means not committed.
Route A is a workstation on the same network (or a small always-on machine registered as an ordinary Actions runner billet does not manage).
Route B is `converge-aws-ssm`: the SSM connection plugin ships every module through an S3 bucket even for modules that send no files, and the App key transits it, so the module creates the bucket with versioning suspended and a short expiry, a hybrid activation, a scoped policy and a GitHub OIDC role trusting an exact subject (a wildcard admits any pull-request job; an environment subject does not close that).
Route C is `converge-cloudflare`: a tunnel, an Access application and a service token, no S3 and no plaintext-secret path, requiring a domain on Cloudflare; `cloudflared` on the host is the `cloudflared_connector` role.
Route D is `converge-cloudflare-warp`: the CI runner enrols as a headless WARP client with a service token (`mdm.xml`), authenticates as the shared `non_identity@<team>.cloudflareaccess.com` principal, and one Gateway L4 rule keyed on that principal is its entire reach; the module creates the token, the Service Auth (`non_identity`) enrolment policy and the rule, and deliberately never adopts the account's WARP enrolment application (an omitted optional plans to null on an adopted resource in provider v5, and `policies` is one).
Routing and serving are pinned to measurement (git 2.51.0, 2026-09-25): `url.insteadOf` drops checkout's github.com-scoped header, so `billet cache git-credential`, run by git in the repository after the node's 401, hands the node the session bearer as the user and that header as the password; an identity `pushInsteadOf` keeps pushes direct; git keeps its old base URL when it follows a redirect on that retry, so the node follows a renamed repository itself (`gitProxy.follow`).
Run `make sqlc` after editing `internal/state/queries` or adding a migration, because sqlc reads the migration history as its schema.
Run as root over an identity directory owned by another account it re-executes itself as that account (`runAsLedgerOwner`, behind the `statusEUID`, `statusOwnerOf` and `statusReexec` seams), because the bundled driver's read-only open of a stopped ledger creates root-owned sidecars the service account then cannot open; an owner that cannot be read is a refusal, not "run in place".
Run in line on the node's serial command queue, each failure delayed the next launch until launches took four to five minutes.

SCOPE, narrowly.
SDK cost: 13.2MB and 15 modules for one `RunInstances`, versus 21.8MB for all of billet.
SETTLED is the steady state — nothing taken, nothing opened, the postconditions judged and reported (`archive`, `config`, and the five units in the words the shared table admits; `masked-runtime` admitted for none, a not-found unit quiescent only BESIDE inactive with no process, a failing one named in a `postcondition` refusal).
SIGKILL re-adopts; SIGTERM drains.
SIGTERM does nothing: `--new-pid-ns` makes the VMM its namespace's init, Firecracker installs no SIGTERM handler, and the kernel drops a default-disposition signal sent to a namespace init from an ancestor namespace (measured 2026-09-30, v1.16.1 under the jailer: `SigCgt 0000000441801449`, `kill -TERM` ignored for over two minutes, `kill -KILL` immediate). billet passes `--new-pid-ns` because the jailer's documentation says the pid file is written only then, and a future version honouring its docs must not make "no pid file" read as "nothing running".
SIGTERM is a drain (the node reports it is not taking new work and is waiting for the compute already running, with no bound), so the node outlives the job and destroys the VM itself; a restart test that sends TERM proves the drain while looking like it proved adoption.
SIGTERM to a jailed VMM (a pid-namespace init with no handler): ignored for over two minutes; SIGKILL: immediate (2026-09-30).
SKIP accepts `endpoint`, `retirement` and `retirement-request` in any order with no empty or repeated members; `retirement` skips all of R, so the guard group's `SKIP=endpoint,retirement` skips requests too.
SQL lives only in `internal/state/queries/*.sql` (including `internal/alloc`'s and `internal/rollout`'s), compiled by sqlc (pinned, `SQLC_VERSION`) into `internal/state/ledgerdb` and bound by `internal/state/queryset.go`.
SQLite must be on local storage.
SQLite's prepare resolves a missing column, a missing table, a syntax error and an `ON CONFLICT` whose unique index a migration removed (PostgreSQL defers that to EXECUTE), and sqlc models no indexes at all, so nothing else here would catch that class.
SQLite's single-writer rule stops two connections writing at once. It does not stop two billet processes both long-polling GitHub and taking turns writing conflicting scheduling decisions to one ledger, which double-admits jobs onto a host that cannot hold them and fails silently.
SQS endpoint suffixes, resolved 2026-09-04: China is `amazonaws.com.cn` for all three forms (standard, legacy `<region>.queue.`, and `vpce`), the commercial names are NXDOMAIN there and vice versa, and GovCloud takes the commercial suffix — so the partition is derived from the region's `cn-` prefix (`config.AWSDNSSuffix`, which `awsjson.DNSSuffixFor` calls) rather than from the partition name.
SQS hosts, resolved 2026-09-04: `sqs.cn-north-1.amazonaws.com` and `cn-north-1.queue.amazonaws.com` are NXDOMAIN, `sqs.cn-north-1.amazonaws.com.cn` answers and `cn-north-1.queue.amazonaws.com.cn` is a CNAME onto it; `sqs.us-west-2.amazonaws.com.cn` is NXDOMAIN.

Several spot nodes are several queues, and `spot_node_names` is the one input that makes them: each entry creates a queue named exactly it, and the node role's consumer grant, the router's forwarding grant and the served set all derive from the one list `local.spot_queues`, so the three converge to the same set from one input — a queue granted by hand but never named to the router was exactly the shape that dropped a warning while the grant propagated (#66), and the plan test asserts the three sets equal the declared queues rather than a literal.
