Systemd 255 matches property-filter names literally: `*` is not a wildcard, and adding `--all` does not remove a filter.
Systemd 255 prints no text key for empty `EnvironmentFiles`, command arrays or directory-symlink arrays, even with `--all`; a missing text key is never evidence of an empty array.
Systemd nodes through v0.9.2 need one manual move onto the fixed dispatcher, because FROM launches the transaction.
THE ASK IS CHOSEN PER PROCESS BY WHAT THE RUNNING PROCESS SAYS OF ITSELF, never by the binary on disk, which a rollout may have replaced (#281).
THE AVAILABILITY SQLSTATES ARE AN ALLOWLIST, never a class prefix: `08001`, `08003`, `08006`, `08007`, `53300`, `57P01`, `57P02`, `57P03` — because class 08 also holds `08004` (the server refusing this client) and `08P01` (a protocol violation), and class 57 also holds `57014` (a statement the server cancelled, which a `statement_timeout` produces) and `57P04` (a dropped database), every one of which is the caller's to fix.
THE COMMAND RESUMES AN INTERRUPTED TRANSITION FROM EVERY PHASE, by one of two paths, and which one is decided by the FILESYSTEM and not by the phase: a `stopped` journal whose move already completed is past the archive whatever its journal says, because the exclusion and the identity the ordinary path would read are inside the directory that has moved.
THE DANGEROUS ACT IS ANY RESTART OF A RUNNING CONNECTOR, whatever causes it: the role reads the credential and unit as they are (a stat loop for owner, group and mode, which is metadata and uncensored; both slurps as root under `no_log`, because an older installer wrote `--token <TOKEN>` into ExecStart and the unit being adopted may carry it; the template through `lookup`) against the bytes, owner and mode it would write, asks systemd for the unit's ActiveState, and refuses to rewrite either unless the state is exactly `inactive` or `failed` (positive evidence nothing serves traffic; `activating` under a long ExecStartPost is running) or `billet_cloudflared_carries_ansible_transport` is a definite `false`.
THE ERROR IS ASKED FIRST in all of it: a context that has expired by the time it is examined proves nothing about an error that arrived before it, so a binding that established another deployment's ledger is still that.
THE FRAGMENT COMPARED IS THE ONE THE NEXT RELOAD WOULD LOAD: the module's source-name map names the winning entry per unit name, and a higher-priority fragment, a mask or an alias that appeared since the load refuses, as does a not-found unit with a file in a lookup path; absence is positive or nothing (`LoadState=not-found` with no file), an unfamiliar `NeedDaemonReload` answer refuses, every drop-in location is stat'ed first by a task that fails on any error but absence (`find` answers "is not a directory" for any failed stat, permission denied included, so its text cannot tell absence from an error), `find` is given only the directories that exist and anything it then skips refuses, a header outside the grammar this dry run reads refuses (a malformed one is a parse error systemd stops at), and the skipped-paths rule holds for a not-found unit too.
THE GATE PROVES ESCALATION by running the M8 probe, one acquisition (`b1b`) and one dry run (`b7w`) in the `become` mode: the play as the invoker through `setpriv` with no `ansible_become` forced, so a task the role marks `become` goes through sudo and the wrapper's log must show `uid=0`; the `escalated` mode runs the play as root and proves nothing about `become`, and the gate refuses to run as root for that reason.
THE HOLDER GRAMMAR HAS ONE PYTHON TWIN, `plugins/module_utils/holder.py`, exposed to templates as `junioryono.billet.valid_holder` (`plugins/filter/holder.py`, a re-export) and imported by `guard_fallback.py` for a record's `taken_over_from`, held to `tests/fixtures/holder-vectors.json`, which `checkHolder`'s Go test writes (`holder_check.py` imports both by the collection's dotted name and requires the filter to expose the shared function); a regular expression counted characters where the command counts bytes and admitted U+FFFD and the C1 controls (round 3 of commit 4c), and the fallback reader's own `startswith("C")` refused a format character such as U+200B that Go's `IsControl` admits, so a chain Go wrote blocked the fallback (commit 5b's first review).
THE ID IS GITHUB'S, READ BY THE EXACT NAME: a remote node's JIT mint journals the registration's id, but the listener's own launch path journals a member with a name and no id, which the first version skipped.
THE JOURNAL AND THE TABLE live in `internal/retirement`: `Journal` (schema 1, root-owned 0600 under the 0700 `retired/` directory, which `EnsureRetiredDir` examines on EVERY admission (this account's, 0700, not a link; a 0600 file in a directory another account can write is one that account can replace by its entry) and whose parent it flushes on every admission too, since the creating invocation may have died before its own flush; read through `regularfile` THROUGH EOF (a stat's size is not the file: a complete document in a prefix with more behind it is malformed, and a file that moved under the read is unreadable) and trusted only when owned by the reading account with no group/other bits; the writer held to the reader's 64 KiB bound before publication, the previous journal kept; `provenance` immutable, `ownership` rebound with the chain appended; `row_done`, `completed_by`, `settled`, `timer_stopped_at`, held to the TAIL'S ORDER by `tailWellFormed` on every read and write (`done_at` with `done` and nowhere else, `row_done` iff `completed_by`, `settled` only over an acknowledged row, so a hand-written "settled" journal cannot take the settled shortcut past the acknowledgement); validated whole by `Validate` against the retiring host, the identity, the row's binding fields and the guard's holder or takeover chain, a settled `done` by provenance alone), the completion document and the survivor's answer (`DecodeCompletion`, `DecodeAnswer`, `Answer.MatchesJournal`, every binding field required), and the phase table (`Decide(variant, phase, Facts)` and `DispatchFor(row, journal)`, whose every cell is written to `tests/fixtures/retirement/vectors.json` by the Go test and compared on every run, so the role's and the loader's readers are held to the Go table; `config-rewritten` with the stage installed on a retained node restarts under either verdict and REFUSES an unobservable one, as `archived` does).
THE LEDGER FACTORIES RUN UNDER THE SAME EXCLUSION (`underIdentityExclusion` in `ledger.go`): a command that already holds an access is found in the process-wide registry (`heldAccesses`, keyed by cleaned directory, registered by `openIdentityAccess` and cleared by `Release`) and lends it; a command that holds none (`billet status`, the upgrade timer's `openStateForDecision`) takes one for the open and releases it once the handle exists, so `state.OpenAdmin`'s `MkdirAll` can never race a retirement's rename and a `billet status` five minutes later cannot mint a second identity beside the archive.
THE LOCK ORDER IS `session.mu` THEN `hv.io`: a transfer holding `io` never takes `session.mu`, so a write is marked `Dirty` durably when it is ADMITTED (`openCASHandle(write)`), which is also what lets a restart before the completion still publish it; `releaseCASVolume` waits for `io` at most `casReleaseWait` and comes back on a later pass.
THE MARKER IS CLEARED ONLY ONCE THE JOURNAL ACKNOWLEDGES THE ROW and fresh local postconditions pass; those postconditions are checked again after marker persistence before `settled` is written, so the one crash remainder is an unsettled journal beside a guard with no marker, which is exactly what the takeover rule reads as an unfinished tail; the marker is cleared from the record READ AGAIN through the guard's descriptor (`classifyGuardDirFrom` then `judgeGuardShape`), never from the shape the run classified before its own intent wrote the marker.
THE NODE'S REGISTRATION RECORD is the inspector's evidence of what the running process dials: `internal/nodeclient/record.go` writes `/run/billet/registration/current` (seven members: `schema` 1, `node`, `deployment`, `incarnation`, `invocation_id`, `endpoint` as `internal/endpoint`'s canonical text of the client's request base, `registered_at`) through the zero-value `durablefile.Installer` after EVERY accepted registration and never before one, a drain's re-registration included, a failure logged on every registration that fails to record with the node kept serving and nothing retried without another registration; the path is `nodeRegistrationRecordPath(hostOS)`, one spelling, empty on darwin; the node unit's `RuntimeDirectory=billet/locks billet/registration` (packaged and templated, the server declaring none, because systemd re-owns a declared directory recursively at a start where its owner differs and removes it at that unit's stop, measured on systemd 255, 2026-09-09) is what makes `/run/billet/registration` writable under `ProtectSystem=strict` and empty at every node start.
THE OPTIONAL TEXT MEMBERS OF AN ANSWER (`shape`, `next`) ARE TYPED BY THE CHECKS whatever the outcome, and the refusal's `fail_msg` reads them only under `is string`, because Ansible templates an assert's `fail_msg` before the assertion decides, so a null `next` on an ACQUIRED answer failed there, after the judgement and before the facts, and the token was never saved (round 8).
THE PRE-R OBSERVATION REQUIRES AN EXIT THE EXECUTABLE CHOSE, defined, POSITIVE and not the bound's (`rc > 0 and rc not in [124, 137]`; a kill that reaches `timeout`'s own process group is a NEGATIVE status in Ansible, because GNU timeout signals its group and SIGKILL cannot be ignored, and the gate's `BILLET_GATE_PRE_R_IGNORE_TERM=1` makes the fake reach it) before the diagnostic is matched, at all four sites (the parser, the dry run's two reads, the closing recheck), because an executable that prints "unknown command" and then hangs exits 124 under `timeout` and would otherwise have selected the unheld legacy protocol (the gate's `BILLET_GATE_PRE_R_HANG=<cmd|all>` makes the pre-R fake do that).
THE PREPARATION IS ONE COMMAND UNDER ONE LOCK (`convergeguardprepare.go`, `billet converge-guard prepare --holder H --json` with `--validate`, `--candidate C [--allow-downgrade]`, `--no-change`, `--recovery`, `--dry-run`, `--expect-bootstrap`, `--expect-id`; the flag table refused before anything is opened): the record's eight members add `id` (public, 128 bits from `crypto/rand`, minted at publication, adopted onto a five-member record by the first `--validate`), `token` (the acquirer's, printed only in the `acquired` answer) and `preparing` (true from acquisition to `settle --token`); the pointer validated under the lock, the recorded executable verified by digest on every mutating branch, the owed flushes completed on readmission, a stray `guard.json.tmp` removed first, the judgement (capability through the candidate's `prepare --dry-run --json`, judged by `judgeDryRunAnswer` as the dry-run report naming the held guard's own id and never through `status`, which the guard's first commits answered without a `prepare` to follow, the downgrade through `version.Compare`) before any re-binding; `release --cleanup --token` only for a preparing guard with that token and no pointer (a settled one answers "the preparation window has closed"); refusals exit 2 with a reason code, could-not-tell exit 3; `--dry-run` takes no lock and reports every shape.
THE RECOVERY DIRECTORY IS THE VALIDATED `pointer_target` ALONE: the command answers `recovery_dir` beside it on a validation, the parser requires the two equal (`recovery_dir` check) and takes the fact from `pointer_target`, never from a member the grammar did not judge.
THE ROLE'S OUTER BOUNDS around the endpoint commands are sums over the phases and observations the commands may make, from role vars in `vars/main.yml` that `TestTheRoleMirrorsTheEndpointCommandsPhaseBudgets` holds to the Go constants.
THE ROW GOES THROUGH THE JOURNAL'S LOCATOR (`retireOpenLedgerByLocator`: the backend, the DSN variable's name, the environment file and the archive recorded at `intent`, since the installed configuration has no `server:` and the identity has moved) AND THROUGH `state.OpenPostgresCompletion`, which claims nothing and migrates nothing — an admin open takes the deployment's controller exclusion and migrates the shared schema whenever the survivor happens to be down, which is the one moment a retired host must not become this deployment's control plane; a structural witness holds the file to that one open.
THE SIGTERM PATH IS ONCE PER PROCESS, ACROSS CALLS, through `launchctl kill TERM gui/<uid>/<label>` (which addresses the service's current process, never a pid read earlier that another process may have reused), because the node's second SIGTERM escalates its drain: before sending, the stop writes `<log dir>/.stop-<label>` naming the process's incarnation (pid and `ps -o lstart=` start time, the `started` seam), a retry that finds the same incarnation resumes the wait and sends nothing, a different process under the same pid is asked afresh, a record that cannot be written means nothing is sent, and the record is removed once the process is gone.
THE STAGING'S OBSERVATION OF THE MANAGED BINARY IS HELD TO THE HOLD'S (round 9): on the candidate-first routes the staging stats `/usr/bin/billet` BEFORE anything is held, and that observation is what the transaction backs up from and what its rollback restores, so `prepare-exclusion.yml` compares it with the second answer's `managed.present` and `managed.sha256` (the command's own observation under the lock) and refuses a disagreement inside the protocol block, where the rescue releases the guard (`b6j`).
THE TOKEN an `acquired` answer carries is the acquiring invocation's one authorisation, the cleanup release inside its own preparation window (`release --cleanup --token`, refused for a settled guard, a wrong token or a transaction pointer): it is printed only in that answer, kept in a fact no report prints, and passed in the argv of the second call, `settle` and the cleanup under `no_log`; on a default kernel other local users can read that argv, and a party holding it can do nothing to a root-owned guard without being root, and root needs no token.
THE WHOLE ATTEMPT IS BOUNDED (`retireLedgerBound`, two minutes), because the open's thirty-second budget ends when it returns and the binding and the completion would otherwise run with no deadline at all while the guard is held.
Tagged releases exist (`release/vX.Y` branches, a moving `v0` tag, signed manifests), so the ledger's schema is no longer free to change: migrations are append-only, their statement bytes are published and checksummed, and every deployment records them — see `billet-state`.

The CA is a slow cliff.
The CI key and the App key are written under `RUNNER_TEMP` by a shell builtin under `umask 077` (BSD `install` refuses a pipe as its source, so not `install /dev/stdin`) and named through `ANSIBLE_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE` and `BILLET_GITHUB_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH`; the WARP service token goes into `mdm.xml` through `install -m 0600 /dev/stdin` on the Linux runner; the `environment` input is validated line by line into a 0600 file and reaches every Ansible call (the listing, the render and both passes) through `with-environment.py`, which puts the lines into a dictionary and `execvpe`s, never `env(1)`, whose own argv would carry the values until it execs, and never a shell assignment, because bash evaluates the value assigned to `RANDOM`, `SECONDS` and their kin as arithmetic (a subscript there runs a command substitution), a failed `export` inside a subshell does not stop the run, and an exported loop cursor is overwritten by the next iteration; the script's own decisions are readonly under a `billet_action_` prefix the input refuses by name; a name that would change Ansible, ssh or the runner (`ANSIBLE_*`, `GITHUB_*`, `RUNNER_*`, `SSH_*` (an askpass helper runs, an agent socket changes the identities offered), `DISPLAY`, `PATH`, `HOME` and their kin) is refused by name; a line carrying a control character is refused, because a carriage return inside a value is one line to the shell and two to a reader with newline translation, the second of which can set `PATH` (the launcher reads with `newline=""` and refuses the same bytes); a malformed line is reported by its number, never its contents, and a host-key refusal (`actions/converge-fleet/judge-ssh-options.py`, with a `--decode` mode so a test can observe what it reads) interprets ONLY `-o` in the tokens Ansible hands ssh, which are `shlex`'s, each stripped and the empty ones dropped (its connection plugin's `_split_ssh_args`; a token that opens with a space is a flag to ssh, not a non-flag), and refuses every other flag by name, because ssh parses flags with getopt and `-4oStrictHostKeyChecking=no` or `-4F/tmp/x` is a cluster the action would otherwise skip (`AddressFamily=inet` is the `-o` spelling of `-4`); inside an option the keyword is read the way readconf's `strdelim` reads it (a double-quoted keyword runs to its closing quote and the value starts right after, so `"StrictHostKeyChecking"no` is the keyword and `no`; otherwise to whitespace or `=`) and the value the way `argv_split` reads one argument (single or double quotes, concatenated fragments; a backslash escapes a quote or a backslash in either quote mode and a space outside quotes only, any other backslash kept as written; a hash is a comment only where a token would begin; an unquoted space or tab ends it, and nothing else does), so `'no'`, `n"o"` and `no # x` are all `no` and `"key\"name"` is `key"name`; a keyword is a letter followed by letters and digits (`ForwardX11`), one with a quote in its middle and an unclosed quote are unreadable, and what the two parsers do not model is refused rather than guessed at; the refused keywords are each a way of accepting a key the pins do not hold: `Include`, `UserKnownHostsFile`, `GlobalKnownHostsFile`, `KnownHostsCommand`, `HostKeyAlias`, `StrictHostKeyChecking` off, `CheckHostIP` off, `NoHostAuthenticationForLocalhost`, `VerifyHostKeyDNS`, `GSSAPIKeyExchange` (a patched client authenticates the server without a host key), and `ControlPath` or `ControlMaster`, because ssh reuses an existing master socket before it verifies anything and that master was authenticated under whatever checking it had; the refusal names the canonical option, never the SSH arguments, which may carry a ProxyCommand (`-e` is for non-secret values, because argv is world-readable for the run).
The CN decides which node a request is from and the organization which deployment; a node's state directory mints an identity when it has none, which is right for a control plane and wrong for a node, so `state.AdoptDeploymentID` writes the certificate's answer down and refuses to overwrite a different one.

The disabled-override database is durable, keyed by label, outlives the plist and accepts labels that never existed: `uninstall` removes the plist, flushes that removal, then clears the override, because the reverse order leaves a window in which a login starts the node being uninstalled, and leaving it set makes the next install bootstrap a service launchd silently refuses to run.

The drain waited on them until a second signal ended it, because the drain-time reconcile retires only surplus beyond `TotalAssignedJobs`, and the declined assignments kept that count above them.
The drain-request gate is therefore about a stop waiting on a drain nobody began, and about the instant before a process's runtime installs its handler.
The drift check accepts a loaded `ExitTimeOut` equal to the declared value, or to `min(declared, 60)` only on a release that clamps (`sw_vers -productVersion` 27 or later, the `productVersion` seam; unreadable counts as unclamped), and refuses anything else, such as the five-second default of a stale bootstrap; refusing 60 refused every `local up` after the first on macOS 27.
The drop-in is validated as the whole configuration sshd reads, with the file in place and a backup taken; the rescue restores the backup or removes the file only when the copy itself succeeded, judged from a stat the role took beforehand and never from the copy's missing return metadata; and the restart handler is notified by the validation, not the copy, so a rollback never restarts sshd onto a configuration another file broke.
The dry run is a CLASSIFIER that answers one word, and the role's caller (`retirement.yml`) branches on nothing else.
The dry run will not reload the live manager; `roles/host/tasks/dryrun-policy.yml` compares, for each billet unit reporting the flag, the facts the inspection reads from the loaded state (`User`, `Group`, `Type`, the loaded ExecStart records over `busctl`, as an array) with the on-disk fragment READ AS SYSTEMD READS IT (every assignment held to `billet_service_policy_known_directives`, the directives the shipped units and templates write per section, since a directive the gate does not know can stop systemd's parser before the compared ones, `ExecStartPre=/` failing the load with ENOEXEC; a section outside that set refuses; one of the four directives counts only inside `[Service]`, a repeated header resumes the section, whitespace around `=` on one of the four refuses, a continued, indented or non-assignment line or a carriage return refuses; every other assignment is ignored, since the shipped units carry `[Unit]` and `[Install]` lines, comments and an empty `CapabilityBoundingSet=`) and held to the role's own template grammar (exactly one of each of the four, ExecStart words of plain characters separated by single spaces: no prefix, specifier, quote, backslash, `$` or tab), refuses any drop-in loaded or on disk in any location the running manager searches (`Manager.UnitPath` from the bus, held to `billet_service_policy_unit_path_allowlist`; `<unit>.d`, `<alias>.d`, `billet-.service.d`, `service.d`), refuses an alias loaded (`Names`) or on disk, where `plugins/modules/unit_names.py` builds the manager's effective source-name map in lookup order (a shadowed lower-priority symlink disregarded; masks and links out of every lookup path set apart; a target chased with missing components tolerated and classified an alias when it lies under any lookup path, original or resolved spelling, nested or not, as systemd 255 does) and follows alias chains by unit name as systemd's lookup does (an instance target with no entry falls back to its template; at most seven hops; a dangling target, a cycle or a longer chain refuses; an alias systemd's name map would reject, such as a plain name pointing at a template or a self-alias, refuses rather than claiming the name and hiding the entry below it; a mask is decided after the chase, so `/missing/../dev/null` is a refused unsafe remainder and not a mask; search-path membership includes equality, so a link to a lookup directory itself refuses rather than claiming the name), and continues with a report when every pair agrees; the packaged units and the rendered server template are passing fixtures.

The shape's price (`leases.price_micros_per_hour`) and the placed host's site are written on the lease when the shape is charged, at escrow and again on a resize, and `archive` copies them with the provider, the shape and the charged vector onto `job_history` (migration 49); the price is never re-read from the node's catalogue, because `sameEC2PlacementShapes` ignores price and a node may re-register with new rates while the lease is open.
The shared controller-side postconditions remain strict; only this ordinary-entry observer permits quiet inactive/failed nodes with zero main/control/cgroup processes, no job, persistent enablement and loaded/installed agreement.
The shared renderer supports zero files or one absolute literal path, excludes control/space/specifier/escape syntax and emits `-` only for `ignore_errors=true`.
The shared stopped proof checks current quiet timers and controller enablement, zero controller main PID plus positive cgroup disappearance or empty `cgroup.procs` throughout its subtree under `/sys/fs/cgroup`, reconciled backup completion, and the retained invocation, runtime registration and resource identities before stopped status, again after status persistence before stopped journal, and under the authority exclusion immediately before archive.
The shared typed environment reader now supplies release inspection's `environment_file_specs` alongside its path-only compatibility field; both opening and closing reads preserve optionality, including for quiet units.
The shim is installed twice on the host and detects a sibling shim by the marker on its line 2, never by path, because two copies comparing paths exec each other forever; it is never mounted over an image's own client.
The shipped `playbooks/fleet.yml` targets the entire `control_plane` group in one play, so both controllers share that play when both are in the group and included by the host limit.
The shipped image's apt source names TWO HTTPS mirrors (`archive.ubuntu.com`, then `mirrors.edge.kernel.org`) with `Acquire::Retries 3` and 30-second timeouts in `/etc/apt/apt.conf.d/90billet-fetch`, written by `install_cloud_base` before GitHub's build; since the `ubuntu24/20260920.314` pin GitHub's `configure-apt.sh` writes `zz-retries` (one retry, 15-second timeouts on x64, for fast failover), which apt reads last, so those are the image's effective values from that step on and GitHub's apt tests assert them; GitHub's `configure-apt-sources.sh` rewrites only `azure.archive.ubuntu.com` URIs, so it leaves them as they are.
The shipped playbook `junioryono.billet.fleet` is the consumer's `site.yml`, and it runs the converge guard first in every play.
The shutdown grace was 90 seconds against a 10-minute node command timeout, so ordinary slow destroys tripped it; a bound must be larger than the longest legitimate operation under it.
The slots are left registered and charged, exactly as the second signal leaves them, and the successor adopts them.
The snapshot version is `0.0.0-SNAPSHOT-<sha>` because Debian requires a leading digit.
The source binding is necessary even with the current workflow guard: older tagged reusable workflows remain callable.
The state and the enablement are two `systemd_service` tasks, both `no_log` because the module returns the unit's whole status, ExecStart included, and an adopted unit may still carry an inline token in a dry run that did not rewrite it; "the state task changed" is what means a process was started or restarted (from `inactive`, `failed` or `deactivating` alike), and the wait keys on exactly that.
The state words reach the statements as parameters (`RetirementReserved` etc.), never as literals, and the reservation time is compared as the STRING the row holds, never re-formatted.
The stock fake control includes inactive condition-skipped `systemd-firstboot.service` beneath active `sysinit.target`; admission never traverses it.
The store lock closes the delete race.
The strip must be whole-line: `s/#.*$//` treats `${v#v}` as a comment and the result fails `bash -n`.
The suite replays three hundred jobs by default; `BILLET_REPLAY_JOBS=2000` is the acceptance-size run, about a minute and a half on a laptop without the race detector and too slow for CI's shared race-instrumented test job, so CI runs it in its own `replay` job without `-race`; `-replay.out DIR` keeps each run's records and summary.
The supported unit `shape` is exactly what billet ships: one loaded record, argv `<managed path> <role> --config <absolute path>`, path the managed path, the rendered view equal to the argv joined by spaces, no filesystem-remapping directive (`RootDirectory`, `RootImage`, `BindPaths`, `BindReadOnlyPaths`, `MountImages`, `ExtensionImages`, `ExtensionDirectories`, `TemporaryFileSystem`: under those an absolute path names another file while the root still reads `/`, a configuration extension overlaying `/etc` included), at most one `EnvironmentFile` (the package has none, the role's template adds one; every `EnvironmentFiles` property line is read with exactly the ` (ignore_errors=yes|no)` suffix stripped and the whole path kept, because a path can itself contain ` (`), no `Environment=`; a wrapper, an expansion, a quoted multi-word argument, a relative path or a second record is could-not-tell, and a drop-in that loads as the supported shape passes, because the loaded records are what is judged.

The systemd readiness loops wait 720s, longer than the two bounded calls they follow, and stop at once on a container that has exited.
The tail is the local work first and the ledger last, and its order is what makes its crash windows recoverable.

The threat model is stated in the README: billet is not a sandbox for untrusted code, and a job can affect the host it runs on unless the backend is a real boundary and the network is its own.
The token exchange is admitted one at a time through a channel, not a mutex, so a waiting caller gives up with its own context (#206).
The token is decided by the exact reason and by `job_history.started_at` before the reason's text, so a node cannot suppress it for a job the ledger saw start; `force-released` is refused over the wire.
The token names the operation (key plus volume), never the attempt, so a restarted attempt finds what a previous one made; a refusal AWS parsed is never retried; an ambiguous answer is reconciled against eventually consistent `DescribeSnapshots` for about a minute; a snapshot in error state counts as the token spent; two snapshots carrying one token are refused.
The toolcache installers are one file with one seam.
The trailing `< /dev/null` is mandatory.
The transaction flock is taken non-blocking before the network, because resolving a channel can hang past the node's acknowledgement and every retry started another stuck process; lock order is transaction lock then `decision.lock`.
The transaction then inspects the candidate digest, preserves config, units, binary and enablement in a manifest, publishes its pointer `active/recovery` inside the guard by `ln -sT` proved by `readlink` (a managed binary that predates the guard, with no candidate, claims `active` with the pre-R no-replace hard link under the legacy protocol), proves the configured images compatible, drains node then server, removes `/usr/bin/billet`, fences, snapshots, installs and migrates as sole writer, runs `--upgrade-probe` units that never poll or dispatch, then installs steady units, records the decision, opens the fence and starts server then node.
The transaction's image step, `Host.PrepareImages` (the `imaged` step, after the stop and before the fence), is the candidate's `images compatible --result-file` then `images pull --verify` per listed image on firecracker, `pullTartImages` on tart.
