Unconfirmed cleanup names the outstanding retiring host, survivor, run and transition; ordinary work stays bypassed even when cleanup succeeds.
Under `controllers: active-passive` the first controller logs `standing by` and then `promoted to`, never `claimed`.
Under `default-branch` a job's writes publish only for a completion whose `server.CacheAuthority` is proven from GitHub's record of the run (never the launch assignment, never `ACTIONS_RUNTIME_TOKEN`, never `jobWorkflowRef` alone, which a feature branch can point at the default branch by calling a reusable workflow pinned `@main`) and names the session's exact lease, owner and repository; could-not-tell publishes nothing.
Under `fair` the longest-waiting tier holds freed room until its shape fits (head-of-line blocking on purpose, and deadlock-free because there is one winner chosen by a wait it cannot extend); it is bounded by the longest running job ONLY WHILE THE WAITER'S LISTENER IS THERE TO BUY, which on 2026-09-23 it was not: the longest waiter's listener sat on a dead broker connection for 18 minutes, could neither buy nor clear its wait, and every tier sharing its host declined every assignment with 78 of 136 vCPU free.
Under systemd (`linux` and `INVOCATION_ID` present), `launch` runs `systemd-run --unit=billet-host-upgrade-<rollout>-g<generation> --service-type=oneshot --collect --quiet --no-block --property=TimeoutStartSec=88200 -- <binary> host-upgrade ...`: the root unit escapes the node's read-only mount namespace and cgroup, its name prevents concurrent redelivery, and `CombinedOutput` reports launcher failures immediately.
Unfinished journals without the captured configuration path or original invocation evidence refuse the pre-handoff proof by name; an unmarked resource defaults to required input.
Unix sockets support the bound on both platforms.
Unknown boot-id, directory or traversal evidence refuses.
Unknown path or service-effect evidence refuses before dependent mutation; exact node unit replacement cannot introduce unproved execution semantics.
Unknown selectors, selecting and skipping the same section, and `ONLY=retirement-request` with `SKIP=retirement` refuse.
Unknown, absent, repeated or contradictory observations remain could-not-tell.
Unknown, open and recent leases and foreign names are kept and counted; a ledger error stops the pass; every pass is recorded in `credential_sweeps`.
Unlike the package the role owns the file and puts back an edit.
Unreachability is a property of the ERROR, never of the step that produced it, and its rule is MEASURED.
Unreadable, changed or unsupported evidence refuses as could-not-tell before the operation and leaves the phase unchanged.
Until 2026-09-25 it was, and a waiter launching eight slots one at a time into a node whose command queue took four to five minutes a launch held every tier for twenty minutes.
Untrusted work needs `node.ec2.untrusted_security_group_ids`; an instance isolates the kernel, not the VPC.
Untrusted work needs a real boundary and a network of its own, and each backend answers differently.
Up to the archive the ordinary path reads both from the installed configuration and takes the transition's own exclusion; past it (`retireResumeArchived`, `cmd/billet/serverretireresume.go`) EVERYTHING COMES FROM THE JOURNAL — the identity from the archive it recorded, the ledger from the locator when the tail asks for it — and the driver runs with NO configuration observation, because there may be none to take (the rewrite installs the staged bytes and holds them to the digest intent recorded).
Upgrade the server first; the reverse is refused, and the node adds its own range to every registration failure so the operator is not left with `json: unknown field "min_version"`.
Upstream bugs GitHub ships are parity too: `install-bazel.sh` writes `USE_BAZEL_FALLBACK_VERSION=silent:` with no version, because it reads a `bazel --version` line Bazel 9 no longer prints, and the gate holds the variable, not a value GitHub's image lacks.
Use a cleaned-up `os.MkdirTemp("/tmp", ...)` for socket directories: macOS `t.TempDir` paths exceed the Unix address limit.
Use a here-string, which has no writer to signal.
Use one when the failure mode is a step moving rather than a property changing.
User data is 16384 bytes, gzipped, and `packUserData` is the gate.
Validate every finding yourself before acting on it.
Validated against a live account with `iam:SimulateCustomPolicy` in both modes.
Vendored scripts are pinned to LF.
Verify by hash, not by grepping for text that may already be absent: a substitution that matches nothing reports SURVIVED, which is indistinguishable from a vacuous test.
Versions are dense from 1 and that is load-bearing.
Virtualization.framework refuses a third concurrent macOS guest ("The number of VMs exceeds the system limit") and a guest under 4GiB (`LessThanMinimalResourcesError`).
Virtualization.framework refuses a third macOS guest and one under 4GiB; `config.DefaultMacOSVMLimit = 2` is pinned to that refusal.
WHAT WAS COMPARED MATTERS: seven of those compared the id and the per-kind counts, and the eighth compared the job identities the message carries and found the same one assigned job — same run id, same stable workflow-job id, `runnerRequestId` zero on both deliveries.
WHOSE DEADLINE IT WAS decides what an expiry means (`retireDeadlinePending`): the caller's own context ending is the operator stopping the converge and is no pending row, this command's bound is the ledger taking longer than the attempt may, and a deadline NEITHER set is the open's own startup budget — the case an unresponsive connection during the open produces.
Waiting inside the teardown was never the fix, because a node runs one command at a time.
What a default-branch job publishes, every later job of the pool reads, a pull request included, so the namespace is a static repository and an untrusted pool's namespace (`<ns>.scoped/untrusted/…`) is unreachable from a trusted one's and from any guest-chosen key.
What a release publishes.
What admission guarantees is that the host's unit configuration is judged at each distinct retirement step: before each service operation, and before each persistence step (a journal write, a status publication, the stage write, the archive rename, the configuration rewrite, the receipt publication, the completion-ledger preparation and row completion, the acknowledgement, marker clearing, settlement).
What billet may say about a failed launch comes from a status file its own launcher wrote (`launching` before the identity check, `started` before the pid, `command-missing`), never the guest's stdout or stderr, because the registration travels on that delivery's stdin and a guest whose shell is `cat >&2` reflects a credential into a node log. billet reads the status and the pid in one query: `launching` with no pid is conclusive, `started` with no pid is transient once and conclusive on a second observation.
What changed and why, with the failure mode if there is one.
What each build cache did is observed like the image store.
What each module creates.
What each proves is narrower than it looks: `does not exist` about a directory billet just enumerated is tart reading a different store, not a corpse; `missing files` means tart cannot reconstruct the VM, not that a running guest stopped.
What each version added, and whether an older peer is refused or reported.
What escapes it is written down rather than implied: a file falsely marked generated, a dependency reaching `database/sql` under its own name, and `sql.Conn.Raw`.
What holds either way is ownership: this guard carries the journal's marker, and the journal names this host, this deployment (read at the archive) and this holder or one its takeover chain reached.
What holds whichever it was is ordering: the build's last act on the image before step 6 is `chown -R runner:runner /home/runner`, and a test pins that it comes after GitHub's build and step 5.
What is KNOWN AND DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED, by name, with "do not re-report it; DO report anything else it implies that is fixable."
What is NOT covered.
What is best effort: a handshake slot, refused instantly so the node redials.
What is guaranteed: anonymous traffic can never displace an admitted node.
What is steered: one virtual `Clock` that the allocator and every simulated provider read (the plane, the heartbeat and the node loops stay on wall time, because a plane on the simulated clock would expire a node parked across a jump of hours), and the order in which tiers open their sessions and contest freed room (fixed to the fleet's tier order, since escrow is placement and goroutine order would otherwise decide where a tier's first job lands).
What it does not gate is `alloc.Resize`, the remote fallback growing an EXISTING lease to the shape the cloud sold: that is re-authorised against the ceiling and every floor, the order admitted the lease already, and the resize is asked for by the node (the plane's resize route, or the in-process runtime) and the queue is handed only to listeners, so nothing on that path holds it (a wiring fact, not a layering one: `nodeplane` imports `server`) — so a fallback to a larger shape can take pot a waiter was accumulating.
What launchd loaded is not what its plist says. launchd reads a plist once, at bootstrap; `launchctl print` reports the loaded values, so a node can run a stale five-second drain grace while its file is byte-identical to the shipped one.
What made it expensive is that `/usr/bin/command` exists on macOS (an Apple stub, link count 15) and not on Ubuntu, so a gate emitted as `<drop> command -v "$1"` exited 0 here and 127 on the image, refusing every correct artifact.
What makes an answer evidence is the fence: `nodes.dispatch_generation` is bumped durably before a launch enters the queue, under the same hold of `Plane.mu` (`BumpDispatch`), and an observation is recorded only while that number and the epoch are unchanged.
What must run alone is a test sharing process-global state: one SQLite file two tests open, a fixed port, a daemon, the environment (`t.Setenv` refuses in a parallel test), or a package variable one of them mutates.
What needs judgment goes in a skill.
What neither path closes is a restart between the drain's end and the `bootout`: the bootout's SIGTERM is then the new process's first, under launchd's clamped grace.
What pre-1.0 still permits is breaking a non-ledger on-disk format (the recover journal, an archive schema, a channel statement), provided the refusal detects the old shape and says what to do about it.
What releases it is `decommission_proven = 1`, which the drain's compute barrier writes.
What stays open is an operator running `tart delete` by hand.
What still returns, and so still stops every tier, is what the deployment must stop for: a response wrapping `ErrUntrustworthySession`, a lost controller claim (`state.ErrLeadershipLost` or the listener's fence, checked before every close and open, and by `openSession` before every attempt including each wait on a 409), an open that itself answers with either (returned as itself even mid-drain, never collapsed into the cancellation), a misconfigured listener, and every other listener failure (an `Escrow` error, a failed acknowledgement or `AcquireJobs`, which are not yet recovered this way).
What the cache did for a job is recorded as an observation, from a closed vocabulary, first observation kept.
What the classes of thing are, what each is allowed to do, and which fact is authoritative.
When a bug is a class, encode it, in this order.
When a check cannot be built, observe.
When a platform behaviour matters, write a throwaway probe and run it where the code runs.
When any tier has waiting work, the harness nudges every listener, including positive-advertisement donors: a donor parked forever cannot complete the withdrawal that releases its backing.
When newer it runs `images pull --verify` then `images reap --keep 3`; a failed pull reaps nothing; `--dry-run` reports.
When preparation has an empty answerer, no claim and an unstaged Linux candidate, `unverified-check-mode` may preview ordinary work without classification; a real run stages and classifies and can select different work.
When recovery or the sweep proves an orphan destroyed, `forgetRunning` drops it too.
Where the call site cannot be reached from a unit test, assert it structurally with `go/ast` (below).
Where the thing faked is a command a shell script runs, define it as a shell function in the script under test; where a real executable is unavoidable, write it while holding `syscall.ForkLock` (`internal/guestassets`' `writeExecutable`), because syscall's forkExec, the path every `os/exec` start takes, holds that lock while it creates the child, so no such child can copy an open write descriptor (a raw or native fork is not covered).
Which executable answers: the managed binary; when it predates the guard or is absent and a guard exists, the executable the record names after the `guard_fallback` module proved it (the five members plus `id`, `token` and `preparing`, typed when present); on a bootstrap or a pre-R host with a candidate, the STAGED candidate after the staging (`--expect-bootstrap` on a bootstrap).
With `backup.s3` set, `local backup` uploads what it just wrote (never instead), and `local restore --from-backup latest` fetches, verifies and restores on a machine holding only the binary; an `s3://` URL could not replace the config because it carries no region and SigV4 signs one into every request.
With `billet_ledger_volume_id` set to the module's output, the role resolves the volume by its NVMe identity (never a filesystem UUID, which a snapshot clone duplicates), formats only when blank, mounts through a systemd unit with no `nofail`, adds `Requires=` and `RequiresMountsFor=` to `billet-server.service`, proves the state directory is served by the expected volume and refuses to shadow a root-disk ledger.
With an open non-TTY stdin — every background shell — `codex exec` prints "Reading additional input from stdin..." and hangs forever.
With integer casts spelled `BIGINT`, sqlc's two engines emit byte-identical Go differing only in `?N` versus `$N`, and modernc.org/sqlite executes `$N` correctly, so a `$N` constant runs on both and a `?N` constant does not. sqlc's schema is the migration directory itself, so a migration is an input to code generation: run `make sqlc` after adding one, and `sqlc diff` in CI catches forgetting.
With no token each role does nothing, so a play can run them everywhere. cloudflared's token is `base64({"a","s","t"})`, `billet_cloudflared_expected_tunnel_id` is REQUIRED whenever a token is supplied and checked against the `t` before anything is installed, because a token for the other host's tunnel installs cleanly and comes up healthy advertising routes the host cannot serve (measured on the reference deployment), and an empty id would skip that one check by default.
With nothing configured it does nothing, which is what lets the collection's fleet playbook run it on every host in its `control_plane` and `linux` groups.
Within a step, the syscalls a shared primitive performs (temporary files, chmod, sync, lock-file creation) are covered by the step's admission; a unit a root user arms concurrently, while a step runs, is outside the boundary and is detected by the next step's admission.
Without a capable executable it holds.
Without it CocoaPods aborted on the macOS tier ("Unicode Normalization not appropriate for ASCII-8BIT", measured 2026-09-24).
Without that an analyzer could silently stop detecting anything and still report zero violations, which reads exactly like a clean tree.
Without that, a failed mount lets the controller start on the root disk with a new ledger, identity and CA.
Without the bound a hung `systemctl` held `local up` forever, and a cancelled one was KILLed under its own stop job (`internal/lifeops/systemctl_bounds_test.go`).
Without this you get the same accepted limitation every round, crowding out new findings.
Write `//nolint:<linter> // <reason>`. billet's own analyzers use `//billet:ignore <analyzer> // <reason>` with the same three rules: a bare directive is reported, an unused one is reported, and a trailing directive covers only its own line while a directive alone on its line covers the line below.
Write output to a deterministic path keyed to the topic, so a fresh shell can re-derive it after the notification.
Write the failing path as an `if` with an explicit `exit 1` and a message.
You run every gate yourself anyway.
ZFS clone reachable from one machine only; RBD clone mapped from a second kernel client.
`! cmd | grep -q .` under `set -e`: the script continued and exited 0 (`/bin/sh`).
`!` inside an `if` condition is fine, because the condition's status is consumed rather than inherited.
`$TART_HOME/.billet/store.lock` is flocked around the rename that publishes a lease name and the delete that removes one, and deliberately not around the clone or a staging cleanup.
`%+v` on `awscreds.IMDS` printed the secret access key and session token through an unexported field.
`--ack-path` replaces `--ack-fd` (the node launches its own binary, so the two ends share a version).
`--cache` adds the cloud half's store: `sites:` on the controller (the local place is `ceph`, the cloud one `ebs-s3`), `node.site` on each node, and on the commission render `node.ebs_s3` plus a `node.cache` HTTPS listener on the controller's address at the module's cache port — every one of which config validates at load (`node.cache` on EC2 needs `node.ebs_s3`, which needs `node.site`, whose declared store must be `ebs-s3`, and the guest endpoint must be https naming the same address and port).
`--candidate` is a file inside a `recovery-*` direct child of the root, opened relative to the validated root's descriptor (`openat`, `O_NOFOLLOW`), examined on its descriptor, hashed through it, and the name checked against the descriptor afterwards (`guardAfterHash` is the seam a test swaps files under); else the managed binary the same way.
`--dry-run` takes no lock, because taking one creates a file.
`--emit ansible` prints the `billet_config` block instead of writing a file.
`--environment-file` reads the PostgreSQL DSN through `environmentFileValue`'s restricted grammar whenever it is named, on every backend, and the value reaches no argument, no report and no error (pgx redacts the password in its own parse error, measured 2026-09-09).
`--join ADDR` is a transform of the generation (`initconfig.Join`), never a second generator: it drops `server`, `github` and `targets`, moves the measured `server.max_vcpu`/`max_memory` onto `node.max_vcpu`/`max_memory` (unset, the node contributes its whole machine against a ceiling sized for less), names `node.tls` under the config directory's `tls/`, skips the App-identity carry, proves the result with `config.Parse`, and prints the control plane's half; it is detected by presence (an empty `--join "$ADDR"` is refused, not a control plane), refused beside `--emit ansible`, and never replaces a config whose server state holds a live or unreadable deployment identity (`refuseServerRemoval`), because the generated state directory being the same one is exactly the case `refuseIdentityMove` lets through.
`--net-softnet-block=@host` names that gateway without knowing its address (the bridge exists only while a VM runs, and no vmnet preference records it on macOS 27); the longest prefix wins and block beats allow, and with it a guest timed out on both ports, still reached the internet and still renewed its DHCP lease: softnet forwards validated DHCP to the host's `bootpd` ahead of its block rules. softnet 0.18 refuses the alias (0.19 added it), so `billet check` asks the installed binary's `--help` for `@host` and fails an untrusted node without it.
`--no-block` matters because a oneshot's start job lasts the transaction; the node waits only on the socket.
`--note` on `prepare --validate` and on `hold`, at most 200 bytes of printable text (`checkNote`), written at acquisition and never rewritten by a validation, a re-binding, a settlement or a takeover; every reader (`checkGuardRecord`, `guard_fallback.py`'s `OPTIONAL_MEMBERS`, `guard-answer.yml`) admits its absence and refuses a non-string.
`--provider tart` is refused anywhere but Apple Silicon (the ceiling, the node name and the paths all come from the machine running it) and requires `--node-name`, because a stock Mac hostname is not a legal node name and sanitising one would name a host the operator never chose.
`--reservation-fresh` is passed exactly after `reserved`, never after `adopted`.
`--sandbox read-only`, and say "do not build or test" in the prompt.
`--skip-signature-verification` is deliberate.
`.claude/` is excluded because sessions park worktrees there and a pass was linting another branch's half-finished code.
`.codecov.yml`: project target `auto` (no regression from base, 1% threshold), patch target 80% (5% threshold), and only `cmd/billet/main.go` ignored, which is why nothing carrying real semantics may live in that file.
`.gitattributes` marks `scripts/kernel/check-config.sh` `text eol=lf`, because the release gate refuses a copy that does not hash to the pin, and a line-ending conversion on checkout changes every byte.
`.gitattributes` pins the files to LF because a checkout conversion changes every checksum.
`.github/`, the `Makefile`, any `go.mod`/`go.sum`, `sqlc.yaml` and the classifier select everything, and so do a push, a merge commit it cannot read, a mode change, a symlink, a submodule and ANY PATH NO RULE NAMES: an unknown path never selects nothing.
`.github/workflows/cache-conformance.yml` is the matrix it runs: host and container save/restore, BuildKit through container and loopback drivers, the passthrough kill switch, pinned and embedded clients, and a poisoned-clients suite.
`.github/workflows/cancel-superseded.yml` runs on a GitHub-hosted runner on every same-repository PR push, and force-cancels each unfinished CI run on that branch whose head is not the pushed commit.
`/bin/sh` does not stop there: it records the error and carries on down `PATH`, so a fake `df` lost to the real one, whose ample free space made `TestTheFreeSpaceGuardRefusesWhatItCannotRead` accept "not-a-number" (CI run 34827346038, 2026-09-14); `internal/guestassets` failed the same way exec'ing a shim it had just written.
`/opt/hostedtoolcache/.billet-unpublished` must be written by the narrowest question available, because "my query found nothing" is three facts: the vendor published nothing (record it), the vendor published something billet cannot verify (record it), or billet's selector went stale against a rename (fatal).
`/run/billet/registration/current` is written 0600 by the node (root) through the durable installer after every accepted registration; the inspector admits it only when the fstat of the descriptor it then reads says root, 0600, regular and within the bound, never from an `Lstat` beside the read, because a record another account owns or could write names any endpoint and incarnation that account likes, and a foreign file swapped at the name between a lookup and the read would otherwise be judged by the lookup and read as the record.
`/usr/bin/command`: present on macOS (link count 15), absent on Ubuntu; `env -i … command -v sh` exits 0 here and 127 on the image.
`/v1/ca` and `/v1/enroll` must serve a machine with no certificate; while they lived on `server.listen` their connections shared the fleet's budget, and a caller that handshook and idled held a slot until `IdleTimeout` (about 4.3 requests a second emptied 512).
`/v1/register` authenticates before it reads a body.
`/var/lib/billet/node/endpoint-migration.json` is root 0600 in a root 0700 directory whose parent must be a root-owned directory and not a link; the reader (`readEndpointReceipt`) examines the name before the open (a link or a special file is positively not a receipt and is never opened, so a FIFO never waits), opens identity-first without following, requires the owner root and mode 0600, bounds the read at 4096 bytes, and decodes under the exact ten-member set; a failed examination, open, reopen or read is `unreadable` and never absence.
`/var/lib/billet/upgrades/active` is a symlink to the recovery directory (the journal publishes through a rename, so a hard link would go stale), released on commit or rollback and not on cordon, published after the journal (the reverse let a resume clear the claim of a live upgrade).
`/var/lib/billet/upgrades` is omitted from retained directory work.
`/var/lib/billet` is created by the script rather than shipped, so a removal cannot delete the identity and the CA key.
`169.254.170.2` serves the build's role credentials inside a VPC on-demand build.
`;` chain with a failing `sha256sum -c`: exit 0 under dash in `ubuntu:24.04`.
`@verified` resolves to the newest generation proved to boot, intersected with the generations that still exist, contract-relative (`NewestVerifiedForContract`), so a fleet takes up a new image with no config edit and rollback is `images unpromote`.
`ACTIONS_RESULTS_URL` carries artifact metadata as well as cache traffic, so interception terminates TLS only for that host and handles only three CacheService methods; a mistake there breaks a deploy.
`AMIContract` is the analogue of `GuestContract`; the tag is a promotion added by `CreateTags` after billet booted the image, and contract 2 means the toolcache GitHub's declaration names with the variables that make it findable.
`Accepts` and the flag builder are one function in tart, because written as two a mechanism admitted and not applied boots untrusted work on the trusted bridge.
`Accepts` is asked before anything expensive.
`Acquire::Retries` retries the failing URI and the timeout is per read, not per download.
`AcquireJobs` is one-way; there is no decline.
`AdvertiseNothing` and `WithHurry` are the server options a dry run and a hurried stop use.
`Allocator.Escrow` reserves against the global ledger first (vCPU, memory, per-tier concurrency, macOS licence slots), and the headroom check and the insert are one transaction: measured, moving the check outside produced 28 grants against a ceiling of 4.
`App` redacts on every rendering path (`String`, `GoString`, `Format`, `MarshalJSON`, `LogValue`, value receivers).
`BILLET_RETIREMENT_SHARD` splits the namespace caller workload into `parser`, `routes`, `compatibility`, `retained`, `recovery`, `settled`, `parity-basic`, `parity-network`, `parity-negative` and `resume` with `ONLY=retirement` and requests skipped, plus `request-evidence`, `request-collection`, `request-windows`, `request-cancellation` and `request-retained` with `ONLY=retirement-request`.
`BILLET_SKIP_ACTIVE_BUILD_GUARD=1` is the operator asserting the fleet was drained.
`BILLET_TC_ARCH` is required, because an unset one defaulting to x64 builds an x64 toolcache onto an arm64 image where nothing fails until a job execs a binary.
`BILLET_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN` gates `internal/state` and `internal/alloc`; `cmd/billet/localbackup_test.go` fails rather than skips when `CI` is set and the DSN is missing.
`BILLET_TEST_STAGED=staged run "case"` is fine for a command and, for a function, leaves the variable set for every later case in some shells (POSIX leaves it unspecified; measured 2026-09-06: the connector gates' serial case ran the previous case's play, and the staged allowance leaked into every later refusal, so a refusal that wrote a file would have passed).
`BilletCacheCloneSource` grants it on `arn:<partition>:ec2:*::snapshot/*` conditioned on the owner tag.
`Bootstrap failed: 5: Input/output error` means already loaded, still draining or disabled alike; diagnose with `print` and `print-disabled`.
`CanGrow` errs towards true where the model is uncertain, because a tier wrongly excluded is starved while one wrongly included only waits its turn, and it is three questions in order.
`CapabilityBoundingSet` is the full set on the node.
`CapacityReport` joins that observation to still-open ledger rows, reports unclassified capacity as unknown, and separates pending, launching, idle, running, cleanup, configured floors and additional headroom.
`ClaimController` records the epoch after its own transaction commits; `checkLeadership` re-reads `controller_claim` on every later `Tx` before `fn` runs and returns `ErrLeadershipLost` if it moved.
`ClientToken` is durable.
`CommandDestroy` is addressed by request id because it must work for compute whose lease is already gone.
`CommandInventory` is asked, not waited for.
`CommandUpgrade` returns the instant the detached updater starts, because an inline upgrade would hold the slot for the whole drain.
`CommandUpgrade` sends an exact version, `--manifest-sha256`, `RolloutID` and `Generation`; `node.upgradeArgs` is a function so a test can see all four reach argv (a review found three of the four built and dropped while a test at the interface passed).
`ConditionResult` is never a proof input.
`CreateSnapshot` + `ClientToken`: `UnknownParameter` (HTTP 400), every settlement failed, every job ran cold (2026-09-03).
`CreateSnapshot` takes no `ClientToken` (`UnknownParameter`); the token travels as the `sh.billet.snapshot-token` tag.
`DB.Reader()` returns a narrow `Querier`, never `*sql.DB`.
`DB.Tx` begins IMMEDIATE and holds SQLite's single writer slot from BEGIN, so a network call inside a transaction stalls every scheduling write.
`DecodeSettledVerdict` keeps the purposes distinct; `DecodeSettledRefusal` admits only its refusal branch and matching exit semantics.
`DefaultMacOSVMLimit` is 2, pinned to Virtualization.framework's own refusal of a third guest rather than to a licence reading; `NodePolicy.MacOSLimit()` answers it for a host nothing was declared about, and the default is keyed on `RunsOnHost` because a CodeBuild `MAC_ARM` fleet runs under AWS's agreement (left alone it capped a five-instance fleet at two and blamed Apple).
`DeleteMessage` acknowledges a notification and does not decline a job; `AcquireJobs` is one-way with no decline or release, which is why a promise to GitHub cannot be revoked by a local timer (`billet-capacity`).
`DeleteProject` succeeds during a live build; the build runs to completion and `BatchGetBuilds` keeps answering for it.
`DeleteProject` succeeds under a live build; the build runs on.
`DeleteProject` succeeds while a build is in its `BUILD` phase (measured 2026-09-02); `refuse-active-builds.sh` walks the project's builds through the operator's `aws` CLI as a destroy-time provisioner, pins `TZ=UTC`, and never calls `StopBuild`.
`ErrNoSuchObject` is S3's `NoSuchKey` and nothing else: every 404 used to come back under that name, so a bucket that does not exist reached a restore as "no archive here" on the one day the machine is new and the operator has nothing but the binary — the fix is one line of config and the diagnostic was pointing at their backups (`internal/awss3`, and `billet-providers-aws` for the measurement).
`ErrSchemaAhead` is the typed ahead-schema refusal `refuseUnknownVersions` now wraps, so a retiring host at R beside a survivor that migrated to R+1 maps it to `pending` rather than refusing.
`ErrSchemaAhead`, `ErrSchemaBehind` and `ErrReleaseBehind` are the other half of a retirement tail's pending list — a ledger that answered and said something this binary may not write — and everything else refuses.
`ExecStart=+/usr/bin/billet …` runs with full privileges whatever `User=` says, and `-p ExecStart` is byte-identical with and without the `+`.
`ExecUpgrader.AckDir` is the node's private writable state directory, wired from `cfg.Node.StateDir`; `StartUpgrade` listens at `upgrade-ack-<random>` and closes the listener on every return, which unlinks the socket.
`ExecUpgrader.Check` runs at node startup and in its candidate probe, refusing an absolute state-directory path whose generated socket name exceeds 107 bytes on Linux or 103 on macOS (measured with Go `ListenUnix`, 2026-09-06).
`Execute` leaves a recovery fenced (`Result.Unfinished`), the command seals through `state.OpenMaintenance` (the one typed fence crossing), and `deployarchive.Finish` lifts the fence afterwards, under one acquisition of the directory lock, asking `state.PeekAdmission` (no lock, no migration, no fence) whether an operator seal is in place and refusing a journal still at `publishing`.
`Find` prefers the single live match, refuses two, and returns the newest terminal only when nothing runs.
`Finish` proves the seal rather than documenting it; before that the two tests named for the invariant demonstrated it did not hold.
`Finish` returns `ErrOutstanding` and the coordinator suppresses only that.
`Hold.Admit` is the ordinary writers' gate and refuses a closed status; the status a transition publishes is its own, and the transition is the one writer it allows, because it holds the host's transaction lock and this converge's guard, which no ordinary writer does.
`Holding()` counts `running` as well as custody and `launching`, and a drain ends only when all three are empty.
`Inputs.Build` once emitted the runtime statements unconditionally, so a controller that launches nothing held `ec2:RunInstances` (hence `NoCompute`), and the terraform module hand-wrote the grant until `internal/tfpolicy`'s drift test began reading the generator's rendering.
`Installation.PermissionMismatches` reports both directions and `billet check` (so `billet local up`) refuses on either: a missing permission breaks runner registration later with an error that never mentions permissions, and an extra one falsifies the credential-isolation claim.
`InvalidateBarrierRun` reads before it writes, because it runs ahead of the revocation check and a revoked credential could otherwise reserve the writer slot on every request.
`Job.JobID` (GitHub's workflow-job id, empty for a pooled launch) travels plane to node and needs no gate, because the node decodes leniently and an older one ignores it.
`JobStarted` logs run, event, owner, repository and workflow_ref, the evidence the rule was measured against.
`Limits.Shares` (from `config.Config.TargetShares`, passed at every `alloc.Limits` the CLI builds) caps what one target's tiers hold together.
`ListBuildsForProject` has no status filter, keeps a year, returns 100 ids a page and errors if `sortOrder` is passed above 100 builds.
`ListExpiredLeases` selects `chosen_provider` because the reaper archives from that projection; before it did, every reaped lease was archived as having run on nothing.
`List` and `Find` are a bounded page walk, bounded by CodeBuild's own enforced ceilings (`timeoutInMinutes + queuedTimeoutInMinutes + slack`).
`List` and `Find` verify both, and an owner-marked build whose lease marker names no lease fails the whole inventory, because this list frees capacity.
`List` cross-checks tart's JSON against the vms directory and asks `tart get` about each absence.
`List` errors rather than answering short.
`Listener.heartbeatLock` is the seam a test stands in.
`LoadServing` is one call rather than four walks so a retire cannot land between reads and produce a plane presenting a retired authority while trusting only the new one, the one failure here that is not fail-closed; it also re-reads `ca.crt` at the end and starts over if it moved (`servingReadAttempts`), because a whole rotate-and-retire can pass between two reads.
`LockDeployment` excludes a second process on the same deployment identity (a copied state directory locks happily, because a copy is a different inode); failing to place it is an error rather than a downgrade (`allow_unlocked_deployment` is the explicit opt-in), it never lives in a cache directory (unlinking a held lock file detaches the path from the inode and the next process locks a fresh file), a shared `lock_dir` must be setgid and the lock's gid must match the directory's, and it is claimed before `state.Open` or a process about to be refused first migrates the ledger.
`LookupRunnerGroup` exists so the live measurement records the service's answer rather than a fake's.
`MinMacOSGuestMemory` is 4GiB because the framework answers `LessThanMinimalResourcesError` below it and `provider.Spec` carries no guest OS, so config is the only layer that can hold the rule.
`MinVersion` is a promise about meaning, not about whether fields parse.
`Names=` shows an alias only once its link exists.
`NeedDaemonReload` IS REPORTED AS A FACT (`need_daemon_reload`) AND IS NOT PART OF THE SHAPE, because on systemd 255 it answers yes when this unit's fragment, source or drop-ins changed since load OR when the manager's flag `unit_file_state_outdated` is set, and the second cause dominates in practice: the flag is set by any bus unit-file operation that changed something (`EnableUnitFiles`, `DisableUnitFiles`, `PresetUnitFiles`, `MaskUnitFiles`, `LinkUnitFiles`, `RevertUnitFiles`, `AddDependencyUnitFiles`, so every `systemctl enable` a snap refresh, a package or the role itself performs) and cleared only by `daemon-reload`, and while it is set EVERY unit answers yes whatever its own file's state; measured on the reference controller on 2026-09-07 (systemd 255.4): 464 of 464 units after snapd enabled a new mount unit, billet's unit files unchanged since the last reload.
`NeedsRunEvidence`/`TargetNeedsRunEvidence` say which targets' Apps need `actions: read`.
`NewRunnerGroupPolicyClientAt` is the one constructor: it builds an `*http.Client` and transport of its own (dial, TLS-handshake, response-header and overall bounds, the same HTTP/2 health check as the scale-set client from #205), never `http.DefaultClient`, whose transport is process-wide and has no timeout.
`Nodes` are the hosts an empty fleet could place the tier's SHAPE on, not every host the policy would consider, or a waiter would block tiers a host it cannot use can really serve.
`ONLY=retirement` alone still runs both halves; the default runs every section.
`O_RDWR` on a `0444` kernel: permission denied; chmod and fsync through a read-only descriptor succeed; a no-op chmod on a read-only mount: EROFS.
`OnFailureJobMode` is `replace` and the `*Action` settings are `none` on the packaged units, so "refuse if non-empty" refuses every correct host.
`OpenAdmin` is an operator command: it proceeds without the lock when a plane holds it (the lock stops two control planes, not two processes), still takes it when free (a fresh install runs `ca issue` before any server), and when it cannot take it verifies the schema instead of migrating, returning `ErrSchemaBehind` naming which side to restart, then re-verifies inside every transaction.
`OpenInspect` and `OpenPostgresInspect` (`inspect.go`) are the fourth mode, a construction path of their own and never a flag on the admin one: they validate everything an open validates (the migration set readable first, the schema exactly the binary's with an interior hole or an edited early checksum refused by name, the fence, the watermark, the binding through the caller's `verifyLedgerIdentity`) and mutate nothing (no `MkdirAll`, no `Chmod`, no directory lock, no integrity scan, no claim, no migration, no watermark write), on SQLite through `mode=ro` plus `query_only` on both pools and never `immutable=1`, on PostgreSQL through `default_transaction_read_only=on` on both pools with the durability check told not to refuse its own read-only writer; `Tx` answers `ErrInspect` before any transaction begins and so does `ClaimController`, before the backend's advisory lock is asked for; an absent ledger is `ErrNoLedger` from an `Lstat` and never a created file; the read-transaction revalidation of an unlocked handle is kept, so a version written after the open refuses the next `View`, and an inspection's `View` re-reads the release watermark inside its transaction too (`checkReleaseWatermarkIn`), so a newer release that claimed the same-schema ledger after the report's open refuses the next read as it refuses a fresh open.
`OpenMaintenance` is the one typed entry that crosses the maintenance fence (`billet.maintenance`), used by the host-upgrade probe and by `local recover`'s seal; `OpenAdmin` honours the fence.
`OpenPostgresCompletion` writes one row and is not a control plane.
`OpenPostgresProbe` is the standby's open with the fence bypass: verify-not-ahead, no claim, no migration, every `Tx` refused, for the host transaction's probe on an external ledger.
`OpenPostgresStandby` holds no exclusion and refuses every `Tx` with `ErrStandby` until `ClaimController` succeeds, because the epoch fence protects a controller that was replaced and does nothing for one that never claimed.
`Open` is the control plane: it takes the exclusive directory lock (`billet.lock`, a flock so a crash releases it) and migrates.
`POST /v1/nodes/{node}/leases/{lease}/usage` (`UsageRequest`: an `alloc.JobUsage` summary and an optional `alloc.UsageSeries` blob bounded at 512 KiB so the report fits the 1 MiB body) goes through `forOwnLease`, is validated at the boundary and fenced on the epoch by `alloc.RecordLeaseUsage`; `nodeclient.Client.RecordLeaseUsage` sends it only on 24 and treats an older plane as success.
`ParseCertificates` reads every `CERTIFICATE` block of a bundle's CA file in order, because a node mid-rotation legitimately holds a predecessor beside the current authority, and it follows the TLS loader's line rule rather than being more forgiving: a BEGIN marker counts only at the start of the text or after a newline (Go's `pem.Decode` skips an indented one, so the loader's pool would not hold that certificate and the report must not say it does), an END marker must end its line, trailing spaces or tabs allowed as Go allows them (two blocks glued together are a malformed boundary, not two certificates), a malformed block is refused rather than skipped, and only whole blank lines are permitted around and between blocks.
`PeekLedger`, `PeekAdmission`, `PeekMigrations` and `PeekDeploymentID` read without a lock, a migration or the fence, for callers that hold the lock already.
`Plane.ArrivingForRegistration` discards the host's stored run before a registration is judged, on both wiring paths, before the body is decoded and before revocation is checked, because a permanently refused registration is still an authenticated host reporting live compute.
`Plane.ArrivingForRegistration` runs first on both paths (`Plane.Register` for in-process wiring and `handler.register`, which assembles the sequence itself), before the body is decoded and before revocation is checked, on the certificate's own name (`certificateName` reads the verified chain without the revocation check).
`Process.Release` filled the process table one refused updater at a time.
`ProviderKind.RunsOnHost` is the one reader of that distinction and is keyed on the host backends, so a second remote backend nobody remembers to add is treated as remote.
`PublishDefault` needs the default branch and an event in GitHub's writing set (`push`, `schedule`, `workflow_dispatch`, `repository_dispatch`, `delete`, `registry_package`, `page_build`; GitHub changelog, 2026-06-26, pinned both ways by a test).
`READY=1` is sent before the wait or systemd kills the standby at `TimeoutStartSec`.
`ReadOps` and `WriteOps` are hand-written on purpose. sqlc emits one `*Queries` carrying every method; binding that to the reader would turn the compile-time read/write split into a runtime one.
`ReadQueries` returns `ReadOps` through `readOnlyDBTX`, whose `ExecContext`/`PrepareContext` refuse; the generated `DBTX` demands `PrepareContext` even under `emit_prepared_queries: false`, so `Querier` stays two methods and is adapted.
`ReadRetirementIn` serves `rollout.Store.StatusSnapshot`, so `rollout status --json` reports the row (`retirement`, null when none) from the same read transaction as the binding.
`ReadString` returns bytes together with the error, so `accepted` without a newline is not an acceptance.
`Recover` likewise only closes the sessions of compute the inventory proves absent (`ReconcileInventory`), and a failure there is a warning, never a reason to refuse work.
`Recover` runs at every registration, not only at start, so what it finds includes this process's own jobs (#227).
`RefuseUnknownVersions` is the one cold reader (the restore planner calls it before any ledger is open), so it calls `sqliteTimeline.require()` itself; ungated it answered from an empty set and accepted an archive whose applied set was empty.
`RegisterRequest.Incarnation` is a fresh random value per node process, carried on every request as the `Billet-Incarnation` header (`HeaderIncarnation`) because some requests have no body; it distinguishes a restart from a duplicate and routes new commands to the newest registration while a superseded process may still maintain and report the work it holds, because a draining process has to outlive its replacement.
`Release` hands back the identity artefacts AND the ledger artefacts, because a ledger open made before an installer published the record found no account at the time.
`RenewalDue` measures a leaf from its issue, not from its `NotBefore`: `leafTemplate` backdates `NotBefore` by `ClockSkew` (an hour), and counting that hour as life made a twenty-minute leaf look eighty minutes long and due the moment it was issued, so a rehearsal's nodes renewed onto the old authority before the rotation (found in review, 2026-09-04).
`ResolveQuarantineFor` settles from a fresh observation; a first version settled a completion from the plane's cached inventory snapshot, which has no ordering against the quarantine and would free capacity under a running build.
`Rotate` and `Retire` take `LockAuthority` themselves.
`Rotate` refuses if either previous file already exists, with two different messages, because `ca retire` is gated on the certificate and says "no rotation is running" when only a key is left; billet does not remove that key but does say, from having read both, whether it is a byte-identical copy of the installed `ca.key`.
`RunInstances` evaluates a snapshot a block-device mapping NAMES, and names it account-less in the refusal; the launch was still allowed with the AMI's own untagged backing snapshot, for the one image and request measured (EC2 itself, `--dry-run`, 2026-09-04).
`Runner.Holding` counts custody, launches and running entries, and a running entry is removed only by a Destroy the plane sends after GitHub reports the job over; a guest whose VMM ended with no such report (a crash, an operator's kill, a runner that never took a job) kept a draining node out of service on 2026-09-30 (#287).
`SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT` (517) appeared the moment operator commands were admitted alongside the plane, with deferred transactions.
`ScaleSets` reads through `View` for the same reason.
`SendCtrlAltDel`: ignored by a real guest for twenty seconds.
`SetReleaseWatermark` is the one write that lowers it, allowed on a maintenance handle and, on PostgreSQL where that handle is a read-only probe, on an admin handle.
`SettleCompleted` (called from `Runner.DestroyCompleted` with the authority) records a durable `publishIntent` on each dirty attachment and never waits behind a session already `closing`; `cleanupSession` in the cache loop runs `publishDeferred`/`releaseCASVolume` before any discard, through the phases snapshotting, snapshotted, publishing, published, abandoned, bounded by `publishWindow` (30 minutes, the writer's wait included).
`StartBuild` has no field that becomes a tag; the boundary is a per-deployment-and-node tagged project plus `BILLET_OWNER` and `BILLET_INSTANCE_NAME` environment overrides read back through `BatchGetBuilds`.
`StartBuild` idempotency: five minutes; same token same id; changed parameter refused.
`StateDirectory=` and `RuntimeDirectory=` are LISTS, and `show` renders one as its entries separated by spaces (`RuntimeDirectory=billet/locks billet/registration` on the node unit, measured 2026-09-09): `lifeops` admits a configured directory that is one entry, whole, and refuses the joined text, a prefix of an entry and the entries' parent; a comparison against the rendered value as one path refused every packaged node the day the unit gained its second entry.
`StateDirectory=` repairs ownership recursively only when the top directory's owner is wrong, so a root-run `billet check` leaves `billet.db` and `billet.lock` root-owned under a correct directory.
`StopAndProve` reports `Gone: Yes, How: "not-found"`; `Disable` returns without an operation.
`StopResult.Asked` says a drain was requested even when its end was not proved, so `local down` reports the unit as touched rather than claiming nothing was stopped.
`Store.ReleaseWriter` gives a lease back on every failure between acquisition and the pointer advance, on both backends.
`String`, `GoString`, `Format`, `MarshalJSON` and `LogValue`, because each ignores the others: slog's JSON handler never consults `fmt`, `%#v` never consults `String`, and a pointer-receiver `String` is not consulted when a value is formatted.
`TF_MODULES` is discovered by `find`, because a listed module let two siblings go green through the whole suite without ever being validated; `tf-modules-check` refuses an empty or incomplete list (a `.tf.json`-only module would otherwise be skipped in silence).
`TerminateInstances` returns when the request is accepted.
`TestAHealthyUpgradeRunsInOrder` asserts the whole sequence, because the failure mode is a step moving.
`TestAPullDoesNotPublishAGenerationBeforeTheKernelIsDurable` fails each step in turn and asserts `ImportGeneration` was never reached.
`TestConcurrentReservationsNeverOvercommit` is the guard.
`TestEveryPostgresMigrationIsItsSQLiteTwinTranslated` re-derives four declared substitutions and compares statement bytes both ways, lexically aware rather than by regexp (a global replacement would rewrite `SET kind = 'INTEGER'` and bless it).
`TestImportGenerationConfirmsRemovalAfterCallerAndRemovalDeadlinesExpire` set one 20ms knob for two opposite purposes and produced two distinct CI failures under a 30ms stall.
`TestMigrationVersionsAreDenseFromOne` asserts the whole property; the weaker "above the published maximum" was vacuous in every green tree and permitted the gap, measured.
`TestRealSystemdRetiredConditions`, nested in the existing operation-effects witness, is pinned to systemd 255 in `host-lifecycle`'s policy group and records the typed `a(sbbsi)` rendering; each activation mechanism has independent units, fresh condition timestamps and an executable marker-absent counterfactual; implementation-time tests and measurements have not been run.
`TestRealSystemdRetirementSettledEntryObservations` forwards only requested real activity/PID/job/invocation/reload properties from isolated sleep-service units into the settled command fixture.

`TestStopAndProveOutlastsTheClampedExitTimeout` (`BILLET_LAUNCHD_LONG_DRAIN=1`) is the real-launchd witness.
`TestTheAllowlistTableNamesEveryRawStatement` compares the two in both directions.

`TestTheReleaseInspectFixturesAreTheCommandsOwn` will report the added envelope bytes.
