`Tier.EffectiveCache` turns the Git, Bazel and Go caches on for a Linux-only Firecracker tier (`servesGuestCaches`), the Actions cache where `actionsByDefault` holds, and the Docker store and sticky disks everywhere; Go test results stay off.
`Tier.NeedsCacheAwareNode` is the one answer to whether an older node would exceed the tier, reads included: every `default-branch` tier does, because an older node would read the pool's wider pre-#226 keys.
`TierAdmission.TargetShared` makes one target's share a pot like `CeilingShared` (siblings pinned to different hosts compete), and `ShareBound` says the share, measured at the cheapest charged shape rather than the request, is what stops the tier now.
`TimeoutStopSec=88200` is not sized from `drain_timeout` (a drain has no bound); a SIGKILL mid-drain loses billet's bookkeeping, not the jobs, because the guests keep running and the next process re-adopts them.
`TrustUnknown` is refused as malformed.
`Type=exec` returns from `start` as soon as `execve` succeeds.
`UnitsLoadFinishTimestamp` is the boot-time load and is not moved by a reload, so there is no manager property that dates the last reload.
`UnitsLoadFinishTimestamp` is the boot-time load and no reload moves it, so nothing dates the last reload.
`VACUUM INTO` is the ledger mechanism and its constraints were measured: it cannot run in a transaction, is refused on the reader pool, refuses an existing destination (free no-clobber), creates the file 0644 (corrected), and holds the single writer slot while it runs; it is a consistent snapshot of a live database, so no `-wal` travels.
`VACUUM INTO`: refused in a transaction, refused on the query-only pool, refuses an existing destination, creates 0644.
`WithCredentials((*awscreds.IMDS)(nil))` passes `== nil`; `isNilValue` checks the underlying kind.
`WithJobAccounting` (what `node.monitoring` passes) adds `memory.max=max` and `io.weight=default 100` only for a controller `probeAccounting` proved at construction, because the jailer refuses a launch whose key names a file the kernel lacks, and `io.weight` exists only with blk-iocost; the proof for io is `io.weight` in a child that already has io enabled.
`WithOperationUnitDirectories` supplies the persistent destination and all inspected roots.
`WithdrawRequest` is an empty body on purpose.
`WriterBarrier` proves a transaction that began before the fence has finished.
`^`-anchored exclusion paths: 612 findings resurfaced in a second checkout because the cache is content-keyed.
`acquired` IS THE FIRST CALL'S OUTCOME ALONE and the cleanup token is taken from that acquisition and never replaced, because a second answer saying `acquired` with another token would have replaced it and the settlement and the rescue would then have been refused with a token that was never this guard's, leaving the guard behind (round 12).
`actions/actions_test.go`, `siblingrefs_test.go`, `scripts/cache_conformance_cached_test.go`; the live matrix in `.github/workflows/cache-conformance.yml`.
`actions/converge-fleet/prove-idempotent.sh` streams the second pass through `tee` for the log and reads back only the lines after `PLAY RECAP` of the form `<host> : key=N ...`, because a YAML task result above them can carry `changed=1` inside a string; a row is split on the literal ` : ` and its counters on `=`, and a hostname is compared as a literal string (`node.a` is not `node-a`, which a regex would accept).
`actions/converge-fleet` is the consumer's one pin, and the collection it runs is the checkout it runs from.
`actions/convergefleet_test.go` (credentials 0600 and exported, environment lines never in argv, pins appended, `ssh-keyscan` never run, cleanup scoped to the run's marker).
`actions/convergefleet_test.go`: the action's scripts against fakes on PATH (`ansible-playbook`, `ansible`, `ansible-galaxy`, `nc`, `warp-cli`, `ssh-keyscan`, `sleep`), every refusal by its message and by what was not called, and the pin files against `ci.yml`.
`actions/runner` history: v2.285.3 published 2023-01-30, after v2.301.1 on 2023-01-19; one releases page is ~5MB and reaches back five years, so the walk bound is two pages.
`actions/stickydisk` mounts a copy-on-write ext4 volume for one job (`key`, `path`, `size-gb`, `publication: cas | last-write-wins`, `discard-marker`, output `cache-hit`) and publishes in a post step without changing the job result.
`actions/stickydisk`, `setup-docker-builder`, `stop-docker-builder` and `build-push-action` are the published actions.
`active` a symlink is a Go transaction, a regular file a pre-R role transaction, a DIRECTORY holding `guard.json` (holder, claimed_at, hostname, release_executable, release_executable_sha256) a converge guard, a directory without the record an `unpublished-guard`; `classifyClaim` reads it by `Lstat` with no lock and creates nothing, and a directory was chosen because every pre-R reader refuses one and none can release it.
`alloc.BuildCache` (`warm`, `cold`, `disabled`, `unavailable`, `unused`) for sticky disks, Git, Bazel and Go (migration 55), kept per session at the most telling outcome (`noteBuildCache`; CAS hits and uses are atomics on the volume, for the lock order) and reported once, when the session ends (`settledBuildCaches`), `unused` only for a tier that enabled the cache and only from the process that saw the whole session.
`alloc.ImageCache` (`warm` with the generation, `cold`, `unavailable`, `unused`) is what the guest's Docker image-store clone answered, observed in `attachDockerStore`; `alloc.ActionsCache` (`served`, `spliced`, `disabled`, `unavailable`, `off`, `unused`) is what interception did for the FIRST CacheService call, recorded where the disposition is FINAL: `actionsResponse` records only what it decides itself (the kill switch, a client billet does not serve), and `actionsProxy.respond` records `served` once the handler answered, `spliced` when a failed handler is retried through GitHub, and `unavailable` when a reservation-bound call failed and could not go upstream; blob legs and artifact traffic observe nothing.
`alloc.New` is exported, so it cannot assume its catalog came through `config.Load`; a rule enforced in only one of the two has a second entry point that does not enforce it.
`alloc.NodeWithdrawn` writes `live = 0` fenced on epoch and incarnation, releases nothing, marks no disruption and discards no barrier run; the plane writes the ledger first and drops the node from memory second.
`alloc.Quiescence` answers from the ledger and cannot see compute whose lease has already gone (an in-memory destroy obligation, a launch whose lease was reclaimed); both leave an instance carrying billet's name on the host's provider.
`analyze-types: true` so an import alias does not evade a ban.
`ansible_collections/junioryono/billet/tests/*` (the scenario playbooks and shell checks), `scripts/check-module-sources.sh`.
`ansible_collections/junioryono/billet` holds the `host` role (a Linux control plane and Firecracker compute host), `ssh_access` (the keys a converge connects with and sshd hardened only once they leave a way in), `cloudflared_connector` and `warp_connector` (the host halves of Routes C and D below) and `development_host` (a developer machine beside the runners), with examples under `examples/single-host-docker` and `examples/firecracker-host`.
`arn:<p>:ec2:*::snapshot/*` does not match an account-qualified snapshot ARN and `arn:<p>:ec2:*:*:snapshot/*` matches both spellings (`iam:SimulateCustomPolicy`, not an EC2 observation).
`awspolicy` is one generator with three consumers and a measured boundary.
`billet ami build` launches the produced image, reads its report through the console (`GetConsoleOutput`, nonce-bound, no key pair, no inbound access), and only then writes `AMIContract` with `CreateTags`; `ErrPromotionUncertain` is the third value for a failure after the tag.
`billet ami build` takes the id from `--deployment` or the config's state directory and SAYS on stderr when it has neither, because the account-wide value it then stamps is one a value-scoped grant denies at `RunInstances` with nothing naming the reason.
`billet ca issue --lifetime` (`wirecert.CA.IssueNodeFor`; bounded in wirecert to [`MinIssuedLifetime` = 20m, `LeafLifetime`], because a node renews on a five-minute sweep once a third of the life remains, so the final third has to outlast a sweep; ten minutes, the first floor chosen, left a three-minute window) issues a short leaf for a short-lived host or a rotation rehearsal; renewals and the control plane's own certificate keep `LeafLifetime`.
`billet ca issue` hands out the trust bundle, not only the issuer, because during an overlap the new authority issues and the old one is presented.
`billet ca issue` records the admission as `issued` so `billet nodes pending --all` is the one answer to what was let in.
`billet ca rotate` has the new authority issue node certificates while the old one still signs what the control plane presents and both are trusted; nodes adopt the new one through ordinary renewal; `billet ca retire` drops the old one once the fleet has moved.
`billet ca show` warns once that starts; it does not report whether a rotation is running.
`billet cache credential-helper` answers the bearer from the environment only for the node's host, so no bazelrc carries it.
`billet cache enable|disable --org|--repository [--kind docker|sticky|actions|git|bazel|go|all]` writes `cache_blocks(kind, …)` (migration 54; `'*'` is every cache, and a block an older binary wrote was carried as `actions`); nodes read it over `GET /v1/nodes/{node}/cache-policy?kind=` (`CachePolicy.CacheAllowed`), where could-not-tell is refusal.
`billet cache gocacheprog` (`internal/gocacheprog`) speaks cmd/go's cacheprog protocol, keeps a local directory for DiskPaths, re-fetches a damaged local output, keeps a served object only when its bytes are its entry's, and turns into a plain local cache on any refusal: a build never fails because of it.
`billet cache orphans` (`cmd/billet/cacheorphans.go`) lists them and `--reclaim` moves them with `rbd trash mv` for `PurgeTrash` to delete; `ceph.Client.ReclaimOrphans` (`internal/store/ceph/orphans.go`) decides, oldest first, and an image qualifies only when ALL of these hold: an exact writable-volume name (`cacheImageName` kind `v`; a generation is never a candidate), named at least `--older-than` ago (`DefaultOrphanAge` six days, past the five days GitHub documents for a self-hosted job, floor `OrphanMinimumAge` 24 hours) AND created that long ago by the cluster's clock (`rbd info`'s `create_timestamp`, which the OSD sets in `cls_rbd` create and rbd prints with ctime in the local zone, read from the v19.2.2 source; the name carries the creating node's clock, which may be behind) both by this node's clock and against `clusterNow`, the latest `create_timestamp` among the eight newest-named images (a lower bound on the cluster's clock that no node's clock enters, the latest rather than the first because a name's order is its creator's clock; the same two clocks judge `used_at`).
`billet cache status` counts them per tier.
`billet check` always answered it (`github.VerifyAppAt`); `explainGitHubAccess` now asks after a failure, never replaces the original error (asserted by prefix as well as `errors.Is`), never claims to have found the cause, and separates an unreachable GitHub from a refused credential.
`billet check` proves the key works (regular file, no group/other bits, bounded read, parsed, through one `O_NONBLOCK` descriptor).
`billet check` refuses such a cluster.
`billet check` reports an unstamped image as needing a rebuild.
`billet check` reports the newest archive's age because a timer that stopped firing looks like one that works.
`billet fleet converge` (`cmd/billet/fleet.go`) is the same implementation from an operator's machine: it fetches the release's checkout (this binary's version, or `-ref`; a development build must name one) into the user cache directory once, behind a marker written last, and runs the action's own `prepare.sh`, `install-ansible.sh` and `converge.sh`, then always `release-guard.sh` and `cleanup.sh`, with a private `RUNNER_TEMP`, emulating a runner's `GITHUB_ENV` and `GITHUB_PATH` between steps and passing the secrets to `converge.sh` alone.
`billet github-app create --config` edits five scalars under `github:` in place, preserving comments, mode and owner, because the App identity is the one thing no generator can merge.
`billet host-upgrade` is a separate detached program with everything on disk.
`billet images refresh` (`cmd/billet/imagesrefresh.go`, run daily by `billet-images-refresh.timer` or the Mac's `sh.billet.images` agent) resolves the channel manifest through `resolveImageManifest` (the network half of a pull, factored out so nothing is downloaded to answer), and for each configured firecracker image compares `manifest.BuiltAt` with `NewestGeneration(...).Built`: a generation is named for its import time, always after the build it came from, so newest-older-than-built proves a newer image and needs no new Ceph metadata.
`billet init --provider tart` still chooses one preferred Xcode shape as its default, but gives every Linux rung the same whole usable ceiling.
`billet init --repository` refuses `--runner-group`/`--workflow` (a repository has no pool) and refuses the docker backend (it admits only trusted work), each by name, before the generic docker-needs-a-policy answer can send an operator to create a runner group GitHub has nowhere to put.
`billet init hybrid --out DIR` (`internal/initconfig/hybrid.go`, `cmd/billet/inithybrid.go`) never touches `/etc/billet`: it writes a Terraform root, an inventory with both hosts, `site.yml`, `requirements.yml` and `RUNBOOK.md` into a directory, replacing a file only when its first line carries `HybridMarker` and writing `<file>.new` beside an operator's own.
`billet init hybrid` and both examples render `- import_playbook: junioryono.billet.fleet`; a consumer's own plays go after it, and a play CI must never run belongs in another file.
`billet init` appends a commented `release:` block stating the default and the two lines that change it (`initconfig.releaseBlock`).
`billet init` generates a whole file, so it replaces one only where `initconfig.PlanReRun` proves the bytes are its own output (or under `--force`) and otherwise writes `<path>.new`.
`billet init` refuses what it cannot measure.
`billet leases failures` shows both side by side and says the pairing is circumstantial.
`billet local prepare` (root, Linux) is `retirement.Bootstrap`: init lock, the identity directory created ONLY when the service-account record, the global lock and the status are all positively absent beside it (`metadataAbsent`; an absent directory beside any of them is a retirement's move or damage and is left absent, reported as `IdentityDirAbsent` and, in the JSON answer, `identity_dir_absent`), the global lock created (`Hold.Created` says whether), the status read (unreadable OR malformed refuses through `admitBootstrapStatus`; a closed one is returned), the service-account record written from the account the installer VALIDATED (never read back), both locks re-owned by descriptor (`RepairLocks` answers a non-nil list, and `reownLock` refuses a second link or another filesystem).
`billet local prepare` is root's and Linux's, and with no configuration to read it prepares `<retirement.Root>/server`, not `config.DefaultServerStateDir()`, which answers the USER's config directory (`/root/.config/billet` for root): the package's postinstall runs before any configuration is seeded, and preparing root's own directory failed on its missing parent and left the install's unit decisions deferred (measured in CI, 2026-09-12).
`billet local up` installs, starts, proves and enables the agents; run it as the account that will run the node, never under `sudo`.
`billet local up` repaired only `preflightState`, so a deployment restored perfectly and the control plane could not open one file of it.
`billet node migrate-endpoint` (cmd/billet/nodemigrate.go, nodeendpoint.go) decides from the running node's registration record read under a bracket of unit observations, installs nothing (the render precedes it), refuses `KillMode=process`, stops under `--stop-timeout` signalling only its own `systemctl` (the lifeops runner's TERM-then-KILL cancel, `WithWaitDelay` shared with the guard's `guardWaitDelay`), proves the stop by `inactive`/`dead`/`Result=success` on its own observation after `StopAndProve` returns (a zero exit is not the proof: systemd's own timeout completes the job as done), re-observes the unit immediately before the stop (`closeInstalledConfig` and a fresh `observeUnit`: the same process as the bracket's, not `deactivating`, `LoadState=loaded`, the KillMode judged on that observation), closes the configuration again before the start, binds the post-start wait to the started invocation and pid, waits for the record under the new `InvocationID`, and closes every successful answer against the configuration (identity, size, mtime through `closingLstat`) and the process (`MainPID`, `InvocationID`, not `deactivating`); `reported` and `unchanged` retry a moved process three times through `judgeMigration` (`migrateJudgementAttempts`; `closeUnitObservation`'s second result says whether the process moved), `migrated` never (`unknown` `process`, `state: started`).
`billet node receipt` (nodereceipt.go, releaseinspectreceipt.go) reads the two answers strictly (`strictObject`, `exactAnswerMembers` at both depths because Go's decoder matches member names case-insensitively, the booleans by their bytes), re-verifies the record under the bracket, judges the receipt directory's parent and the existing file through `receiptLstat`/`receiptOpen`/`receiptOwnerOf`, validates an existing receipt whole before the `current` shortcut (a valid equal one is left alone, both flushes done, and only when the name still holds the inode read: `receiptEvidence.info`), removes an invalid file only when it is still the file judged (`receiptRemoveInvalid` compares identity, size and mtime), proves the directory's identity before the shortcut, before the write and after it (`sameDirectory`), reads the written receipt back before answering `written`, and writes through the durable installer with the parent flushed before the directory is used.
`billet nodes revoke <node>` withdraws every credential a machine holds (a node renews itself, so the bundle you issued names a serial it stopped presenting); `billet ca revoke <node> --cert` withdraws one; a certificate issued in a later second is unaffected so a rebuilt machine keeps its name.
`billet release inspect --json` is the host's own account of what it runs, and every field is a value or an explicit unknown with a reason.
`billet rollout registration` (rolloutregistration.go) polls `StatusSnapshot` alone, re-peeks the identity at every poll and refuses when it is absent (an absent identity proves nothing), reports the epoch and never compares it, answers a timeout as its own struct with `last` always present (null for no row) and no `live` or `epoch`, and preserves the child's exit through `runAsLedgerOwnerCode`.
`billet rollout start` records one immutable target; a channel advancing mid-rollout must not retarget work underway.
`billet rollout status --json` (`cmd/billet/rolloutstatus.go`, `schema` 1, the field set pinned by name in `rolloutstatus_test.go`) reports the ledger's deployment binding positively from the ledger and never from the host's identity file (which it peeks only to refuse a foreign ledger and never mints), the open rollout or else the newest finished one with its nodes, and every registered host's CURRENT registration (`Store.Registrations`, from `nodes` and never from a rollout row's dispatch epoch), all through `state.OpenInspect` (`openStateInspect`, the one open in `cmdRolloutStatus`, asserted structurally) so the check job of a converge can read every controller without migrating, locking, claiming or minting; a read that fails is the command's failure with nothing printed, never an empty fleet.
`billet runner check` once counted from `/releases/latest`, so every later release moved a deadline that had passed: 2.334.0 went stale when 2.335.0 shipped 2026-06-08, and counting from 2.336.0 on 2026-07-20 reported a month in hand for a fleet refused six weeks earlier.
`billet server retire --dry-run --json` (`cmd/billet/serverretire.go`) takes no lock, mints nothing, migrates nothing and creates no directory, identity, authority or guard — a read-only SQLite open can still leave the driver's `-wal`/`-shm`, which is why it runs as the identity directory's owner.
`billet server retire` (`cmd/billet/serverretire.go`, dispatched from `cmdServer` before its flags) is the command the role calls: `--reserve` (PostgreSQL active-passive only, the row through `openStateAdminWith` under the identity exclusion, `retireTransitionID`/`retireNow` the seams), `--abandon-reservation` (association validated whole, marker cleared before the row is deleted, a mismatched marker or one beside no row could-not-tell and KEPT), `--complete-row` (the survivor's helper: `--as-host` equals the document's survivor, identity equals its deployment), `--acknowledge-row` (`Answer.MatchesJournal` against the local `done` journal, then `row_done`/`completed_by`), `--dry-run` (no lock, nothing written, the row through `openStateInspect`, `unreadable` never absence), and `--input -` (the request: `decodeRetireInput` and `bindRetireInput` in `serverretireinput.go` — every envelope bound to its host, this run's round and the reservation's clock, each document decoded type-directed and read through PATHS (`report.get/str/boolean/requireStr/requireBool/requireNull`), where an inspector's `{"unknown": why}` at any step of a path is could-not-tell and never a value; `judgeRetireRequest` in `serverretirerequest.go` decides in the order the refusals are reached and `applyRetireIntent` records marker, stage, journal, row, status; `serverretirehost.go` holds the host's own proofs: `readMountinfo`/`mountOf` (the kernel's octal escapes decoded, the longest mount point wins, the identity directory refused when it is itself a mount), `walkTraverses` (a component walk that expands every symlink where it stands, applies `..` to the directory reached, distinguishes a missing component from one it could not examine, and refuses at 40 links) and `hostInterfaceAddresses`, which the inspector reports as `host.addresses` beside `host.node_effective_name`; the survivor's authority is compared by the DER of the certificate its report carries against `wirecert.SnapshotAuthority`'s, never by a reported fingerprint); every mutating mode requires this converge's guard through `retireGuard` (holder equal to `--run`, no pointer, not `preparing`, no stray temporary) FIRST, then holds the identity exclusion (`withIdentityAccess`, which the ledger factory borrows from the registry) through the identity peek, the open and the row's write, and observes the configuration ONCE under both (`observeRetireConfig`: bytes, digest and document from one read), because the second review found the eligibility decided before the lock, the identity peeked outside the exclusion and a `--survivor-host` no `--as-host` could spell; the reservation and the acknowledgement hold an existing marker to the row or the journal (`requireMarkerAssociation`), the acknowledgement validates the journal through `Journal.Validate` with the guard's chain and the identity at the archive and holds `completed_by` to a participant (equal to the recorded one on `already`), the abandon's retry flushes the guard directory and the root before the row is deleted even when the marker is already absent (a rename's durability the earlier run may have died before), a document past its bound is drained to EOF before the refusal, the dry run reads a SQLite row another account owns AS THAT ACCOUNT through `rollout status --json` (`reexecCapture`, the `retireReexecCapture` seam) and reads an unminted identity as `unreadable`; exit 0/2/3 with `state: nothing` on every answer of the command's own (the survivor's `Answer` keeps its spec'd schema); the journal's `transition_id` has the marker's grammar (`transitionIDPattern`) and its reader re-stats after the read (`journalBetweenStatAndRead` the test hook); the fixtures under `tests/fixtures/server-retire/` are the tests' own (`TestTheServerRetireFixturesAreTheCommandsOwn`), the one PostgreSQL test (`TestServerRetireReservesOnAPostgresPair`) named in CI's `test-postgres` run list, everything after the row exercised on SQLite by writing the row directly.
`billet status` prints `guard` when one is held, `billet check` warns on a stale, unpublished or unreadable one, and `host-upgrade --status` prints `claim <shape>` for a non-symlink or dangling claim.
`billet-capacity` (escrow and the message lifecycle), `billet-identity-and-ca` (the App key and onboarding), `billet-security` (trust classes), `billet-config` (runner-group validation).
`billet-capacity` (shapes, budgets, the fleet claim), `billet-security` (what a build can read), `billet-shell-gates` (the provisioning script and buildspec), `billet-storage-and-cache` (ebs-s3), `billet-infra-terraform-ansible` (the modules and IAM renderings).
`billet-capacity` (the drain and the barrier), `billet-backup-restore` (the other `local` commands), `billet-providers-local` (the Mac and the jailer that shape the units), `billet-releases-and-upgrades` (what the packages install and the host transaction).
`billet-capacity` (what `List` and `Destroy` prove), `billet-security` (trust gates and the pid rule), `billet-guest-images` (the kernel pair and images pull for tart), `billet-lifecycle` (the Mac agent), `billet-storage-and-cache` (the Ceph root disk).
`billet-capacity` (what the numbers become at runtime), `billet-providers-local` and `billet-providers-aws` (per-backend blocks), `billet-storage-and-cache` (sites), `billet-identity-and-ca` (the App block and `github-app create`).
`billet-capacity` (what the transactions decide), `billet-backup-restore` (the fence and the barrier in use), `billet-checks-and-lint` (`rawsql`, depguard), `billet-releases-and-upgrades` (the schema version in the manifest).
`billet-checks-and-lint` (the gate and the analyzers), `billet-shell-gates` (probes and executed shell), `billet-capacity` and `billet-lifecycle` (the areas whose vacuous tests are catalogued there).
`billet-checks-and-lint` has the anatomy of the gate.
`billet-config` (sites and store pairing), `billet-providers-local` and `billet-providers-aws` (which backend uses which store), `billet-security` (cache trust), `billet-guest-images` (the golden-image generations that share the Ceph client).
`billet-config` has the whole rule.
`billet-guest-images` (what the gates protect), `billet-providers-aws` (the buildspec and provisioning script), `billet-providers-local` (the guest launcher), `billet-testing` (execute, do not pattern-match).
`billet-identity-and-ca` (the App key and the CA in detail), `billet-providers-local` and `billet-providers-aws` (each backend's boundary), `billet-storage-and-cache` (cache trust), `billet-lifecycle` (the units' hardening and ownership repair).
`billet-identity-and-ca` (the authority the wire trusts), `billet-capacity` (what the commands and fences protect), `billet-security` (what a node may and may not ask for), `billet-releases-and-upgrades` (server-first rollouts).
`billet-images-refresh.service` carried `/var/tmp/billet-images` and never started once on a systemd host, so nodes kept their first guest image while the timer failed daily; `TestNoPrivateTmpUnitRequiresAWritablePathUnderTmp` covers every packaged unit.
`billet-node-wire` (server-first and the version range), `billet-state` (the schema version and the fence), `billet-lifecycle` (the units and packages), `billet-guest-images` (the guest channel), `billet-git-flow` (branching for a hotfix).
`billet-node-wire` (the transport the commands ride), `billet-lifecycle` (what `local down` does with the barrier), `billet-providers-local` and `billet-providers-aws` (what `List` and `Destroy` prove), `billet-state` (the fence inside every write).
`billet-node-wire` (what the certificates authenticate), `billet-backup-restore` (the authority as part of the four-piece unit), `billet-security` (what may never be rendered), `billet-state` (the deployment binding and the claim).
`billet-node.service` runs as root because Firecracker needs TAP devices, block-device nodes, cgroups, chroots and verified process signalling, and Docker's rootful socket is host root anyway.
`billet-providers-aws` (the IAM and the CodeBuild facts the modules encode), `billet-releases-and-upgrades` (the host transaction and version pinning), `billet-config` (`--emit ansible`), `billet-lifecycle` (the units the role renders).
`billet-server.service` runs as `billet` with an empty capability set, `ProtectSystem=strict` and a syscall filter.
`billet-shell-gates` (the build scripts), `billet-backup-restore` (the durable kernel install and lock), `billet-storage-and-cache` (the Ceph generations), `billet-providers-local` (the kernel pair at launch), `billet-providers-aws` (the AMI), `billet-releases-and-upgrades` (channels and signing).
`billet-state` (the fence, the barrier, `OpenMaintenance`), `billet-identity-and-ca` (the authority files and the App key), `billet-lifecycle` (`local up` and ownership repair), `billet-guest-images` (the kernel the durable installer exists for).
`billet-testing` (the mutation discipline the guards protect), `billet-state` (why the ledger rules exist), `billet-shell-gates` (the same "a gate must be able to fail" rule applied to shell), `billet-git-flow` (when the gate runs).
`billet-upgrade.service` is `Type=oneshot` with `NotifyAccess=none`, so a child it runs has no `NOTIFY_SOCKET`; the v0.9.0 candidate's probe waited seventeen minutes at `ctx.Done()` under it before a SIGQUIT dump showed why (2026-09-05).
`billet-upgrade.timer` and `billet-images-refresh.timer` are the one exception to the package enabling nothing. postinstall runs `systemctl enable --now` on both (and says so when it cannot), preremove disables them first; the rule they except exists to keep an install from connecting a machine to GitHub, and these connect nothing: the upgrade oneshot runs `host-upgrade --from-rollout` as root every five minutes and acts only on a rollout the ledger records, the images oneshot runs `images refresh` daily, and both exit doing nothing under `release: {automatic: false}`.
`billet.example.yaml` is the annotated reference and `deploy/billet.yaml` the packaged template; both are parsed by the config test suite, so a renamed key breaks the build rather than an install.
`billet_automatic_updates` (default true) installs `billet-upgrade.{service,timer}` on a host whose server should run and `billet-images.{service,timer}` on a firecracker host, and enables the timers (installed disabled when false); `tests/unit-parity.yml` compares their directives with `deploy/`.
`billet_binary_src` or `billet_version` (with `billet_release_url_base` and the channel); `billet_config` (what `billet init --emit ansible` prints); `billet_github_private_key_src` (never replaced implicitly; the role refuses a converge when the managed key path holds nothing) and `billet_github_target_key_srcs` (target name to a local key file for every further `billet_config.targets` entry, installed at `/etc/billet/app-private-key-<name>.pem` under the same owned-versus-foreign rule, computed as one `billet_github_target_keys` list in `tasks/main.yml` and looped in `tasks/account.yml`; `tests/key-policy-check.sh` runs the target cases too); capacity, network ranges, `billet_networks` and guest DNS; `billet_ceph_*` (bootstrap is destructive and never inferred; every disk it may consume is named); `billet_firecracker_version` and checksums.
`billet_requested_server_should_run` preserves public policy for fresh requests, while retirement masks effective server enablement and `billet_server_should_run`.
`billet_retirement_endpoint_failover_verified` carries the operator's assertion that a shared address or DNS name survives removal; it is not an endpoint migration.
`billet_retirement_survivor_host` names a distinct inventory controller in the same play, still active in `ansible_play_hosts`, with its own settled, held, pointer-free guard under this driver's holder; earlier-play survivor facts do not suffice.
`billet_retirement_variant` is reset privately, set from the classifier journal on continuation, and set from `billet_retirement_requested_variant` on a fresh request for its shared post-acknowledgement continuation.
`billet_server_prepare_only: true` is the stopping point for moving a control plane: it mounts and proves the volume and leaves both services installed, disabled and refused by their own units, so nothing can mint an identity until the old host's state is copied in; both are held because whichever role starts first mints the identity.
`bogus-priv` covers only reverse lookups; `stop-dns-rebind` refuses a forward answer in a private range, which no guest can reach anyway, and `max-cache-ttl=300` with `max-ttl=300` bounds how long any other bad answer outlives its cause, in the bridge's cache and in the TTL it hands the guest's own caching dnsmasq.
`bootout`: returns in 0 seconds with the process still draining.
`ca-previous.crt` says a rotation started; `ca-previous.key` says it is committed.
`cache.actions` (or its deprecated spelling `intercept: true`) on a Linux firecracker tier with a static `cache_scope` and a `node.cache` listener; it is on by default only where its scope already holds (`Tier.actionsByDefault`), and explicitly enabled on docker, EC2, macOS or a mixed-provider tier it is refused.
`capacity → assigned → launching → online → busy`, with `custody`, `teardown` and `quarantine` as holding states and `done`/`failed` terminal; `quarantine` exits only to a terminal.
`ceph-health.sh.j2` (hourly, under `billet_alert_email`) keeps the health check names seen since health was last OK (`[WRN] OSD_NEARFULL: …` gives `OSD_NEARFULL`; an unreadable `ceph health` is `CEPH_UNREADABLE`) and mails only when one appears that is not among them: not when ceph's counts or pools move, not when a check gives way to a milder one, not on recovery.
`check-config.sh` exits 1 for host facts unrelated to the config; `grep | head -30` on its 2.9MB output exits 141.
`check-guest-image.sh` refuses an image missing the binary, the wrapper or the agent's wiring.
`checkDowngrade` refuses an unnamed downgrade before anything drains, and precedes the claim (`downgrade_test.go`); `rollout start --allow-downgrade` additionally refuses a target before v0.9.2 (`checkConvergibleDowngrade`, wired between the downgrade check and `Store.Start` and asserted structurally), because a control plane downgraded to a release that names itself without the v runs the old coordinator, never sees itself on the target and dispatches no node; `host-upgrade --version <tag> --allow-downgrade` is the one-host route it names.
`checkSpec` reserves the `.staging` suffix so nothing can be launched under it.
`checkStatement` runs in production on every open, so a new refusal there is a flag day; a rule about what a new migration may contain belongs in a test.
`checksums.txt` answers "did these bytes arrive" and nothing else; every one of the four facts has to be readable before anything stops.
`chown` is no longer a document class.
`ci.yml`'s concurrency group asks GitHub to cancel an older run of the same ref, but a run whose jobs are queued for self-hosted runners ignores an ordinary cancel and keeps its place in the fleet's queue.
`classification.json` beside the module records the cost of every resource change; `make tf-classify` (in the Go job as well) is the vacuity gate proving every module resource is classified, and `scripts/tfclassify` classifies a real plan for an operator.
`client.callCreating` retries only a throttle.
`cloudflared service install` takes the token only in argv and writes it verbatim, no newline, 0600 root, beside a unit that runs `tunnel run --token-file` (its source, `cmd/cloudflared/common_service.go` and `linux_service.go`; measured on 2026.7.3), so the role writes the file and renders that unit byte for byte (the template's own comment is a Jinja comment, because a rendered `#` line would make the units differ) and never runs the installer.
`cloudflared-connector-check` and `warp-connector-check` drive every refusal against fakes that record argv, compare the rendered unit byte for byte with the installer's (the 2026.7.3 tag's template, blank line before `[Install]` included), grep every whole encoded token in argv, output and the unit (a marker inside the JSON is invisible once encoded; the first gate could not fire), assert the journal was read by exactly the invocation the fake systemd runs (the fake answers an old line to a window read and nothing to a wrong id, and its bare `show` carries the unit's ExecStart), judge a refusal by EVERY recap row being unchanged and by the named hosts each having refused (a run_once assertion that failed on one host ends the play for the others without their asserting anything), run the role skipped on the first host with two later hosts sharing a name, run the roles under `serial: 1` and with the name set on the role invocation, and never run the apt path past the keyring, because `deb822_repository` writes under `/etc/apt` with no path seam and a case that reached it would touch the real machine wherever it happened to have `python3-debian` (it failed on the CI runner for lacking it, and would have written sources on one that had it).
`cloudflared_connector` and `warp_connector` read `BILLET_CLOUDFLARED_TOKEN_<HOST>` and `BILLET_WARP_CONNECTOR_TOKEN_<HOST>` (the inventory hostname upper-cased, everything outside `[A-Z0-9]` an underscore; `billet_*_token_env` overrides the name), never `-e`, because ansible-playbook's argv is world-readable for the run and its environment is not.
`cmd.WaitDelay` is what makes a bound real.
`cmd/billet/ca_test.go` (`TestCAIssueDuringARotationWritesABundleThatCanVerifyTheServer`, `TestCAIssueWillNotOverwriteABundle`), `internal/e2e/enroll_test.go`, `revocation_test.go`, `restore_test.go`.
`cmd/billet/codebuildchecklive_test.go` is named live but drives a fake endpoint; it exists because a structural test proves a judgement is called and not that its result reaches the output.

`cmd/billet/convergeguard.go`: `billet converge-guard hold|release|status|recover|holder`.
`cmd/billet/handshakelistener.go` bounds connections on the real wire.
`cmd/billet/handshakelistener_test.go`, `limitedlistener_test.go`, `bootstrapwire_test.go`, `wirewindow_test.go`.
`cmd/billet/hostupgrade.go` reads the running release through the `runningRelease` seam so a test can stand a release in for "(devel)"; the from-rollout and downgrade tests now use the bare shape production had.
`cmd/billet/images*_test.go`, `imageprobe_test.go`, `imagescompatible_test.go`, `imagesreap_test.go`, `runnercheck_test.go`, `verifypair_test.go`, `tartimages_test.go`, `ami_test.go`.
`cmd/billet/imagespulldurable_test.go` (`TestAPullDoesNotPublishAGenerationBeforeTheKernelIsDurable`), `imagespulllock_test.go`, `kernellock_test.go`, `kernelreap_test.go`, `internal/durablefile/*_test.go`.
`cmd/billet/kernellock.go` is an flock on `<kernel dir>/.billet-kernels.lock`, keyed on the directory (two deployments on a host share one; a symlinked directory resolves to one file), waiting rather than refusing, held by the pull from before the install through a successful import and by the reap from before it reads the generation set through the deletion, always outside the publish lock.
`cmd/billet/local*.go` hold the order the commands act in, which is the whole safety content: `up` is check, server, node, each started, proved, then enabled; `down` is seal, wait, stop node, stop server, disable both; `uninstall` is down plus forgetting the services; `backup`, `restore` and `recover` are in `billet-backup-restore`.
`cmd/billet/local_test.go`, `localup_test.go`, `localdown_test.go`, `lifecycle_test.go`, `drain_test.go`, `admission_test.go`, `hostlock_test.go`, `systemd_test.go`; `deploy/units_test.go` (pins `ExitTimeOut` to the unit's 88200).
`cmd/billet/localbackup_test.go`, `localrestore_test.go`, `localrecover_test.go`, `localoffsite_test.go`, `restoreownership_test.go`, `restoreprofile_test.go`, `preservedpaths_test.go`.
`cmd/billet/nodeupgrade.go` builds the updater and calls `ExecUpgrader.Check` at node startup, before identity/provider work and before an upgrade probe may succeed.
`cmd/billet/promotionorder_test.go`, `claim_test.go`, `leadershipwiring_test.go`, `adminlock_test.go`.
`cmd/billet/releaseinspect_test.go` pins the JSON field set exactly, so a rename under schema 1 is a failed test; holds every direct filesystem call in the inspector to a listed few, so a read beside the observed seams is a failed test too; and its fake `systemctl` answers only the properties asked for.
`cmd/billet/releaseinspectregistration.go` reads it INSIDE the node's process sample (between the identity reads, so a record is never reported beside evidence of another incarnation), through `regularfile.Open` with `NoFollow`, judged on the admitted descriptor's fstat (root-owned, 0600, at most 4 KiB), decoded under the exact member set by name, and reports `host.registration` as known only when the record's invocation is the node unit's sampled `InvocationID`, its node and deployment are this host's (the configured `node.name` or the bundle's CommonName; the bundle's Organization, else the server's identity, else the node state directory's, peeked without minting) and its endpoint is a canonical spelling under its own scheme; `host.installed_endpoint` is the configuration observation's `node.server_addr` through `endpoint.Parse`, and the two are reported apart because a configuration installed after the start changes nothing the process publishes.

`cmd/billet/upgradedecision_test.go`, `upgradefence_test.go`, `upgradetxlock_test.go`, `upgradeprobe_test.go`, `hostupgradegate_test.go`, `releaserecord_test.go`, `releaserecordbounds_test.go`, `rollout*_test.go`, `promotionorder_test.go`.
`cmd/billet/upgradetxlock.go` and `convergeguard.go`: every ancestor of the root's parent (walked from `/`, one component relative to the one above it, owned by root or by the account running billet's transactions and group/other-writable only under the sticky bit), the root's parent, the root, `active` and `transaction.lock` are each required to be owned by the account running billet's transactions (the process's euid: root on Linux, the launch agent's account on a Mac), writable by nobody else, and not a symlink, with each component opened relative to the descriptor of the one above it (`openat`, `O_NOFOLLOW`) and judged on the descriptor that is then used, because `/var/lib/billet/upgrades/active` is a name every updater on the host acts on and a symlink there, at the lock, or on the way to them would make a name checked a different thing from a name used; once the lock is held the root's name must still hold the locked directory, and a resume or a takeover reads the journal through the root (the claim's target exactly one child of the root by its text, opened relative to the root and judged owned and unwritable by others, the journal judged on its own descriptor), never by a name; the record, a candidate and an existing lock are opened identity first (`O_PATH` on Linux, then `regularfile.Reopen`), so a device planted at any of them is refused without its driver being invoked; a link on the way to the root is admitted only when the link itself is owned by root or by that account, because a sticky directory protects billet's entries and not a link another account made beside them; the record is judged on its own descriptor (owned, writable by nobody else), because a hard link from a foreign file is a record that account can rewrite; and a stale `guard.json.tmp` is examined through an identity descriptor (`judgeStaleTemporary`: regular, owned, writable by nobody else, ONE LINK) in EVERY command that removes one (the preparation, the settlement, the release, the takeover and `recover --unpublished`) and then removed by name, never opened for writing or truncated, so no inode is ever emptied under another name and a foreign-owned, loose or hard-linked file at that name is refused rather than deleted (a review found the preparation unlinking any regular file there, 2026-09-10).
`cmd/billet`'s `openIdentityAccess` is the one entry: it classifies the host (prepared, legacy, fresh; a lock or a status beside a missing record is damage and refuses), takes what the mode needs in the one order (init lock, lifecycle lock for a root initialiser, global lock admitted, inner `ca.lock`), and `Release` hands root-created artefacts back to the recorded account through lifeops' descriptor repair (one link, same filesystem, named files only, relative to the CLEANED directory through `filepath.Rel`, since the producers clean their paths and a trailing slash once left every target absolute) before it drops the locks in reverse; the account is READ AT RELEASE, under the locks still held, because an installer can publish the record while a legacy root writer holds the inner lock.
`cmd/billet`'s hand-back runs lifeops' `RepairPaths` over the producers' own path helpers (`state.DeploymentIDPath`, `wirecert.CACertPath` and its siblings, `state.LedgerPath`, `state.DirectoryLockPath`): a regular file with more than one link, a file on another filesystem, a symlink or a type other than the one named refuses and changes nothing, so a planted hard link cannot give away the inode it aliases.

`enforceReleaseWatermark` runs after migrate or verify, guarded by `releaseWatermarkApplied` because a standby or a probe may be looking at a schema before 48: a proved older release is `ErrReleaseBehind` for any handle (proved through `version.Compare`, which orders `v0.9.1` and `0.9.1` alike from v0.9.2 on; before that a release binary's bare `0.9.1` was could-not-tell against everything and the mark was neither enforced nor, being gated on `IsRelease`, ever recorded on a release binary, measured 2026-09-05); a proved newer one is recorded by NOBODY AT OPEN and by `ClaimController` inside the same transaction as the binding and the epoch (`raiseReleaseWatermarkIn`, so a failure to record leaves no claim and no published epoch behind), for a handle whose `openMode.records()` (not admin, not standby, not the maintenance probe) or a promoted standby (`DB.recordsRelease`), because a newer binary pointed at a foreign ledger must be refused by the binding with the mark untouched; could-not-tell records nothing.

`exec.CommandContext` kills the process and then `Wait` blocks until the output pipes close, which anything the process spawned holds open: a `tart list` whose child slept sixty seconds took all sixty despite a 300ms deadline.
`executableVersion` (cmd/billet/convergeguardprepare.go) reads the FIRST LINE alone of `<binary> version`, requires `billet <token> ...`, and takes the token as a release (`version.Canonical`) or as one of the COMPLETE development forms the version package prints (`(devel)`, `(unknown)`; a Go pseudo-version judged by Go's own parser, `golang.org/x/mod/module.IsPseudoVersion`, in exactly the three shapes `cmd/go` mints, with the twelve-hex revision required on top because x/mod admits any length, and `module.PseudoVersionTime` and `module.PseudoVersionBase` required to answer on the token without its build suffix, because the shape check admits a month of thirteen and a `vX.Y.0-0.` base with no predecessor (round 11); a dirty checkout at a release tag, `vX.Y.Z+dirty`, or any build suffix on a release base, which the version package passes through and Canonical refuses; a GoReleaser snapshot `X.Y.Z-SNAPSHOT-<hash>`; every one a valid semantic version); a hand-written regexp admitted `v0.10.1-<stamp>-<hash>` (the timestamp-only form needs a `vX.0.0` base) and `v0.10.1-rc10.<stamp>-<hash>` (a prerelease base needs its own `.0.`), which both read as no release to compare, and refused the dirty tag, which blocked every candidate (round 10, 2026-09-10); a prefix alone or text after it is an error and never "a build with no release to compare", because `billet\n  go go1.26.0` once read as a development build and the downgrade judgement was skipped over it (2026-09-10).
`executable_version.py` remains the version observer; `v0.10.1` is an explicit below-floor maintenance release.

`idempotencyToken` is valid for five minutes, so an ambiguous `StartBuild` is not retried.
`idleMembersOnly` ends the drain when every entry left in `running` has no `runningJobs` identity (a runner launched for an assigned job is still waited for) and the ledger records it `PoolRunnerIdle` with no actual request.
`if ! printf … | grep -q …` therefore reads a present value as absent, intermittently.
`image_pool` padding reached `rbd` unchanged before `normalize` existed; site-name padding was found three times in `internal/config`.
`imaged` is the candidate proving this host's guest images compatible with it (`images compatible` from the STAGED binary, its exit status the answer: 0 nothing to do, 2 pull these, anything else could not tell and refuses) and pulling a generation for each that is not through `images pull --verify`; it sits after the stop, because nothing may launch against a generation mid-import, and before the fence, because a pull records in the cluster rather than the ledger, and it has no unwinding.
`images compatible` proves a generation speaks this binary's `GuestContract` (currently `"10"`) without downloading, boot-verifying an already imported match before fetching another, and exit 2 means images need a compatible generation; the host-upgrade transaction runs it.
`images due` reads age from the generation's UTC name so every node carries the timer (exit 2 means nothing to do); `images reap --keep` replans under the publication lock and refuses to remove a generation whose verification or contract changed after the preview.
`images pull` installed the paired kernel, synced it, changed its mode after the sync, renamed it, and committed Ceph metadata naming the file without flushing the directory; `fsync(2)` says flushing a file does not flush the entry, so a power loss left a complete published generation whose kernel vanished in recovery.
`images pull` refuses only a proved expiry (`--allow-stale` skips the lookup) and reports image age as maintenance information (`AgeNotice`, fourteen days) that decides nothing.
`images reap` refuses while any generation's kernel is unknown, because such a generation boots something on disk indistinguishable from an orphan.
`images verify` boots a probe on a root disk grown the way a launch grows it (the largest `disk` a firecracker tier asks for, else 80GiB, or `--disk`; the provider's own resize2fs, so a superblock resize2fs refuses fails verification rather than every launch: g20260926055218 booted and reported on an ungrown disk, then failed every launch for about 90 minutes, #261), reads a report over its own listener, checks that the runner, Docker and Buildx answered at all rather than matching today's major and that the root filesystem the guest booted is the grown one, and records itself (`MarkVerified`, `RecordVerification`) under the publication lock; `images pull --verify --result-file` records the imported generation only after every verification succeeds.
`imagesource.PolicyFor`: the default source requires a signature by the identity `https://github.com/junioryono/billet/.github/workflows/guest-image.yml@refs/heads/main` (every literal quoted, anchored; the first version ended `@refs/.+` and accepted `refs/pull/N/head`) from issuer `token.actions.githubusercontent.com`; a non-default `images.source` with nothing configured is an error, not a skip, because "verify if an identity is configured" fails open exactly when an operator points at a mirror.
`inamedparam` requires named interface parameters because an interface is a contract somebody else implements.
`install-toolcache.sh` is sourced by the guest build and carried to the EC2 builder; `billet_tc_run` is `chroot "$BILLET_TC_ROOT" "$@"` for the guest, which assembles a filesystem it is not running, and `"$@"` for the AMI, which is the target.
`install_guest_billet` builds `/opt/billet/bin/billet` from the checked-out tree with the newest go the image's toolcache installed, because the hosted build runner's own go is removed to make room and the workflow's seam with the release tree is frozen, and installs `/opt/billet/bin/bazel-credential-helper` beside it.
`installation_id is required; creating an App does not install it` exists because the failure is otherwise baffling, so the test asserts the clause.
`installed_config` says which roles, which ledger backend and which controller mode the configuration declares, and carries the file's digest, bracketed like every hash and needing no running process.
`installing` is reachable only from `ready_to_install` and `committed` only from `verifying`, asserted structurally; `draining` has no timeout.
`intercept` is opt-in and allowed only on Linux firecracker tiers with a `node.cache` listener and a static `cache_scope`; `ACTIONS_RESULTS_URL` carries artifact metadata as well as cache traffic, so a mistake here breaks a deploy rather than slowing CI.

`internal/lifeops/systemctl.go`'s `execRunner` cancels with TERM (not exec's immediate KILL), KILLs after the wait delay (`WithWaitDelay`, ten seconds by default), ends the wait at the same delay for a descendant that keeps the pipes open (the answer refused as not read whole, never a truncated value), and bounds each stream at 1 MiB.
`internal/lifeops` inspects a Linux host (units, files, running processes; it prints nothing) and converges it; `internal/lifeops/launchd` is its sibling for macOS launch agents, deliberately not one abstraction because the vocabularies are not shared.

`internal/provenance` records the manifest digest and the sha256 of the binary at commit (`host-upgrade`) and at install (`install.sh` hands the attestation to `billet release record`, which streams the single `billet` member out of the archive in one pass, refuses a link, a duplicate name, a size mismatch, a second gzip stream and a non-zero tail, and reads the manifest once).

`internal/provider/firecracker/*_test.go` (pid proof, chown scope), `internal/lifeops/*_test.go` (descriptor rules, link counts).
`internal/provider/firecracker/*_test.go`: `TestAPidFileThatIsNotAPidStopsTeardown` asserts the jail, the disk and the tap are still there, not merely that an error came back.
`internal/provider/simulated` holds an instance as a record that reports `Running` until a modelled duration has elapsed and `Running=false, Terminal=true` afterwards, still listed until `Destroy` removes it, as an exited container is.
`internal/provider/tart/realguest_test.go` measures the launcher delivery in a real guest.
`internal/provider` is the narrow contract: `Accepts(trust)`, `Kind`, `Launch`, `Find`, `List`, `Destroy`, with `Spec`, `Instance`, `Teardown` (`TeardownRequested` is the zero value and the safe one; only `TeardownStopped` permits a release), `TrustClass` (zero value `TrustUnknown`, refused), `InstanceName`/`LeaseOf` (an instance is named `billet-<lease>` so reconciliation after a crash needs no side table), and the optional capabilities (`VolumeAttacher`, `GuestVolumeLocator`, `InterruptionSource`, `StagedCredentialReaper`, `QuotaReporter`, `UsageSource`: where the host reads an instance's counters, implemented by firecracker, docker and tart; a target carries the VMM pid's start time, which firecracker reads between two `pidOwner` proofs and the sampler checks after every thread read, and docker's cgroup is accepted only when its last element names the container, because a pid reused between two reads is otherwise charged to the wrong job.
`internal/releasesource` reads manifests and channel statements; `internal/provenance` records which manifest produced the installed binary.
`internal/replay` takes a trace of arrivals (tier, repository, workflow, duration; synthetic from `MorningBurst`, `MonorepoFanOut` and `LongTail`, or exported from a repository's Actions history by `scripts/export-actions-trace.sh`) and drives it through a scripted Actions service into the real listener, allocator, placer, node wire and node runtime over `internal/provider/simulated`, then reads every job back from `job_history` and joins it to the trace on the request id; a job the ledger has no row for is reported as missing, never filled in.
`internal/retirement` is the leaf `wirecert` and `cmd/billet` both import: the global lock (`/var/lib/billet/authority.lock`, root:`billet` 0660, opened read-only because `flock(2)` needs no write access), the world-readable status (`authority-status`) a retirement closes the authority with, the service-account record (`service-account`, root's assertion), the fresh-initialisation lock beside an identity directory (`<parent>/.billet-identity.lock`), `Bootstrap` for installers and `Classify` for everyone.
`internal/rollout.Starter` runs beside the coordinator hourly and is network-free: `cmd/billet/rolloutwiring.go`'s `channelResolver` resolves the channel and runs `releasesource.Compatibility` through the same `resolveTarget` the command uses, and `releasePolicyFor` is the one answer to what a manifest must be signed by (it honours `release.signing_identity`; the `--skip-signature-verification` waiver still wins).
`internal/rollout/*_test.go` (`dispatchguard_test.go`: no host is disturbed by a pass that could not settle), `internal/hostupgrade/upgrade_test.go` (fourteen ordering tests), `internal/releasesource/*_test.go`, `internal/provenance/*_test.go`.
`internal/rollout` is one durable fleet decision and its coordinator; `internal/hostupgrade` is the journaled transaction that replaces billet on one machine; `cmd/billet/upgradedecision.go` is the fence between them.
`internal/runnerimages/*_test.go`, `internal/imagesource/*_test.go` (policy, multipart, trust root), `internal/runnerrelease/*_test.go` (the window rules), `internal/provenance/*_test.go`.
`internal/scaleset/*_test.go` (`endtoend_test.go`, `sessionconflict_test.go`, `teardown_test.go`, `wire_test.go`, `repository_test.go`, `version_test.go`), `internal/integration/repositoryscope_live_test.go` (opt-in, `BILLET_LIVE_REPOSITORY`), `internal/e2e/targets_test.go`, `cmd/billet/teardowntargets_test.go`, `internal/server/sessionconflict_test.go`, `sessionrecovery_test.go`, `jobresult_test.go`, `scaleset_provenance_test.go`, `runnerless_completion_test.go`, `internal/scaleset/broker_health_test.go`.
`internal/server` runs one listener per tier against GitHub's scale-set API and consumes escrow; `internal/nodeplane` dispatches commands to hosts over the wire and `internal/node` executes them, holding custody of what it cannot account for.
`internal/server`'s listener runs one session per tier: `Available → acquire, Assigned → consume escrow, Completed → release`.
`internal/server`: `heartbeat_budget_test.go`, `sessionrecovery_test.go`, `drain_nondestructive_test.go`, `forcecallers_test.go`, `sessionconflict_test.go`, `stranded_test.go`.
`internal/state/*_test.go`: single writer, pragmas on the writer connection, reader cannot write, migration checksums, forward compatibility, schema CHECK constraints.
