`internal/state` owns the durable control-plane store: `DB`, the open modes, transactions, the migrator, the locks and fences, the controller claim, admission, pending completions, force-destroy records and the cache kill switch.
`internal/store/ceph/*_test.go` and `internal/store/ebss3/*_test.go` (including each `writer_test.go`, the conformance shared by both backends), `internal/integration/firecracker_ceph_test.go` (real Ceph growth becomes guest capacity).
`internal/store/ceph` drives RBD through the `rbd` command for firecracker sites; `internal/store/ebss3` uses EBS snapshots and an S3 pointer for EC2 sites.
`internal/store` is the contract every cache implementation satisfies: immutable named generations, copy-on-write clones held under active leases, a writer lease for publication and a fenced pointer advanced by compare-and-swap.
`internal/tfclass/*_test.go` (`make tf-classify`), `internal/tfpolicy` (the drift test), `scripts/codebuild_destroy_guard_test.go`, `terraform/modules/*/tests/*.tftest.hcl`, `terraform/modules/billet/modules/fleet-ec2/lambda/*_test.py`.
`internal/wirecert/*_test.go`: rotation ordering, `LoadServing` tears and re-reads, retire refusals, the `billet-replaces:` claim, one-block PEM proof.
`internal/wireshare/*_test.go`; `cmd/billet/promotionorder_test.go` (`TestTheAuthorityIsAdoptedBeforeTheWireAndPublishedAfterIt`), `casync` tests, `identitystore` tests.
`internal/wireshare` carries an authority between controllers through an `awsssm` store.
`internal/wireshare` makes the store a channel: `Publish` what you hold, `Adopt` when you hold nothing, and never write over a local authority (a host holding a different one is refused naming both fingerprints; `ca sync --force` moves the old directory aside rather than deleting a key).
`interruption_queue_url`'s basename must equal `node.name`, because a shared spot queue hides a two-minute warning behind another consumer's visibility timeout; its host's DNS suffix is SELECTED by `node.ec2.region` (`config.AWSDNSSuffix`) rather than chosen from both, since admitting either meant `cn-north-1` accepted `sqs.cn-north-1.amazonaws.com` while `billet init iam` rendered a correct `arn:aws-cn:sqs:...` — a right-looking policy in front of a host that does not resolve, so the reclaim warning never arrived.
`isOnePEMBlock` rests on the same `decodeFirstPEM` and `skipBlankLines`.
`jailer --daemonize` exits 0 for a VM that died on startup (a pid file and a socket beside a VMM that exited 1), so `Launch` believes the VMM's own API and nothing else.
`job_history.result` is GitHub's word.
`journalSchema` is validated before any of it is read, so a downgrade cannot act on a newer record; `Intent` is validated at every exported mutation, and `Abandon` compares the journal's intent with its own, since `understood` proves a journal names an operation and not this one.
`judgeNodeEndpoint` refuses an address of the retiring controller; loopback reaches the survivor only on the survivor's own host.
`judgeNodeEndpoint` refuses an endpoint that is an address of the retiring controller; loopback reaches the survivor only on the survivor's own host.
`last-decision` is the high-water mark written before the transaction starts: equal is a redelivery, strictly older is refused (`ErrSuperseded`), unreadable refuses a fenced instruction and never an operator's unfenced run (`ErrUnreadableDecision`); both acceptance branches record first (`TestANoOpUpgradeRecordsTheDecisionBeforeAcceptingIt`), because a no-op that accepted before touching the fence let a delayed older generation downgrade a machine.
`launchctl kill TERM <service>` measured the same as a direct SIGTERM: drained 90s, exited 0, not restarted, bootout after 0s.
`launchctl kill TERM` would restart these agents (`KeepAlive{SuccessfulExit:false}`), so launchd's stop is `bootout`, and it comes LAST: `StopAndProve` first asks the process to drain, waits with no bound but the caller's for it to exit, and only then boots out a job with no process. launchd SIGKILLs a job `ExitTimeOut` seconds after the SIGTERM a bootout sends, and macOS 27 clamps an agent's `ExitTimeOut` to 60, so a bootout of a node still draining killed its jobs a minute in (#278); neither request below starts such a timer, a drained node exits 0, and `SuccessfulExit:false` does not restart it.
`leases.disruption` is a token from a closed set written in the transaction that observed the disruption (`NodeGone`, `ResolveQuarantineFor`, `MarkFailure`), never reconstructed at completion, because `ForgetEveryNode` sets `live = 0` fleet-wide at every start and a later verdict would blame every host.
`ledgerHost.downgradeTo` is set only for a PROVED downgrade (`version.Compare(ToVersion, FromVersion)`), never on the flag alone, or an upgrade run with `--allow-downgrade` would raise an external ledger's mark before a probe that has no snapshot to undo it.
`ledgerwriters` (`internal/state`, `internal/alloc`, `internal/rollout`, non-test files) may not import `net/http`, `os/exec`, `provider`, `store`, `github`, `scaleset`, `nodeplane`, `nodeclient`, `node`, `server` or `cmd`.
`ledgerwriters`: zero violations at introduction.
`lifeops.RepairPaths` takes its set from the plan just executed, plus the `ca` directory (a root-owned 0700 one cannot be traversed) and the two lock files the command created; a failed repair is reported and the command exits 0, because the next thing reached for after "the restore failed" is `--abandon`.
`lifeops` is a strict allowlist (`$gostd`, `deploy`, `config`, `lifeops`, `golang.org/x/sys/unix`), every entry `$`-anchored because depguard matches a prefix; `unix.Access` is admitted so a `--dry-run` can ask "can this account write here" without writing.
`lint` is golangci-lint at the pinned version in `.golangci.yml`; `lint-custom` is billet's own analyzers in the nested module `tools/lint`; `test` is the race-and-coverage instrumented suite.
`local recover` puts a deployment back over itself, and every step exists because the previous one cannot promise the next.
`local status` reports the update timers' enablement on Linux; `billet check` reports the backup, upgrade and refresh timers, and the host's converge guard (`checkGuard`: informational under a day, a WARNING naming `converge-guard recover` past `guardStaleAfter`, a WARNING for an unpublished hold or a record whose time cannot be read); `billet status` prints `guard` when one is held (`printGuard`).
`local up` on darwin runs as the login user and does none of this.
`local up`'s change is read from its `start`/`enable` lines, never its `schedule` lines, which it prints on every run.
`lock_dir` is set in the packaged config because billet derives the default from `HOME`, which a service does not have.
`lsof -t` exits 1 both for no opener and for an error and suppresses its warnings, so billet passes `+w` and refuses any warning on either exit status; it sees only this user's processes and skips the rest silently.
`macos_vm_limit > 0` beside a `guest_os` allowlist excluding macOS is refused.
`main` is what people `go install`, and billet is a control plane someone else's CI depends on.
`make check` is the floor.
`make check` is the pre-commit gate, and CI runs everything in it plus more on every push to main.
`make cross` before anything touching a build tag.
`make host-upgrade-order`, `unit-parity` and `emitted-block-check` are the gates.
`make lint` on darwin alone missed a linux-only conversion error that CI caught; hence the second pass.
`make no-mutants` runs first in `check` because an interrupted run leaves the original holding the mutant.
`make rollout-rehearsal` moves two hosts from one PUBLISHED release to the next by `billet rollout start` alone and rolls a downgrade candidate back (`BILLET_REHEARSAL_FROM`/`_TO`); `recover-rehearsal`, `ca-rotation-rehearsal` (twenty-minute leaves through `billet ca issue --lifetime`) and `promotion-rehearsal` (a PostgreSQL pair partitioned with `docker network disconnect`, keepalives set on the server) use the tree's own package from `make dist`.
`make systemd-lifecycle` is the only test of the lifecycle against a real service manager and the real package; it skips without a working App credential.
`make test` runs `-race -count=1 -covermode=atomic`.
`make test` runs the ordinary suite with `-race -count=1 -covermode=atomic`; CI adds a real PostgreSQL and a second `internal/alloc` run with `BILLET_TEST_LEDGER=postgres`.
`make tools` installs the pins; `make module-sources` is inside `check` because it needs only git and shell.
`make unit-parity` compares the timers' directives too.
`markFenced` sets the flag and closes `LeadershipLostSignal` at the same instant; `cmd/billet`'s `stopWhenReplaced` cancels the plane, `retryCleanup` refuses once fenced, and a fenced plane exits non-zero without destroying compute, closing its session or handing back capacity, because a successor demonstrably exists and performs all three.
`max_vcpu`/`max_memory` on a target block are its share (`TargetShares`, keyed by name through `ShareTarget`, `""` meaning `default`), refused by `TargetShareErrors` above the deployment ceiling, below a tier's shape or below its tiers' floors, and re-applied by `alloc.New`.
`metadata` and existing-name `mkdir` inspect one name; `recursive-chown`, `recursive-delete`, `recursive-write` and `recursive-walk` refuse a protected descendant.
`migrationsAreFrozen` in `migrationfreeze_test.go` holds every published sum; when it fails after a change to an existing file, revert the file, never the table.
`n, _ := a.Headroom(ctx, "x"); if n != 0` passes when the call fails, because these APIs return the zero value beside an error; it bit seven times.
`new-request` enters `retirement-request.yml`: static policy and the named `billet_retirement_survivor_host` are required in both modes; a real run additionally requires the survivor still in `ansible_play_hosts` and its own published settled/held/same-holder/guard facts and this host's closed preparation window before its explicit early service-account import.
`newHostFor` picks `systemdHost` on Linux and `launchdHost` on darwin and refuses anything else before the ack; both embed `ledgerHost` (fence, snapshot, migrate, provenance, probes).
`newValidatedRetryableHTTPClient` sets `http.Transport.HTTP2` (`SendPingTimeout` 30 s, `PingTimeout` 15 s), which Go 1.26's bundled HTTP/2 honours (1.24 documented the field as having no effect), keeping the `*http.Transport` the upstream client asserts; `broker_health_test.go` silences a live connection through a proxy without closing it and requires the request to fail within the ping allowance and the next one to dial a new connection.
`nfpms` builds deb and rpm only, depending on `e2fsprogs` and `kmod`, shipping the four units and `billet-rbd.conf`, the config template at `/usr/share/billet/billet.yaml` (not under `/usr/share/doc`, which slim Debian images path-exclude) and `/etc/billet` as a 0750 directory; `/var/lib/billet` is deliberately not packaged so a removal cannot delete the identity and CA key.
`no-mutants` runs first and `tests-kept` runs outside.
`node migrate-endpoint` bounds the node's stop with its own deadline and, on expiry, TERMs then KILLs the `systemctl` it ran and nothing else; the node and its compute are never signalled by a converge, and a stop systemd began runs on under the unit's own bound.
`node-environment.yml` preserves typed installed EnvironmentFile operands through bounded descriptor reads and matching observations.
`node.cache.listen` is one literal non-loopback address; TLS on it is required for EC2 and refused on the firecracker bridge.
`node.cache` is what a guest talks to; without it the node builds no store, hands out no `BILLET_CACHE_ENDPOINT`, and every job runs cold with nothing published — measured 2026-09-04 on a lane whose config had `node.ebs_s3`, an `ebs-s3` site and pinned tiers and no listener (`/dev/root 77G` for `/var/lib/docker`, `cache: COLD`, an empty bucket, `purged 0 snapshot(s), 0 volume(s), 0 state object(s)`), while check printed that the bucket answered.
`node.ceph.user` defaults to `billet` and `admin` is refused, because `admin` is what `rbd` picks for itself when nothing names an identity and an admin key can delete a pool.
`node.ceph` is a sibling of `node.firecracker`, because two hosts in one place map the same pools, and that sharing is the whole reason Ceph replaced ZFS (a ZFS clone exists only on the machine that took it, verified by mapping a clone from a second kernel client).
`node.ceph` is a sibling of `node.firecracker`, required for firecracker and refused for every other backend.
`node.tls` against a loopback `server.listen` is a config error, not an upgrade.
`nodeKernelDir` is the one answer to where kernels live, because `--kernel-dir` once defaulted to a constant while the launch and the reaper read `node.firecracker.kernel_dir`.
`nodeapi.MinVersion` is 12 and `nodeapi.Version` is 25; registration negotiates the highest both speak (`Negotiate`) and records it on the node's row, which `billet status` reports under `protocol`.
`nolintlint` runs with `require-explanation` and `require-specific`, so a bare `//nolint` is itself a finding, and `allow-unused: false` reports a directive that no longer covers anything.
`noteStopped` (`internal/node/stopped.go`), run by every Sweep, dates a running entry whose instance the provider lists as `Ended` (execution observed finished: firecracker's VMM proved gone, docker's `exited` or `dead`; never merely `!Running`, which a paused guest mid-job also is), and a later sweep that still sees it stopped `strayGrace` on marks it proved; `Holding` then stops counting it.
`observeRetireDryRunConfig` parses UNVALIDATED and validates separately: a configuration whose bytes decode still names its `identity_dir` when an unrelated clause fails (`server.max_vcpu: 0`), so the identity is observed THERE.
`off`: nothing.
`openSession` waits on `ErrSessionHeld` (`sessionRetryFor`) and returns every other reason at once; a control plane killed and restarted used to not start at all.
`os.Chown` follows symlinks and a name checked is not a name changed.
`os.Root` and symlinks, umask stripping mode bits, BSD versus Linux gid inheritance, `os.UserCacheDir` reading the environment: three defects were documented behaviour that read the other way.
`os.Root` does not refuse a symlink inside the root (measured); `unix.Openat` against a real directory descriptor honours the flag.
`os.Root` opened a relative `link.lock -> real.lock` as `os.SameFile` with its target.
`os.SameFile` type-asserts the concrete `FileInfo`, so a fixture varies link counts with a real hard link; `syscall.Stat_t` widths differ per platform, so stats go through a converting helper; `OnFailureJobMode` belongs in `[Unit]` or the fixture proves nothing.
`packUserData` is the real gate, since deliverability depends on everything else in the script.
`parallelshared` reports state a parallel subtest writes and its parent test owns.
`parallelshared`: zero helpers on this tree make a `T` parallel, zero take more than one.
`paralleltest` and `tparallel` reason about where `t.Parallel()` is placed and neither models what a parallel closure mutates; two parallel subtests writing one map is `fatal error: concurrent map writes`, which aborts the whole binary and blames every unrelated test.
`paralleltest` is disabled as a default rather than a ban, and 37 directories use parallel tests.
`pem.Decode` skips to the first BEGIN and returns a remainder; a second private key appended after a legitimate one parsed clean and was unlinked with the file.
`pgrep -f <marker>` matches its own invoking shell.
`phaseFinished` is written before the fence comes down so a crash on either side leaves something recognisable, and `--abandon` refuses a `finished` journal because undoing a complete sealed recovery removes the restored credentials.
`plan.json` is the template's provisioner list, derived by a test-side reader and pinned; `scripts/run-runner-images.sh` runs it step by step, with Packer's environment, through a target driver.
`planConfigEdit` decides a missing config, a `github:` holding a list, a `targets:` entry it cannot place and an unwritable directory before `github.Onboard`, because the key is spent the moment the App exists; `--target NAME` writes the named `targets:` entry (created with its `name` when absent) and `default` writes `github:`, with exactly one of `org`/`repository` left in the block.
`planned` is true when either the effective or the installed endpoint differs from the rendering's, deliberately.
`plugins/modules/guard_fallback.py` reads `guard.json` in three phases (every component's metadata from `/var/lib/billet` down, owned by the root's owner and writable by nobody else, never a link, the record 0600 and at most 4 KiB; then the five members required and the protocol's `id`, `token` and `preparing` admitted and typed when present, the token judged as a string and never printed; then the candidate's components and its digest through the descriptor), executes nothing, and a candidate that fails any step is never run by the role, which refuses naming what to install by hand rather than falling back to the legacy protocol; hard links are admitted because the command imposes no one-link rule.
`postinstall.sh` loads the `rbd` module, creates the `billet` account (refusing an existing one whose home is not `/var/lib/billet`), creates `/var/lib/billet` as root:root 0755 (the common parent must not let the server rename root-owned node, kernel or upgrade directories), `/srv/jailer` as root:root 0755 and `/etc/billet` as root:billet 0750, copies the template only when no config exists, and warns about drop-in overrides that could break `Type=notify`.
`preRProcess` judges only a completed probe: a run the bound ended or whose output overflowed is never pre-R.
`prepare-exclusion.yml` first clears per-inclusion settlement and answerer facts with a connection-free `set_fact`, retaining a held run's holder, public id and learned claim/recovery facts so reinclusion validates the same guard.
`prepare-exclusion.yml` runs before everything else (the holder from `BILLET_CONVERGE_GUARD_HOLDER` or `-e`; the first call `prepare --validate` acquires or validates BEFORE anything is decided or staged; the staging into an exclusively allocated recovery directory under the guard; the second call declares the intent and is judged under the lock; `settle` last; a refusal inside the acquirer's window releases the guard this invocation acquired and nothing else; a bootstrap and a pre-R host with a candidate hold through the staged candidate after the staging).
`prepare-exclusion.yml` under `--check` runs `prepare --dry-run --json` through the managed binary, or, for a guard directory beside a managed binary that is absent or answers "unknown command", through the executable the guard records after `guard-fallback.yml` verified it (the same import, a second time, under `billet_exclusion_dry_via_record`), and refuses an unpublished guard, an untrusted record and a pre-R recorded executable as the converge does; without that a dry run read a guard carrying a transaction pointer as no claim and planned a binary change over an interrupted bootstrap (round 3, 2026-09-10).
`preremove.sh` stops node then server on a real removal and fails the removal if either will not stop.
`printf big | grep -qxF <early match>` exits 141, a late match exits 0, no match exits 1, because `grep -q` leaves the moment it matches and `pipefail` reports the writer's status.
`private-inputs*.yml` and `host-upgrade-order.yml` belong to `shape`; `retirement-routes-cases.sh`'s `r3-lazy-*` cases belong to `retirement-routes` with `BILLET_GATE_ONLY=retirement`, `BILLET_GATE_SKIP=retirement-request` and `BILLET_RETIREMENT_SHARD=routes`.
`proveRunning` asks the guest whether the recorded pid is alive, because every one of those failures reported success.
`provider` and `store` are siblings below the scheduler: neither imports the other, neither imports `server`, `node` or `cmd`.
`providers: [tart, codebuild]` is the shape a pin cannot express, so `validateUnpinnedMacOSTier` holds each backend's declared `nodes[]` policy to the pinned rules instead, `max_concurrent` defaults to and is bounded by what those hosts permit between them, and a reservation stays pinned.
`publishClaim`, `releaseClaim` and `abandonClaim` never remove a claim that is not a Go transaction's symlink.
`publish` defaults by trust (`defaultPublish`): an untrusted tier with a repository scope is `default-branch`, everything else `trusted-only`; `materializeCacheScope` writes a repository target as the scope of an untrusted tier that sets no rule, at load, so the scope travels.
`pull_request_target`, `issue_comment` and `workflow_run` read the default branch and never write, and `pull_request` writes only `refs/pull/N/merge`.
`putJITConfig` asks for `Tier: Intelligent-Tiering`.
`r_services` opts a case into the recovery's service, cgroup and process fakes; `/run` is overlaid with `/etc` so rollback's runtime enablement removal stays inside the namespace.
`rawsql` reports SQL executed from Go rather than named in a query file.
`rbd info -weirdpool/x`: `unrecognised option`; `client.billet` with a `client.` prefix authenticates as `client.client.billet`.
`rbd rm` and `rbd trash rm` do refuse an image with watchers (`PreRemoveRequest`, EBUSY).
`rbd rm` deletes every data object before it returns; killed at the 15-second rbd bound it left the name listed by `rbd ls` with `rbd info` answering ENOENT and the objects still there, and about 1,260 discarded `cache-v-*` volumes accumulated that way.
`rbd trash mv` does NOT refuse an image in use: librbd's `Trash::move` checks no watchers and refuses only when it cannot take an exclusive lock, which a volume `Create` makes (`layering` only) does not have and a krbd mapping of a clone hands over on request unless mapped `exclusive` (read from the Ceph v19.2.2 source, not measured), so the watcher check is the guard, and the age bound is what makes a map between the check and the move impossible, since nothing maps a volume after the job that named it.
`readFleetDecision` opens through `openStateForDecision`, the one open in `ledger.go` that names no release (exempted by name in `ledgerrelease_test.go`), because a standby's timer is the older binary the leader's watermark would refuse; it still cannot read a schema newer than its binary, and it opens only an EXISTING SQLite ledger (`state.LedgerPath`), since the package enables the timer before the server has ever run and an operator open would mint a root-owned ledger.
`readShareUsage` sums `UsageByTier` over the tiers the catalogue gives each target; a lease whose tier left the catalogue is charged against EVERY share (its target cannot be told, and forgetting it sells its room twice).
`real*_test.go` files assert that what billet says matches what the real system does, because the firecracker backend's two launch-killing defects survived every unit test and died on the first real run.
`reconcilePool` sizes the pool to `TotalAssignedJobs`.
`reconcilePool`'s surplus is judged against `TotalAssignedJobs`, which only a message carrying statistics refreshes, so a quiet tier freezes it and a member whose runner never takes a job is never surplus: on 2026-09-30 one held its lease for ten hours, and a draining node's restart for two of them, because the drain waits for everything the node holds (#287, #288).
`recover --holder` removes a pointerless guard under the same assertion and scan; `recover --unpublished` removes a directory holding nothing but regular `guard.json.tmp` files, every entry examined before any is removed.
`recovery` is permission to run the recovery, and a refused recovery is a failed converge that names its fix.
`recovery` is the one route that is not about a retirement: an interrupted binary upgrade fences the ledger, so the row reads unreadable and the host would hold forever — the recovery tasks sit behind the ordinary gate and only finalisation removes the fence.
`refillEscrow` has no production caller and stages escrow in tests.
`release.automatic` is the one zero value that does not refuse, and it is a pointer so absence and `false` differ.
`release.yml` proves the release immutable, then polls the attestation API for a GitHub-initiated bundle at the tag ref's digest and runs `gh release verify` with an exact-tag filter (several tags can share one commit; `bundle_url` is a URL, not inline JSON); the verifier is checked out from `github.workflow_sha`.
`release.yml`'s job runs only when `github.repository` is this repository, because a reusable workflow called from a foreign repository would be issued that same identity over the caller's source; the verifier also requires `SourceRepositoryURI` to name billet for both default release and image policies (`internal/imagesource/verify.go`).
`release`, `release --cleanup` and `recover --holder` refuse a guard carrying the marker (`errGuardTransition`) and ALSO a host whose retirement journal is `done` and not `settled` (the tail clears the marker and then writes settled, so a crash between leaves an unsettled journal without a marker); a journal that cannot be judged refuses too.
`releasesource.PublishRefPattern` accepts exactly those two.
`request-retained` uses the installed-both classifier and retained settled answer, extends `r_new_document` for all three deployment nodes, and captures B through the ordinary template with an independently expressed four-key projection.
`require-min-compat-client` is the floor and `rbd_default_clone_format` overrides it, cluster-wide or per pool, and measured, the destination pool's value governs a clone; billet reads both for both pools and names the cause with the command that removes it (`ceph config rm client …` does not remove a pool-level override).
`requiresPlacement` (launching, online, busy) refuses to enter a running phase without a bound, still-legal placement, re-checked against policy in force then; `hadCompute` decides whether an expired lease is failed outright or quarantined.
`reserveFloors` holds each target's outstanding floors only up to that target's remaining share, at the charged shape (the placer's deployment room is set to the share budget), and returns what it held per target, so `headroomWithPlacer` and `Resize` subtract a sibling's floor from the share and an impossible remote floor cannot take the deployment from other targets.
`reserveKeyFile` reserves a sibling staging file with `O_EXCL` and `writeKeyAtomically` publishes it with an `os.Link` that fails rather than replaces (no rename fallback, because Go's `os.Rename` has no no-clobber form).
`retained-drift.yml` fingerprints the recursively walked ordinary graph, full task mappings including inherited conditions and variable definitions, and all rendered template variables and fixed writes; `retained-drift.json` is the reviewed catalog and `retained-drift-rows.md` its complete row table.
`retireOfflineMembers` (`internal/server/offline_member.go`) asks GitHub's REST runner record through the registry's `InspectRunner` (the scale-set client's, built on `InspectScaleSetRunner`) about one member idle past `offlineIdleAfter` per `offlineInspectEvery`, and treats two consecutive answers of present, offline and not busy spanning `offlineGrace` (dated when each answer arrived) as naming a candidate, never as permission: no number of REST reads stops GitHub delivering a job the instant after one.
`retireTail` (`cmd/billet/serverretiretail.go`) runs in the same process that reached `done` and does, in this order: the published status (republished when it is absent, malformed or below `done`, since that file is what closes the authority to every ordinary writer); the retained node's endpoint receipt through `refreshReceipt` (the converge that retires a host ends at the retirement and never reaches the ordinary task, and the node's invocation and installed digest both moved under the transition); the completion document, which is emitted on EVERY answer because the role does not decide from the row's word alone; the ledger row; the guard's marker; `settled`.
`retireTransition` observes the host (where the identity directory is, which recorded digest the installed configuration is, whether the stage is the one intent recorded, and at the phases that read them the backup service, the node's changed-since-start verdict and the node unit), asks `retirement.Decide`, performs exactly that action and observes again, bounded by `retireStepLimit`.
`retirement-cases.md` records the exact producer-corpus gaps rather than manufacturing route fixtures.
`retirement-continue.yml` keeps incomplete and unsettled entries on continuation and tail alone; already-settled retained done enters through `retirement-settled-entry.yml`.
`retirement-node-preflight.yml` prepares endpoint, typed installed environment, keyed readiness, provider and alert operands without reloading or writing, then `prepare-node-operations.yml` lists concrete destinations from those same facts and role constants, and `retirement-node-config.yml` binds strict command admission to exact rendering and operation bytes.
`retirement-node-shape` runs the four retained guard/drift/input/operand plays; `host-upgrade-order` retains shared ordering and reader controls.
`retirement-rehearsal` adds a node on the retiring PostgreSQL controller, moves both nodes to the survivor, and submits a retained-node request built from fresh real inspections after reservation; it uses the tree's package too.
`retirement-role-observe.py` independently watches transient filesystem events, protected lstat/hash state, exact ordered service requests, installed E, modeled registration/receipt and final handler flushes.
`retirement-role.yml` uses the test-only strategy in `tests/strategy_plugins/retirement_role.py`, pinned to the suite's ansible-core version.
`retirement-settled-entry.yml` calls `--check-settled-entry` before `--check-node-config` binds exact E/rendering and operation bytes; ordinary E removes only `server`, `github`, `targets` and `backup`.
`retirement.SettledVerdict` carries schema 2, purpose `settled-entry`/`settled-closing`, outcome `admitted`/`verified`, invocation/classifier bindings, done/row/settlement/completion facts, observed node activity, `enablement_changes` (departures from retirement quiet enablement, reported without refusal) and `state: nothing`.
`retirement.yml` resets a legacy claim's retirement answerer to empty and selects it only after the managed executable passes verification.
`runCandidate` asks the candidate's `-h` the same question (`candidateHoldsOnFlag`): one that lists the flag is judged by its exit status alone and a readiness line from it is refused as a broken protocol; one that does not is a release through v0.9.0, its line means "stop me" and is its only proof (silent exit zero is a could-not-tell, refused); it answers SIGTERM by exiting zero, so its exit status is its verdict and a signalled death is a refusal whoever sent it; SIGKILL is always sent before the reap because output closing is not exit (the shipped probes hold their descriptors until exit, so a closed output is a zombie the kill cannot change; one that closed its output and kept running is killed and refused); the deadline is `runCandidate`'s own and never `exec.CommandContext`'s, whose kill runs beside `Wait` and on a kernel without pidfd may reach a reused number, so every signal precedes the one `Wait`.
`runnerrelease.Resolve` is the one calculation over the installed version and the stable release history, asked by `runner check` and `images pull`.
`safeDigest` refuses where `safeRelease` repairs, because a digest is compared.
`scalesetclient` confines `github.com/actions/scaleset` (a public preview) to `internal/scaleset`.
`scripts/` holds thirty-odd Go test files that run the build scripts against fixtures; `internal/provider/codebuild/buildspec_test.go` parses the buildspec and runs its commands under `/bin/sh`; the EC2 boot script is run with the runner command replaced by one that prints what it would have read.
`scripts/build-guest-image.sh` remains for a custom or air-gapped build, on a machine with systemd-nspawn.
`scripts/build-guest-kernel.sh` once ended its Docker compatibility check in `| grep -Ei missing | head -30 || echo "NOTHING MISSING"`: with `CONFIG_VETH=y` removed the checker exits 1, the pipeline prints fifteen `missing` lines and then `NOTHING MISSING`, and the build exits 0.
`scripts/ca-rotation-rehearsal.sh` is the rotate-then-retire sequence across two renewing nodes on a packaged host, and after `ca rotate` the control plane must be RESTARTED to present the overlap, which the command's own output says.
`scripts/check-guest-kernel-config.sh` captures the status first, and the checker is vendored at `scripts/kernel/check-config.sh` with its commit and sha256 in `check-config.pin`, verified before it runs and copied into the gate's private directory before it is hashed, because hashing a path and executing that path are two lookups of a name.
`scripts/check-no-mutants.py` refuses to proceed while a `.bak` sits beside a tracked Go file, because an interrupted mutation run leaves the original holding a mutant that compiles and mostly passes; it is first because it cannot be a false alarm.
`scripts/check-retirement-shards.py` owns the expected case counts, checks source ownership, and consumes each completed shard's observed names to refuse omissions or duplicate execution.
`scripts/check-tests-kept.py` reports `Test` functions HEAD has and the tree does not; it is deliberately not in `check` because deleting a test is sometimes right, and it exists because a scripted edit once swallowed a neighbouring test with every gate green.
`scripts/ci_scope_test.go` holds the classifier's cases, the per-path map, the verdict and the structure.
`scripts/hybrid-root-check.sh` (`make hybrid-root-check`, in CI's terraform job) generates the untrusted, trusted, builder and cache shapes, rewrites the module source to this checkout, and runs `terraform fmt -check`, `init` and `validate`, because HCL rendered as text can name a module input that no longer exists and every Go test would stay green.
`scripts/kernel_gate_test.go`, `scripts/image_manifest_test.go`, `scripts/movingmajor_test.go`, `scripts/guest_image_*_test.go`.
`scripts/mkreleasemanifest` reads every compatibility fact out of the packages that define it (the wire range, `state.LatestSchemaVersion`, the guest contract, the rollback target), never from YAML; a snapshot writes the manifest and does not sign it (keyless signing needs an OIDC identity).
`scripts/onelinerblock_test.go`: `TestNoGoBodyIsWrittenOnOneLine`; `scripts/golangci_exclusions_test.go` pins the exclusion anchoring.
`scripts/promotion-rehearsal.sh` runs the pair against `postgres:18-alpine` with `tcp_keepalives_idle=10 tcp_keepalives_interval=5 tcp_keepalives_count=3`, partitions the leader with `docker network disconnect`, and records partition-to-promotion and the old leader's exit and restart as a standby when the partition heals; the numbers are in `docs/reference/records/host-rehearsals.md`.
`scripts/rehearsal-lib.sh` (`make rollout-rehearsal recover-rehearsal ca-rotation-rehearsal promotion-rehearsal`) installs the `.deb` into privileged `ubuntu:24.04` containers with systemd as PID 1, runs `billet local up`, `local down`, `local recover`, `resume` and `host-upgrade` there, and asserts on `systemctl is-active`, journals and the state directory's ownership.
`scripts/rehearsal-lib.sh` starts privileged `ubuntu:24.04` containers with systemd as PID 1 (the shape `scripts/test-systemd-lifecycle.sh` measured), installs a `.deb`, issues certificates as the service account and asserts on unit state, journals and files, never on an exit code alone.
`scripts/releasemanifest_test.go`, `scripts/movingmajor_test.go`, `scripts/scripts_test.go` (install.sh), the Ansible scenario targets.
`scripts/rollout-rehearsal.sh` (`make rollout-rehearsal`): two packaged hosts moved from one published release to the next by a rollout under real systemd, the controller through `billet-upgrade.timer` (or, on a FROM before v0.6.0, the operator's `host-upgrade`), then a downgrade candidate that cannot open the migrated ledger proved to roll back; the first real run of `hostupgrade.go`'s doing rather than its ordering, recorded in `docs/reference/records/host-rehearsals.md`.
`scripts/runner-images-nspawn.sh` starts the machine in a transient unit with `--keep-unit`, `DevicePolicy=closed` (only `/dev/net/tun` and terminals; with every capability and no user namespace a block class would be the builder's own disks), `--network-veth` and owned FORWARD rules on the exact link `ve-<machine>` (names of at most twelve characters, so the link name fits).
`scripts/runner-images/upstream/` vendors that tree at one commit (`COMMIT`, equal to the toolset pin), every file held to its git blob id and every directory to its tree id (`BLOBS`, `TREES`).
`scripts/runner-images` vendors GitHub's `actions/runner-images` tree at one commit and the guest build runs it; `internal/runnerimages` vendors GitHub's `toolset-2404.json` and the EC2 toolcache installer; `internal/imagesource` fetches and verifies; `internal/runnerrelease` knows which `actions/runner` is installed and how close to refusal it is.
`scripts/scripts_test.go`, `scripts/kernel_gate_test.go`, `scripts/guest_image_pipefail_test.go` and the other `scripts/guest_image_*_test.go` files execute the scripts against passing and failing fixtures.
`scripts/test-systemd-lifecycle.sh`, `scripts/test-package-lifecycle.sh`.
`server retire --check-node-config` is the read-only future-rendering boundary for a settled retained node.
`server retire --check-settled-entry` and `--check-settled-closing` are separate read-only modes with `--config`, `--run`, `--retiring-host`, `--transition`, `--expected-holder` equal to the run and `--expected-guard`.
`server.DecideCacheAuthority` is the one place the rule lives.
`server.WithRolloutStarter` is what wires it, asserted structurally by `rolloutstarterwiring_test.go`.
`server.controllers: active-passive` makes a refused controller wait in `AwaitController`, which waits out `ErrControllerHeld` and nothing else.
`server.drain_timeout` used to bound the shutdown wait and then destroy what was left; it is now the point where `warnDrainOverrun` starts repeating every fifteen minutes.
`server.runTier` now hands every listener `WithSessionReopen` over `openSession`, and `recoverSession` closes the failed session (bounded by the close grace), opens a new one (waiting out `ErrSessionHeld` when the close did not land), and retries with backoff (`sessionReopenFirst` 5 s doubling to `sessionReopenMax` 5 min, reset by the first poll that answers), logging every failed attempt at Error with the tier.
`serverretirecaller_cancel_test.go` produces the older-run cancellation classifier and the continuation after a survivor acknowledgement; new fixture bytes are harvested from CI, never assembled in the corpus.
`serverretireinert.go` durably writes the protected `<RetiredDir>/<transition_id>` record and exactly five `10-billet-retired.conf` files through `durablefile`, then reloads once and proves the effective condition.
`sessionrecovery_test.go` pins both sides.
`set -e` is ignored for a pipeline that begins with `!`.
`set -e` is the trap, because a CodeBuild buildspec's commands run under CodeBuild's shell, not a script billet controls.
`set -o pipefail` is what makes a failed `ansible-playbook` visible behind a successful `tee`.
`setsid` does not escape the unit's cgroup; `KillMode=mixed` kills that child when the updater stops the node.
`setup-docker-builder` starts an isolated BuildKit daemon whose whole state lives on a sticky disk (`resolve-policy.sh` reads the tier's `buildkit_cache_mount_limit` ceiling first); `stop-docker-builder` quiesces BuildKit before its disk commits and enforces `mount-limit-bytes`; `build-push-action` runs `docker/build-push-action` against that builder and never writes `secrets` to the disk.
`siteAcceptsProvider` maps each store to the one backend that uses it; `validateCodeBuildNode` refuses a `codebuild` node that names a `site`, and `validateSites` refuses a sited tier that lists codebuild, because placement confines a sited tier to hosts at that site and a codebuild node declares none, so the tier advertises 0 while `billet check` reports healthy (measured on a live acceptance).
`sites[].name`, `tiers[].site`, `node.site`, `github.org` and `tiers[].runner_group` are refused with padding (`checkIdentityPadding`), because a trimmed identity names a different deployment or organization on another machine; one shipped version authorised `" home "` at load and refused every node reporting `home` forever.
`sizes` beside explicit `vcpu`/`memory` is refused.
`sleep --id <id> 30` exits immediately on real coreutils; put the marker in `$0` via `sh -c <script> <name>` and poll `/proc` until the process is there, so "not appeared yet" and "exited" stop being the same observation.
`sqlc` and `sqlc-check` are outside `check` for the opposite reason to the terraform gates.
`sqlcgenerated`: generated code imports nothing of billet's.
`sqlitedriver` confines `modernc.org/sqlite` and `github.com/jackc/pgx` to `internal/state`, which verifies WAL and `synchronous=FULL`, takes the process lock and serialises writers.
`ssh_access` never hardens a host its own converge leaves with no way in, and that refusal is not gated.
`stage-candidate.yml` first decides the binary change from installed/candidate evidence, then dynamically includes `prepare-desired-ledger.yml` only for a real binary change or a managed executable proved to predate the guard.
`stage-candidate.yml` judges nothing about the guard: the channel resolves into the private `billet_resolved_version` (the public pin is never assigned by a task), the recovery directory is allocated by `allocate-recovery.yml`, one `mkdir -m 0700` without `-p` inside a five-attempt loop that draws its suffix from `billet_recovery_dir_suffix_command` under `sh -c` on every attempt (`file: state=directory` accepts an existing directory, so two stagers would share one journal), and the candidate is copied into it; the floor, the downgrade and the intent against the record are the command's, under the lock.
`startupTimeout` bounds the ping, the backend's preparation, the schema check and a migration, and `TestAnOpenThatTimesOutOnItsOwnBudgetSaysSo` pins that it surfaces as `context.DeadlineExceeded` (a listener that accepts and answers nothing).
`stat -f '%Lp' f 2>/dev/null || stat -c '%a' f` reads a mode on this Mac and prints filesystem statistics with status 0 in `ubuntu:24.04` (measured 2026-09-06), so the gate compared inode counts against `600` on the one platform CI runs.
`stat -f` is the filesystem form on GNU coreutils, so a BSD-first mode read never falls back on Linux.
`state-rds-postgres` and `control-plane-postgres`: the PostgreSQL ledger (or a grant for one you run; it never learns the password) and a controller with no ledger volume, so it can be rebuilt rather than recovered.
`state.LatestSchemaVersion()` is one `int` in the release manifest, and the upgrade fence refuses a candidate below the installed ledger's maximum; that is a sound proxy only while versions are dense.
`state.Unreachable(err)` is written from `TestUnreachableIsMeasuredAgainstPgxsOwnShapes` (pgx v5.10.0 against PostgreSQL 18, 2026-09-13, every case through database/sql, each asserting the SHAPE it produced as well as the verdict), because two of its rows are what reading alone gets wrong: a WRONG PASSWORD (28P01) and a MISSING DATABASE (3D000) arrive INSIDE a `ConnectError`, and `context.DeadlineExceeded` satisfies `net.Error` (pgx wraps it in `errTimeout`).
`status --json` answers `release_executable_verified` by hashing, never by executing (`TestTheRecordedExecutableIsNeverRun` plants a script that records its own run).
`stopGracefully` sends `POST /v1/nodes/{node}/withdraw` after its wait on every exit and never from a superseded process.
`strayLedgerSidecars` treats an `Lstat` error as could-not-tell, not absent.
`supersedeLedger` records the digest of every file it moves before it moves anything; `putSupersededBack` compares what it finds against those, refuses a canonical file whose digest differs or that is present with nothing recorded, and refuses to lift the fence if it would leave no ledger.
`systemctl disable` follows `[Install] Also=`.
`systemctl show` hides the privilege prefix.
`systemctl stop` returns when its job completes and says nothing about whether the unit came back; refusing only `active` and `activating` accepted `deactivating`.
`t.Context()` and `t.TempDir()` (enforced by `usetesting`), `t.Cleanup` for teardown so it runs on the `t.Fatal` path, table tests for pure functions and named tests for invariants so a failure names the invariant.
`t.Parallel()` turns on the sharing, not the disk.
`takeLock` now records every cookie it gives up with its fate unknown (an add answering anything but success, 16 or 2, and a `Release` whose listing or removal failed after the heartbeat stopped) in `Client.abandoned`.
`takeTxLock`: the root's parent is reached by `openTrustedDir`, an ANCHORED WALK from `/` with each component opened `openat` relative to the descriptor of the one above it, `O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW`, a link component opened as itself (`regularfile.OpenIdentityAt`), required to be a link OWNED BY ROOT OR BY THE EXPECTED ACCOUNT (a sticky directory keeps another account from renaming billet's entries and says nothing about a link that account made there, which it can repoint), then read with `readlinkat` and its target walked the same way with its components AS WRITTEN, a `..` opened where it stands after the links before it (macOS spells `/var` as a link; at most `maxTrustedLinks` hops), and every directory on the way judged by `requireTrustedAncestor` (owned by root or by `guardExpectedOwner`, and group/other-writable only under the sticky bit, because a writable ancestor lets another account rename the whole chain); the parent itself owned by `guardExpectedOwner`, the process's euid, and not group/other-writable; the root `Lstat`ed (created with `mkdirat` inside the parent when absent, refused as a symlink) and THE PARENT FLUSHED BY EVERY ACQUISITION right after, opened `openat` relative to the parent and judged on the descriptor (owned, not group/other-writable; the role establishes it 0700 and a test's `TempDir` is 0755, which is why the rule is "nobody else can write it" rather than one mode); the lock opened `openat` relative to the root with a create-or-open loop (`openLockFile`: a single `O_CREAT` open answered ENOENT to a racing loser on APFS, measured 2026-09-09), an EXISTING lock opened identity first (`regularfile.OpenAt`, `O_PATH` on Linux and `O_SYMLINK` elsewhere, so a link at the name is the link's own inode and refused as not regular on every platform) so a device at its name is refused without its driver, and required a regular file owned by the account; and once the flock is held, `requireRootInPlace` requires the root's NAME to still hold the directory the lock was taken inside (`Lstat` by name, `SameFile` with `txLock.dir`), and a resume or a takeover reads the journal THROUGH THE ROOT (`readJournalUnder`: the claim's target a direct child of the root, opened relative to `txLock.dir`, the journal read relative to that by `hostupgrade.ReadJournalAt`), with the claim's target required to be EXACTLY `<root>/<name>` by its text (`recoveryChild`: no `.`, `..` or separator, nothing cleaned first, because `<root>/hop/../x` is `<root>/x` to a lexical check and `/elsewhere/x` to the kernel), the recovery directory judged on its descriptor (owned, writable by nobody else) and the journal on its own (`ReadJournalAt`'s trust callback), because a journal reachable through a second name is a step and a generation another account chooses and a writable recovery directory lets a journal's removal read as a transaction that never began; as the Go transaction's own claim helpers (`publishClaim`, `releaseClaim`, `abandonClaim`) act relative to the root descriptor they are handed, so a root displaced at its name after the lock resolves nothing; what still goes by name is the transaction's own journal writing under the lock (`internal/hostupgrade`) and the abandoned tree's removal, both bounded to a direct child of the root.
`tart delete` resolves a name, so a VM appearing under it microseconds after the check would be destroyed.

`tart exec` starts a session with no LANG, so the delivery script passes `LANG` beside the credential as a command prefix, only where the guest set none: `en_US.UTF-8` on macOS, `C.UTF-8` on Linux (GitHub's values).
`tart get` has three measured answers: a real VM returns its configuration; a name with no directory exits 2 with `does not exist`; a directory tart cannot read exits 1 with `missing files for a supported layout`.
`tart get`: exit 2 `does not exist`; exit 1 `missing files for a supported layout`.

`tasks/backup.yml` renders and enables `billet-backup.{service,timer}` under that predicate and `billet_backup_timer`, and refuses an effective drop-in on the backup unit the way `account.yml` refuses one on the services (asked of systemd through `DropInPaths` after a reload, status judged), because the ledger fence is rendered into the unit; a consumer that carried the fence as a drop-in removes it before converging with this role.
`tasks/needrestart.yml`, imported in the ordinary block after every refusal and before `account.yml` (whose apt install is itself an upgrade needrestart answers), stats `billet_needrestart_binary` and `billet_needrestart_dir` and, where either exists, creates `conf.d` and renders `needrestart-billet.conf.j2` to `90-billet.conf`, root:root 0644; the template is byte-for-byte `deploy/needrestart.conf` (`deploy/needrestart_test.go` compares them and refuses a Jinja delimiter in it), so a host that installed the package and was then converged sees no change.
`tasks/node-restart.yml` (imported by services.yml under the name "Restart the billet node after non-binary inputs change", whose `when` the gates pin as text) records `MainPID`, runs `systemctl restart --no-block billet-node.service`, and polls `systemctl show` in short `until` steps every `billet_node_restart_poll_interval` seconds until a deadline `billet_node_restart_wait` (3600) after the request on the controller's clock (`'%s' | strftime | int`, epoch seconds: `now(utc=true).timestamp()` reads a naive UTC datetime as local time and moves an hour across a daylight-saving change, measured 2026-09-30 on a Pacific-time Mac as hours off `date +%s`; the retries only cap the loop), proving active, running, an empty `Job=` and a MainPID other than the recorded one (a node that was not running recorded 0; a new process beside a queued job may predate the request).

`trusted-only`: a trusted pool publishes and an untrusted one discards, with the pre-#226 keys unchanged byte for byte.
`trusted` requires a non-default `runner_group` with `restricted_to_workflows` and `selected_workflows` equal to the tier's `workflows` list; the control plane reads the policy at startup and immediately before each registration and refuses drift.
`uid_t` is unsigned 32-bit, so parse ids with `ParseUint(…, 10, 32)`, reject `MaxUint32` and reject 0.
`unsupported-variant` belongs to a REQUESTED NODE-ONLY HOST: with no server there is no ledger, so its row is unreadable; without the request it is `ordinary`.
`untrusted_isolation` is not free to name speculatively: `billet check` is fatal when it is named and softnet carries no setuid-root grant.
`up` also requires `/usr/local/bin` writable (`UpRequest.BinaryDir`, added to `requiredDirs`), because the updater renames into it as the operator.
`up` compares the loaded job's program, arguments, timeout and whole environment (a redirected `TART_HOME` makes the inventory describe another machine, which resells live guests).
`up` enables the timers as a reported last step outside the unit plan.

`upgrade-inspect.yml` refuses a converge over a symlink claim (the Go transaction's) naming `--status` and `--resume`; `account.yml` compares the two binaries' `version` output and refuses a proved downgrade before the drain unless `billet_allow_downgrade`; `billet_automatic_updates` (default true) renders and enables the two timers wherever they apply; the role's own transaction still refuses a PostgreSQL host, and its message says the timer does that upgrade.
`validate-interpreted-inputs.yml` runs on every ordinary host before templates: guest DNS is literal IP, SMTP members have no controls and match their grammars, network configuration uses typed literals; TLS settings are constants.
`verify-all-checks` judges each job by its own family: a KEPT job must succeed, a selected job must succeed, an unselected one may succeed or be skipped, a push must select every family, and the FAMILY map must cover every job it needs; a selected job skipped because what it needs failed is a failure.
`version.Compare` is the one ordering, and it orders BOTH spellings of a release, `v0.9.1` and `0.9.1`, because the release build stamps GoReleaser's `{{.Version}}` (bare) and releases through v0.9.1 reported, journaled and registered that form; `version.Version()` now spells a release as its tag, `version.Same` is equality across the spellings (never `==` on a release string), `version.IsRelease` stays the tag grammar for pins and the watermark, and `version.Canonical` turns a bare report into the tag before it is recorded (`alloc.highestRelease`).
`waitForHolding` asks `Holding()` every `holdingCheckEvery` (2 s, or the sweep interval if that is shorter) and runs `Tend` only on the sweep cadence (#240): asked once per five-minute sweep, a drained host stayed out of service for up to five minutes after its last VM was destroyed, measured in the v0.12.11 rollout, and a rollout paid that per host.
`warp-cli connector new` takes the token only as `<TOKEN>` (measured, 2026.6.880.0), runs exactly on the daemon's own `Registration Missing` read from the one `Status update:` line (a daemon that answered without one is refused, not read as any state), and never re-enrols, because that tears down the interface the play may be running over.
`wirecert.LockAuthority(ctx, dir)` resolves the exclusion itself for a caller with no command around it; `LockAuthorityWith` takes a resolved one; `RotateWith`/`RetireWith` run under a lock the command already holds, since a second flock in one process is denied.
`wirecert.ResolveRetiringExclusion` is that path (a PREPARED host only: a host with no record has no global exclusion to close), and `openRetireIdentity` (with `retiring` set) takes the inner `ca.lock` inside the directory under it, after the retirement's own admission for that step and again after the global lock's wait, so a legacy writer holding only the inner lock is excluded from the rename too.
`wirecert.SnapshotAuthority` reads the public half of the authority (`ca.crt`, `ca-previous.crt`, `authority-created`) twice and answers only when the two reads agree, an absent file and an empty one being different observations (`bytes.Equal` alone calls them equal and would confirm a read that saw no predecessor with one that saw a malformed one), three attempts, else `ErrAuthorityChanging`: the same confirming-read shape `LoadServing` uses, because a rotation or a retirement can cross a single read.
`wiring.BuildTargets` refuses a duplicate name, a missing client and a client whose own target is not the config's, because the server resolves the first entry of a name and the plane the last.
`withRetireInspection` takes only existing trusted transaction/global locks; `observeRetireOrdinaryEntry` shares trusted settled records, archived identity/provenance, closure status, absent marker/original identity location, current guard ownership, installed node identity, controller postconditions and current resource protection with node-config admission.
`wsl_v5`: 5882 findings on this tree.
billet attributes a lost job; it never re-runs one.
billet holds a GitHub App private key per target that can mint tokens for a whole organization, or for one repository through `administration: write`, the only permission GitHub offers for registering a repository's runners and a far wider grant than the organization one (used for registration and nothing else, disclosed at creation, and installed on the one repository rather than every one the owner has); a node-wire CA, per-job runner registrations (JIT configs), per-guest cache bearers, an optional TLS interception CA, and on cloud nodes AWS credentials that can create and destroy machines.
billet is not actions-runner-controller without Kubernetes.
billet long-polls GitHub's Runner Scale Set API; GitHub never connects to billet.
billet signs its own requests, pinned to AWS's own signer.
billet's shell lives in `scripts/` (guest image, guest kernel, release, install, rehearsals), in `internal/runnerimages/install-toolcache.sh` (sourced by both the guest build and the EC2 builder), and in Go that renders shell: `internal/provider/ec2/build.go` (the provisioning script), `internal/provider/codebuild/buildspec.go`, the tart and firecracker guest launchers.
billet's suite is 450-odd `_test.go` files across unit tests, structural tests that parse Go source, cross-package integration tests in `internal/integration`, the end-to-end suite in `internal/e2e` (a real control plane, real node wire and real container runtime against `internal/fakeactions`), `real*_test.go` files that assert billet's model against a real tart, docker, firecracker, CodeBuild, S3 or launchd, and opt-in live tests that spend money.

softnet admits the host, so billet blocks `@host`. softnet's default lets a guest reach its vmnet gateway, which is the Mac: an untrusted guest connected to the host's SSH and Screen Sharing (macOS 27.0, tart 2.37.0, softnet 0.23.0, 2026-09-23).
softnet blocks the guest's resolver, so billet configures one and proves resolution. softnet blocks the private address space, which includes the vmnet gateway the DHCP resolver points at; egress keeps working and every job fails to clone. billet sets a public resolver before delivering the registration (three spellings: systemd-resolved, plain `resolv.conf`, macOS `networksetup`, since `resolv.conf` there is generated and read by nothing) and verifies resolution, turning a silently stopped mechanism into a launch error.
sqlc's two engines: byte-identical Go with `BIGINT` casts; modernc.org/sqlite binds `$N` positionally, a repeated `$1` once, and a `$2` appearing before `$1` correctly.
trivy 0.74 needs `GOEXPERIMENT=jsonv2` to install under Go 1.26.
| Key | Read by | What it is |
| `backup` | `local backup`, `local restore --from-backup` | `s3.bucket`, `s3.region` (required even with an `endpoint`), `s3.prefix`, `s3.endpoint` (path-style; RGW, MinIO, R2), `s3.kms_key_id` |
| `github` | `billet server` | the target named `default`: exactly one of `org` or `repository` (`owner/name`), `app_id`, `client_id` (optional), `installation_id` (required; creating an App does not install it), `private_key_path`; `name` is refused here |
| `images` | `images pull` | `source` (empty means billet's own), `signing_identity` and `signing_issuer` (required for a non-default source) |
| `node` | `billet node` | `name` (from the certificate when there is one; required on loopback), `server_addr`, `bootstrap_addr`, `provider`, `site`, `max_vcpu`/`max_memory` (what this host contributes; required for `ec2` and `codebuild`), `tls` (all three of `cert`, `key`, `ca`), `lock_dir` and `allow_unlocked_deployment`, `state_dir` (required), `max_custody`, `drain_timeout`, and one provider block: `firecracker` plus `ceph` (both required for firecracker, refused otherwise), `tart` (optional), `ec2`, `codebuild`, plus `ebs_s3`, `cache`, `registry_mirrors`, `monitoring` (`interval` 250ms to 30s, the bound set by RAPL's wrap; `rapl`; `idle_package_watts`, which requires `rapl`; refused on any provider but firecracker, docker and tart, and `rapl` and `idle_package_watts` refused on tart, whose VMs carry macOS's own per-process energy estimate; absent means off) |
| `nodes` | control plane | per-host policy, not a roster: `name`, `provider`, `guest_os` allowlist, `macos_vm_limit` |
| `release` | the rollout starter, `host-upgrade --from-rollout`, `images refresh` | `channel` (`stable` or `candidate`), `version` (an exact tag or a 40-hex SHA; `latest` and `main` refused; exclusive with `channel`), `automatic` (a `*bool` whose nil is TRUE, read only through `AutomaticUpdates()`; the one switch for starting rollouts, acting on them and refreshing images), `maintenance_window` (bounds when a rollout may begin; refused beside an explicit `automatic: false`), `signing_identity` and `signing_issuer` (both or neither) |
| `server` | `billet server`; a certless node sharing the file reads it to learn which deployment it joins | `listen` (loopback means plain HTTP; anything else requires mTLS), `bootstrap_listen` (the enrollment listener; absent means no network enrollment), `node_tls_hosts` (required when `listen` is a wildcard; both listeners present one certificate), `state_dir` (shorthand for `identity_dir` plus `state: {backend: sqlite}`; writing both is refused), `identity_dir`, `state` (`backend: sqlite` or `postgres`; `postgres.dsn_env` names the variable holding the DSN, never the DSN), `controllers` (`single` or `active-passive`, refused on SQLite), `identity` (`backend: file` or `aws-ssm` with `aws_ssm.region/prefix/kms_key_id`), `max_vcpu` and `max_memory` (required, positive, the deployment ceiling), `placement` (`pack` or `spread`), `drain_timeout` |
| `sites` | control plane | `name` (matched exactly), `store` (`ceph` or `ebs-s3`) |
| `targets` | `billet server` | further targets, each `name` plus the `github` fields; requires the `github` block (always the first target, always `default`); names label-shaped (`CheckTargetName`) and unique, `default` refused; no two targets share a key path; every tier then needs `target`.
| `tiers` | both roles | one tier is one scale set; `label` is the tier's identity in the ledger and allocator, unique in the file, and `runs_on` (default `label`) is the scale set's name and the `runs-on` value, unique per GitHub owner (`validateTierTargets` keys on the target's path, and refuses a repository target reusing a name its organization's target has, since the organization's set would take the same jobs), so targets on different owners can share one name; `teardown --tier` names the set and `--target` scopes it to one target.
